Plan §14 Definition of Done requires multi-pod Kubernetes acceptance tests.

## Acceptance Criteria (from Phase 6 epic DoD)

1. **Multi-pod deployment**: replicas=3 — every pod independently serves requests with identical routing
2. **Chaos test**: Kill one of three pods mid-traffic — zero client-visible errors beyond retry budget (plan §8 chaos)
3. **Mode A test**: Spin up 3 pods, anti-entropy runs exactly once per shard per interval cluster-wide
4. **Mode B test**: Start 3 pods, exactly one holds the reshard lease at any given instant; killing it promotes another within `lease_ttl_s`
5. **Mode C test**: Submit a 10GB dump; chunks distribute across 3 pods and HPA reacts to `miroir_background_queue_depth`
6. **Memory validation**: All §14.2 memory rows fit within 3584 MiB under realistic steady-state load
7. **Alerts**: All §14.9 alerts present in PrometheusRule manifest and trip under induced fault

## Current State

Phase 6 components are implemented and have unit/acceptance tests:
- P6.2 Peer discovery: verified
- P6.3 Mode A coordinator: implemented
- P6.4 Mode B coordinator: 21 leader election tests pass
- P6.5 Mode C coordinator: 22 acceptance tests pass
- P6.7 Resource-pressure metrics: tests pass (with 2 known bugs noted)

What's missing are **end-to-end multi-pod Kubernetes tests** that verify:
- Pods discover each other via headless Service
- Mode A partitioning works across 3 pods
- Mode B leader failover works within TTL
- Mode C job distribution and HPA reaction
- Chaos resiliency (pod kill mid-traffic)

## Implementation Approach

Create `tests/p6_8_multi_pod_acceptance.sh` that:
1. Uses `kind` or `minikube` to spin up a 3-pod Miroir deployment
2. Runs client traffic in the background
3. Verifies each acceptance criterion above
4. Tears down the cluster

This blocks closing the Phase 6 epic (miroir-m9q).
issue.title: P6.8 Multi-pod Kubernetes acceptance tests (plan §14 DoD)

issue.description:
## What

Support the §14.10 single-pod oversized mode for dev clusters / very small deployments / constrained environments. Operators may provision a single pod at higher limits (e.g. 4 vCPU / 8 GB); memory budgets scale linearly by multiplier; HPA may remain disabled.

Specifically:
1. `values.schema.json` MUST allow `replicas: 1` with `taskStore.backend: sqlite` and `hpa.enabled: false` AND with `resources.limits.{cpu,memory}` larger than the §14.8 baseline.
2. Document the multiplier behavior: when `resources.limits.memory` is N× the baseline, the in-Rust budgets (idempotency.max_cached_keys, session_pinning.max_sessions, etc.) should scale linearly OR the operator overrides each.
3. `docs/horizontal-scaling/single-pod.md` documents this is supported, NOT recommended for production, and explains the fault-tolerance trade-offs (zero-downtime rollouts, pod-loss survival lost).

## Why

§14.10 promises this works. Currently nothing in `values.schema.json` rejects oversized single-pod, but nothing exercises it either; without explicit support, operators may have surprising memory-cap interactions when the runtime budgets don’t auto-scale.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Fixture in `tests/integration/` boots a single 4-vCPU / 8-GB pod successfully
- [ ] `values.schema.json` accepts the oversized-single-pod combination
- [ ] Memory-multiplier behavior documented (auto-scale or operator override) and one of the two implemented
- [ ] `docs/horizontal-scaling/single-pod.md` includes the trade-off explanation from §14.10
- [ ] README.md "When to use" section calls out single-pod as supported but not recommended

issue.description:
Split-child of bf-5aon3 (verify backfill progress ratio non-zero + monotonic). Child 2 of 4 — property (c), the [0,1] ceiling. Depends on child 1's snapshot loop.

## Scope

Build on child 1's bookkeeping harness and add the missing property: across the same multi-shard sequence, every sampled backfill_progress() must be <= 1.0 (plus an epsilon). This is the regression guard against double-counting once bf-2tddo's up-front denominator exists.

Crucially cover BOTH branches of incorporate_shard_total (executor.rs:665):
1. upfront_total_known=true -> the denominator is already the full-index total seeded in start_backfill; per-shard totals must NOT be added, or the ratio overshoots 1.0.
2. upfront_total_known=false -> the legacy fallback accumulates per-shard totals into the denominator (executor.rs:671); the ratio must still not exceed 1.0 at completion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Asserts every sampled backfill_progress() <= 1.0 + epsilon across the multi-shard sequence.
- [ ] Covers the upfront_total_known=true path (denominator not inflated by per-shard totals).
- [ ] Covers the upfront_total_known=false legacy per-shard accumulation path.
- [ ] cargo test passes for the new/extended test in crates/miroir-core.
issue.title: Assert backfill ratio never exceeds 1.0 across the upfront_total_known double-count guard

issue.description:
Split-child of bf-67ki8 (populate total_documents at reshard backfill start). Child 3 of 4 — the propagation seam that makes the admin status endpoint read a real denominator. Depends on child 2 (bf-1rodg): propagate the correct, non-double-counted total.

## Scope

Add the optional persisted-operation seam to `ReshardExecutor`: a `progress_operation: Option<Arc<RwLock<ReshardOperation>>>` field, a `with_progress_operation(op)` builder, and a `report_progress(&state)` method that, when an operation is attached, calls `op.write().await.update_backfill_progress(processed_documents, total_documents)` (crates/miroir-core/src/reshard/executor.rs:123-132, 672-679).

Call `self.report_progress(&state)` at the end of `start_backfill` (after child 1 seeds the denominator and child 2 reconciles it) so the real `total_documents` reaches the persisted `ReshardOperation.total_documents` via `update_backfill_progress(backfilled, total)` (crates/miroir-core/src/reshard.rs:813). This is what makes `ReshardOperation::backfill_progress()` (reshard.rs:819) return a real ratio instead of 0.0 from an unset denominator.

`report_progress` must be a no-op when no operation is attached, so the default executor path is unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] When a `progress_operation` is attached, `start_backfill` propagates the real `total_documents` to `ReshardOperation.total_documents`.
- [ ] `ReshardOperation::backfill_progress()` (reshard.rs:819) returns a non-0.0 ratio from the very first shard.
- [ ] With no operation attached, `report_progress` is a no-op and the default executor path is unchanged.
issue.title: Propagate backfill total_documents to the persisted ReshardOperation

issue.description:
Split-child of bf-67ki8 (populate total_documents at reshard backfill start). Child 2 of 4 — the reconciliation that prevents child 1's up-front count from being double-counted. Depends on child 1 (bf-2tddo).

## Scope

Add a `upfront_total_known: bool` field to `BackfillProgress` (crates/miroir-core/src/reshard/executor.rs:43) with `#[serde(default)]` so previously-serialized `ReshardState`s deserialize to the legacy fallback (`false`). Gate `incorporate_shard_total` (executor.rs:81) on it: when `true` the method is a no-op (denominator is already the full-index count); when `false` per-shard counts accumulate as before. `start_backfill` sets the flag from `total_documents > 0` once child 1 seeds the real count.

This is what keeps the progress ratio in [0,1] once the up-front count exists.

## Key correctness

Key the mode switch on the `upfront_total_known` flag, NOT on `total_documents == 0`: once the legacy fallback folds in the first shard the denominator is non-zero, so keying on zero would silently drop every subsequent shard and stall the ratio mid-backfill.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `BackfillProgress` has `upfront_total_known` with `#[serde(default)]`; previously-serialized states deserialize as the legacy fallback (`false`).
- [ ] With an up-front total set (`true`), `incorporate_shard_total` is a no-op — no double-count, ratio never exceeds 1.0.
- [ ] With up-front stats unavailable (`false`), per-shard counts still accumulate into the denominator across a multi-shard index.
issue.title: Add upfront_total_known flag so per-shard accumulation skips a known total

issue.description:
Split-child of bf-30m2j. Investigate and document that the disabled test's acceptance criteria are ALREADY covered inline, so later children attack the real (narrow) gap instead of rewriting a redundant test.

## Why this is step 1

Parent bf-30m2j claims `acceptance_4_mode_a_shard_partitioning` (disabled in `crates/miroir-core/tests/p13_8_anti_entropy.rs:244-247`) is "the only automated test" verifying Mode A shard-partitioning for anti-entropy, blocked by API drift (`with_mode_a_scaling` removed). That premise is STALE and is the likely reason this bead failed 3x - workers keep trying to rewrite a test whose coverage already exists.

Evidence already in-tree (`crates/miroir-core/src/anti_entropy.rs`, the cfg(test) block). Run `grep -n "fn test_mode_a" crates/miroir-core/src/anti_entropy.rs` to list them; the relevant ones are:

- The 3-pod exactly-one-owner test at anti_entropy.rs:1541. Builds 3 `ModeACoordinator`s via `PeerDiscovery::new` + `set_peer_set_for_test`, asserts every one of 64 shards is owned by EXACTLY ONE pod (`owner_count == 1`) and all 64 covered (`total_owned == 64`), plus even distribution (15-25 per pod).
- The pod-reassignment test at anti_entropy.rs:1665. 3->2 peer-set resize; asserts the removed pod's shards go to exactly one survivor and all 64 stay owned.
- The partitioning-wiring test at anti_entropy.rs:1761. Asserts the reconciler uses Mode A when a coordinator is configured.

The API problem is ALSO already solved: `ModeACoordinator::set_peer_set_for_test(peer_set)` injects a synthetic peer set with NO `peer-discovery` feature and NO SRV lookup, so these tests run in plain `cargo test -p miroir-core`. The removed `with_mode_a_scaling` was replaced by `with_mode_a(coordinator)`.

## Task

1. Run `cargo test -p miroir-core mode_a` and `cargo test -p miroir-core anti_entropy` in the DEFAULT config (no `--ignored`, no `--features peer-discovery`, no docker). Record which tests execute and pass. Disk hygiene: check `df -BG --output=avail /` before building; miroir-core target/ is large.
2. For each of the three inline tests above, list exactly which of parent bf-30m2j's acceptance criteria it satisfies (cite file:line).
3. Enumerate the GENUINE remaining gaps. Confirm or rule out each:
   (a) No explicit MINIMAL-RESHUFFLING assertion: the pod-reassignment test (1665) checks the removed pod's shards are re-homed, but does NOT assert the surviving pods KEEP the shards they already owned (survivor stability) - i.e. it does not pin the "minimal reshuffling" property from plan section 14.5.
   (b) No SCALE-UP case (3->4); only scale-down (3->2) is tested.
   (c) No pinned hash-vector test asserting a specific shard->owner mapping against the `top1_by_score(hash(shard_id || peer_id))` rule (`rendezvous_score` is private in mode_a_coordinator.rs:112).
4. Post the coverage map + enumerated gaps as a comment on bf-30m2j and on this child.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `cargo test` output pasted showing the three inline tests executing (not skipped) in the default config.
- [ ] Coverage map: each parent acceptance criterion marked `[covered by <test>:<line>]` or `[GAP]`.
- [ ] Enumerated list of genuine gaps (confirm/refute a, b, c) recorded as a comment.
issue.title: Map existing Mode A partitioning test coverage vs disabled acceptance_4 test

issue.description: plan section 13.10 (docs/plan/plan.md) implements query coalescing: identical concurrent search requests within a 50ms window share one upstream scatter via pending_queries: DashMap<QueryFingerprint, broadcast::Receiver<Bytes>>. This only dedupes requests that are in-flight at the same time -- it does nothing for the common case of the same query recurring seconds apart (pagination, retries, repeated facet-count queries from the search UI described in section 13.19, polling clients). Add a short-TTL (target 250ms-2s, configurable) LRU cache of completed merged scatter-gather results, keyed on (index, canonicalized query body, settings_version), sitting alongside the existing coalescing map in miroir-core. This reduces redundant fan-out to Meilisearch nodes under bursty repeat-query traffic without the staleness risk of a longer cache. Add config under miroir.result_cache (mirroring the query_coalescing config block) and metrics miroir_result_cache_hits_total / miroir_result_cache_size.
issue.title: Add short-TTL merged-result cache for repeated identical searches

issue.description:
Split-child of bf-49a17 (reshard backfill progress never populated). This is the foundation piece: a reusable mechanism to compute a reshard source index's real document count, with no change to the reshard state machine.

## Scope

Implement a helper that computes the total document count for a reshard's source index across its source shards, so the backfill denominator is known before backfill begins. Reuse the existing per-node node-stats aggregation pattern rather than duplicating it.

## Context (from bf-49a17 exploration)

- `crates/miroir-core/src/ilm.rs:795` `fetch_index_stats` already does exactly this: it iterates node addresses, GETs `{address}/indexes/{uid}/stats`, and aggregates `node_stats.number_of_documents`. This is the precedent to reuse/extract.
- `crates/miroir-core/src/reshard/executor.rs:513-530` `start_backfill` (Phase 3) currently hardcodes `total_documents: 0 // Will be updated`.
- Note: `executor.rs:608-610` DOES accumulate `state.backfill_progress.total_documents += total_docs_in_shard` on the first page of each shard in `advance_backfill` — but that only populates the in-memory executor state incrementally, and never reaches the persisted `ReshardOperation.total_documents`. The up-front count this child introduces is the missing denominator that exists before the first page is fetched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New helper (on the reshard executor and/or extracted from ilm.rs into a shared location) queries each healthy source node's `GET /indexes/{uid}/stats` (or an equivalent per-shard count via the `_miroir_shard={id}` filter) and returns an aggregated total document count.
- [ ] It reuses/extracts the existing `ilm.rs` node-stats aggregation rather than duplicating the HTTP+aggregate logic.
- [ ] Unit-tested against a mock node client returning known per-node counts.
- [ ] No change to the reshard state machine or backfill migration logic (pure additive helper).
issue.title: Add per-node document-count query helper for reshard backfill

issue.description:
## Evidence

p13_8_anti_entropy.rs (crates/miroir-core/tests):240-244:

    // NOTE: Test acceptance_4_mode_a_shard_partitioning is disabled because it requires
    // the peer-discovery feature and ModeACoordinator. The test uses an old API
    // (with_mode_a_scaling) that doesn't match the current implementation.
    // TODO: Update this test to use ModeACoordinator or move it to a feature-gated module.

The test is not merely #[ignore]-marked — it appears to have been removed/commented out
entirely, so it does not even show up as a skipped test in `cargo test` output. This is
the only one of the anti-entropy acceptance tests without any working equivalent.

This matters because plan §14.5 "Mode A — Shard-partitioned ownership" explicitly lists
the anti-entropy reconciler as a Mode A consumer: "Anti-entropy reconciler (§13.8) — each
pod fingerprints and repairs the shards it owns" (rendezvous hash over the live peer set
via ModeACoordinator / peer_discovery.rs). The bead that closed §13.8
(miroir-uhj.8, "P5.8 §13.8 Anti-entropy shard reconciler") lists as an explicit
acceptance checkbox: "Mode A: 3 pods, each owns ~1/3 of shards; anti-entropy runs exactly
once per shard per interval cluster-wide" — i.e. this bead was closed claiming that
property holds, but the only automated test that verified it is currently disabled due to
API drift (`with_mode_a_scaling` vs. the current `ModeACoordinator`/peer_discovery API).

Practical risk: a regression in the rendezvous-based shard-ownership partitioning for
anti-entropy (e.g. two pods both claiming the same shard, causing duplicate repair work,
or a shard being owned by no pod, causing silent AE coverage gaps in a multi-replica HA
deployment) would not be caught by CI today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Rewrite (or reinstate) `acceptance_4_mode_a_shard_partitioning` in
      p13_8_anti_entropy.rs (crates/miroir-core/tests) (or move it into
      rebalancer_worker/anti_entropy_worker.rs's own
      acceptance-test module, matching the pattern used by
      mode_c_worker acceptance_tests.rs and rebalancer_worker/acceptance_tests.rs) using
      the current ModeACoordinator / peer_discovery.rs API instead of the removed
      with_mode_a_scaling API.
- [ ] Test asserts, for a simulated 3-pod peer set: each shard is owned by exactly one
      pod (no double-ownership, no orphaned shard), matching the
      `top1_by_score(hash(shard_id || pod_id))` rule in plan §14.5.
- [ ] Test asserts ownership redistributes correctly (minimal reshuffling) when the peer
      set changes size, consistent with the "transient double-work during a 15-second
      discovery window is harmless" note in §14.5.
- [ ] Test runs in the default `cargo test` (or `cargo test --all`) invocation without
      requiring `--ignored" or a docker-compose stack, so it actually executes in CI
      (crates/miroir-core has no docker dependency for this class of unit-level
      coordinator test elsewhere, e.g. leader_election acceptance_tests.rs).
- [ ] Update or remove the stale comment block at p13_8_anti_entropy.rs:240-244 once the
      test is reinstated.

## Priority rationale

P2 — this is a test-coverage gap, not a known-broken feature (no evidence the actual
Mode A partitioning logic is wrong, only that its test bit-rotted). But it directly
covers an acceptance criterion that a closed P0 bead (miroir-uhj.8) claims is satisfied,
and it's the kind of gap that's easy for autonomous workers to silently regress further
if left unaddressed.
issue.notes:
## Reconciliation: miroir-uhj.8 acceptance checkbox now verified by running tests

The acceptance checkbox from closed P0 bead **miroir-uhj.8** (§13.8 Anti-entropy shard reconciler):

> 'Mode A: 3 pods, each owns ~1/3 of shards; anti-entropy runs exactly once per shard per interval cluster-wide'

This checkbox is now backed by **REAL, RUNNING tests** (not just the disabled test referenced in this bead's description):

### Verifying tests (file:line)
- **crates/miroir-core/src/anti_entropy.rs:1541** — `test_mode_a_three_pods_each_shard_processed_once`: 3 pods, each shard processed exactly once per interval cluster-wide
- **crates/miroir-core/src/anti_entropy.rs:1665** — `test_mode_a_pod_reassignment`: pod removal and shard re-homing
- **crates/miroir-core/src/anti_entropy.rs:1761** — `test_mode_a_anti_entropy_partitioning`: shard ownership partitioning validation
- **crates/miroir-core/src/anti_entropy.rs:1846** — bf-4t3o4's `test_mode_a_minimal_reshuffling_scale_down_survivor_stability`: minimal reshuffling on 3→2 scale-down
- **crates/miroir-core/src/anti_entropy.rs:1927** — bf-4t3o4's `test_mode_a_minimal_reshuffling_scale_up_survivor_stability`: minimal reshuffling on 3→4 scale-up

This closes the documentation loop: the acceptance criterion claimed in miroir-uhj.8 is now verified by CI-enabled tests that assert the rendezvous-based shard-ownership partitioning properties for anti-entropy in Mode A.

Both sides added module declarations. Include all modules from both sides (alphabetically sorted is fine). Deduplicate any doubled declarations.

Both sides added config fields. Include all fields and impl blocks from both sides. Pay attention to struct field ordering and derive macros.

This is the largest file. main added extensive search result merging logic (2493 line diff); master may have added different merger logic. ### router.rs
main added `write_targets_with_migration()` and `get_all_migrations()` accessor. master may have modified routing logic. Keep all functions from both sides.

### scatter.rs
Both sides modified the scatter/gather implementation. Carefully read both halves and produce a version that includes all functionality from both sides.

### topology.rs
Both sides modified the topology model. Include all struct fields, impls, and new types from both sides.

### raft_proto/mod.rs
Include all proto definitions and command types from both sides.

### Add/add conflicts (hedging.rs, query_planner.rs, replica_selection.rs, task_store/)
For add/add conflicts: open both versions (one is in the conflict markers), produce a single file that incorporates all of the functionality. If one version is clearly more complete, use that as the base and add missing pieces from the other.

Split-child of bf-5aon3 (verify backfill progress ratio non-zero + monotonic). Child 1 of 4 — the cheap, high-confidence slice of the verification gate.

## Scope

The three ratio properties bf-5aon3 gates are ultimately computed by ReshardOperation::backfill_progress() (reshard.rs:819), which report_progress (executor.rs:692) mirrors straight from BackfillProgress.processed_documents / total_documents. Assert properties (a) and (b) at that bookkeeping level, WITHOUT driving the fragile HTTP fetch path.

Reuse the existing executor test helpers: backfill_state(progress) (executor.rs:1289) and bookkeeping_executor() (executor.rs:1307). Attach a progress_operation via with_progress_operation, seed a non-zero total_documents with upfront_total_known=true, then for a synthetic >=3-shard sequence: advance processed_documents by each shard's doc count, call report_progress(&state), snapshot op.read().await.backfill_progress(). Assert (a) the ratio is > 0.0 from the very first shard, and (b) the sampled ratios are monotonically non-decreasing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Test attaches a progress_operation and drives report_progress over a synthetic >=3-shard processed_documents sequence.
- [ ] Asserts the ratio observed via backfill_progress() is > 0.0 from the first shard.
- [ ] Asserts the sampled ratios are monotonically non-decreasing across shards.
- [ ] No HTTP transport exercised (bookkeeping level only); cargo test passes for the new test in crates/miroir-core.

issue.description:
## What

Implement a contract-test suite that asserts every custom HTTP header in plan §5 "Custom HTTP headers" behaves exactly per its row. Many of the headers tie to feature beads; this bead tracks the unified contract test, not the feature implementations.

Headers from the §5 table:

| Header | Direction | Feature bead |
|--------|-----------|--------------|
| `X-Miroir-Degraded` | Response | §2 write path / scatter (already implemented in `routes/search.rs:298`, `routes/documents.rs`) |
| `X-Miroir-Settings-Version` | Response | §13.5 → `miroir-uhj.5.3` |
| `X-Miroir-Min-Settings-Version` | Request | §13.5 → `miroir-uhj.5.5` |
| `X-Miroir-Settings-Inconsistent` | Response | §13.5 → `miroir-uhj.5.x` (verify phase) |
| `X-Miroir-Session` | Both | §13.6 → `miroir-uhj.6` |
| `Idempotency-Key` | Request | §13.10 → `miroir-uhj.10` |
| `X-Miroir-Over-Fetch` | Request | §13.12 → `miroir-uhj.12` |
| `X-Miroir-Tenant` | Request | §13.15 → `miroir-uhj.15` |
| `X-Admin-Key` | Request | §13.19 / §5 dispatch (covered by `miroir-9dj.7`) |
| `X-CSRF-Token` | Request | §13.19 → `miroir-uhj.19.5` |
| `X-Search-UI-Key` | Request | §13.21 → `miroir-uhj.21.x` |

## Why

Each feature bead tests its own header in isolation; nothing asserts the FULL surface stays Meilisearch-compatible (clients that do not recognize these headers MUST keep working — §5 explicit promise). A single contract suite catches drift when a feature lands without honoring the request/response convention.

## Acceptance

- [ ] One test file `crates/miroir-proxy/tests/header_contract.rs`
- [ ] Round-trip test for every Request header: present, absent, malformed → expected status code per §5
- [ ] Echo test for every Response header: header is set when the feature condition holds, absent otherwise
- [ ] Forward-compat test: an unknown `X-Miroir-Future` is silently ignored (does not 400)
- [ ] Meilisearch-compat: a vanilla Meilisearch client (no Miroir headers) gets identical behavior to a single-node Meilisearch
- [ ] Test runs in CI on every PR

Parent epic: `miroir-9dj` (Phase 2 — Proxy + API Surface). Blocked by feature beads only insofar as they implement the headers; the test scaffolding can land first with `#[ignore]` for unimplemented headers.
issue.title: P2.10 Custom HTTP header contract test suite

        ...

Confirmed this is not a stale/dead path: `total_documents` is never populated from a
real node document-count query anywhere in the production reshard flow. Grepped every
write site of `total_documents` in crates/miroir-core/src/reshard.rs and
crates/miroir-core/src/reshard/executor.rs — every call sets it to `0` at struct
construction; `update_backfill_progress()` (reshard.rs:813) is defined but has zero
production callers (only referenced in test setup, e.g. reshard.rs:2023 sets
`total_documents = 1000` manually). mode_c_worker/mod.rs (the actual background-job
worker per plan §14.5 Mode C, which large reshard backfills route through) contains no
call to Meilisearch node /stats or any document-count query at all.

Downstream impact: admin_endpoints.rs:3640-3641 computes
`backfill_progress = documents_backfilled / total_documents` for the
`GET /_miroir/indexes/{uid}/reshard/status` admin endpoint (plan §4 Admin API table,
§13.1 online resharding). Since total_documents is always 0 in production, this ratio is
never meaningful — operators running an online reshard (plan §13.1, a major documented
capability with its own shadow-index dual-hash architecture) get no usable progress
signal during backfill, only phase name and documents_backfilled count with no
denominator.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Reshard backfill start (Phase 3 in reshard/executor.rs and/or the mode_c_worker
      reshard_backfill job path) queries each source node's `GET /indexes/{uid}/stats`
      (or equivalent per-shard count via the `_miroir_shard` filter) to compute a real
      total_documents value before backfill begins, and stores it via
      update_backfill_progress or equivalent.
- [ ] GET /_miroir/indexes/{uid}/reshard/status returns a non-zero, monotonically
      sensible backfill_progress ratio partway through a real reshard (verified via an
      integration test that starts a reshard on a populated index and polls status
      mid-backfill).
- [ ] Existing reshard tests (p5_1_d_reshard_verify.rs, p5_1_e_reshard_alias_swap.rs, and
      any ModeC reshard_backfill job tests) still pass.
- [ ] No behavior change to the reshard state machine itself (this is a progress-
      reporting fix, not a correctness fix to backfill migration logic).

## Priority rationale

P2 — not data-loss or security-affecting (the reshard itself completes correctly per the
plan §15 Open Problem 1 cutover-race testing), but it's a real, user-facing gap in a
capability the plan documents extensively (§13.1) and exposes via a documented admin API
that operators are expected to poll during a live topology change.
issue.title: Reshard backfill progress never populated: total_documents stays 0 in production

issue.close_reason: All acceptance criteria completed. search_handler and search_multi_targets already extract real client IP from X-Forwarded-For/X-Real-IP headers (matching admin_endpoints.rs pattern). Added comprehensive test suite p13_21_search_ui_rate_limit.rs with 10 passing tests covering per-IP isolation for both Redis and local backends, X-Forwarded-For parsing, X-Real-IP fallback, multi-pod shared buckets, and hash uniqueness for abuse forensics. Documented in CHANGELOG.md under Fixed section with behavior change note for operators.
issue.description:
## Evidence

crates/miroir-proxy/src/routes/search.rs has two separate handlers that hardcode the
client source IP to the literal string "unknown" instead of extracting it from the
request:

- search.rs:189-190 (`search_handler`, the main `POST /indexes/{index}/search` path
  used by the embedded search UI per plan §13.21):
      // TODO: Extract source IP from headers - need to add back HeaderMap extraction
      let source_ip = "unknown".to_string();
- search.rs:1026-1027 (`search_multi_targets`, used for multi-target-alias / ILM
  read_alias queries per §13.7/§13.17):
      // TODO: Extract source IP from headers
      let source_ip = "unknown".to_string();

Both values feed directly into the search-UI per-IP rate limiter: search.rs:205
(`redis.check_rate_limit_search_ui(&source_ip, ...)`) and search.rs:229
(local in-memory limiter `.check(&source_ip, ...)`), which back the
`search_ui.rate_limit.per_ip` config and the `miroir:ratelimit:searchui:<ip>` Redis
keyspace documented in plan §4 and §13.21. Plan §13.21 explicitly states
`GET /ui/search/{index}` is "the one public SPA entry point served outside /_miroir/"
and is "Rate-limited per source IP" — this is the primary anti-abuse control for an
endpoint that can run in fully unauthenticated `public` auth mode.

Because source_ip is always the constant "unknown", every client — regardless of real
IP — shares a single rate-limit bucket. In `public` auth mode this means: (a) the
control is not actually per-client, so one abusive client exhausts the shared budget for
every legitimate user (denial of service), and (b) source_ip_hash values logged at
search.rs:209/232/1046/1069 are useless for abuse forensics (they all hash the same
literal string).

Confirmed the extraction logic already exists elsewhere in the codebase and is not being
reused: admin_endpoints.rs:1374-1375 correctly extracts
source IP from `X-Forwarded-For`/`X-Real-IP` for the admin-login rate limiter
(bead miroir-46p.7, closed). The fix is to apply the same pattern in search.rs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] search_handler and search_multi_targets in crates/miroir-proxy/src/routes/search.rs
      extract the real client IP using the same header precedence as
      admin_endpoints.rs:1374-1375 (X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP, falling back to the
      connection's peer address via ConnectInfo where available), replacing the literal
      "unknown" TODO stubs at lines 189-190 and 1026-1027.
- [ ] Add a test (extending header_contract.rs or a new focused test) asserting that two
      requests with different X-Forwarded-For values are rate-limited independently
      (i.e. exhausting one IP's budget does not throttle a different IP), for both the
      Redis-backed and local in-memory rate limiter backends.
- [ ] Confirm source_ip_hash values logged for two different real client IPs differ in
      the structured logs.
- [ ] No change to rate-limit behavior when running behind a trusted proxy that already
      sets X-Forwarded-For correctly (existing deployments relying on "fail open to a
      shared bucket" should not silently become stricter in a way that surprises
      operators — document the change in CHANGELOG per plan §7 CHANGELOG format).

## Priority rationale

P1 — security/abuse-prevention gap on a documented public, potentially unauthenticated
endpoint (search_ui.auth.mode: public). The rate limiter is not a no-op, but it is not
doing its documented job (per-IP isolation), which is worse than an obviously-missing
feature because it looks functional in casual testing (limits still trigger, just on the
wrong key).
issue.title: Search-UI per-IP rate limiting is a no-op: source_ip hardcoded to literal unknown

Implement six-phase resharding: shadow create, dual-hash dual-write, backfill, verify, alias swap, cleanup.

issue.description:
## What

Implement write-path rejection of reserved `_miroir_*` field names per plan §5 "Reserved fields". The merger already strips these from responses (`crates/miroir-core/src/merger.rs:540, 955`); writes need the symmetric enforcement.

Reserved fields per §5 table:

| Field | Reserved when |
|-------|---------------|
| `_miroir_shard` | Always (unconditional) |
| `_miroir_updated_at` | Only when `anti_entropy.enabled: true` (§13.8) |
| `_miroir_expires_at` | Only when `ttl.enabled: true` (§13.14) |

When a configuration disables the conditional reservation, client values in that field MUST be preserved and passed through untouched. When reserved, a write containing the field is rejected with HTTP 400 `miroir_reserved_field`.

## Why

Plan §5 promises the contract; without write-path rejection clients can poison the rebalancer (`_miroir_shard`) and tie-breaker logic (`_miroir_updated_at`). Strip-on-response is implemented but reject-on-write is not.

## Acceptance

- [ ] POST/PUT `/indexes/{uid}/documents` containing `_miroir_shard` always returns 400 `miroir_reserved_field`
- [ ] When `anti_entropy.enabled: true`, writes with client-supplied `_miroir_updated_at` are rejected; when disabled, the field is preserved end-to-end
- [ ] When `ttl.enabled: true`, writes carrying `_miroir_expires_at` succeed (clients SET it); reads still strip it; when disabled, client values pass through
- [ ] Error body matches Meilisearch shape `{message, code, type, link}` with `code: miroir_reserved_field`
- [ ] Unit tests in `miroir-proxy/src/routes/documents.rs` cover all four matrix cells
- [ ] Integration test confirms `_miroir_shard` injected by orchestrator passes write-validation (orchestrator stamping path is exempt)

Parent epic: `miroir-9dj` (Phase 2 — Proxy + API Surface).
issue.title: P2.9 Reserved-field write rejection (miroir_reserved_field)

issue.description:
Split-child of bf-49a17 (reshard backfill progress never populated). Depends on child 1 (the document-count helper). Wires the inline reshard executor path to populate a real denominator at backfill start and propagate it to the persisted operation the admin endpoint reads.

## Scope

At Phase 3 `start_backfill`, call child 1's helper to compute the real `total_documents` BEFORE backfill begins (replacing the `total_documents: 0` placeholder), and propagate it to the persisted `ReshardOperation.total_documents` via `update_backfill_progress` so the admin status endpoint reads a real denominator. Reconcile the new up-front count with the existing per-shard incremental accumulation so the progress ratio is monotonic and non-zero from the start.

## Context (files)

- `crates/miroir-core/src/reshard/executor.rs:513-530` `start_backfill` sets `total_documents: 0` on the in-memory `BackfillProgress` (`executor.rs:43`).
- `crates/miroir-core/src/reshard.rs:749` persisted `ReshardOperation.total_documents`; `reshard.rs:813` `update_backfill_progress(backfilled, total)`; `reshard.rs:1134` async `update_backfill_progress` writes `self.leader.extra_state().total_documents = total`; `reshard.rs:819` `backfill_progress()` ratio returns 0.0 when `total_documents == 0`.
- `executor.rs:608-610` already accumulates `state.backfill_progress.total_documents += total_docs_in_shard` per shard — reconcile so the up-front count is not double-counted and the ratio stays in [0,1].

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `start_backfill` computes a non-zero `total_documents` from real node stats (via child 1's helper) before backfill begins.
- [ ] That value is propagated to the persisted `ReshardOperation.total_documents` so `backfill_progress()` (reshard.rs:819) returns a real ratio, not 0.0.
- [ ] Progress ratio is non-zero and monotonically non-decreasing from backfill start through completion (no double-count vs the existing per-shard accumulation at executor.rs:610).
- [ ] No correctness/behavior change to the reshard state machine or document migration (progress-reporting only).
issue.title: Populate total_documents at reshard backfill start and propagate to persisted operation

1. GET /health -> 200 (cycle 5 00:13:02.996957Z, req 81f0188f; RUN B at t+0.9/40/82/115s): LOCK SET EMPTY — LOCKS NONE, CONFIRMED. Registered main.rs:842. The wedged POST shares none of this: it passed the same lock-free gauntlet and then acquired the one lock /health never touches (topology.read). Its own requests_in_flight gauge entry is still outstanding (created :1716, drop :1720 never reached) — that is a counter, not a lock.

2. /nope -> 404 (cycle 5 00:18:30.048403Z, POST, req 2c9fc976, 5 ms, x-request-id present): LOCK SET EMPTY on BOTH branches, CONFIRMED; observed branch is the authenticated one. Authenticated branch (the cycle-5 capture — x-request-id present implies request_id_middleware, inner to auth, actually ran): bearer matches the node master key via dispatch Rule 3 (constant_time_compare, auth.rs:769 — pure string op) -> router miss -> axum default unmatched-route 404; there is NO .fallback() on the main router (main.rs:841-895; the only fallback is GET-scoped inside the /ui/search nest, search_ui.rs:150, unreachable from /nope). The /indexes nest (main.rs:850 -> routes/indexes.rs, router fn :304, registrations :308-330) enumerates exactly: / POST+GET (:309), /:index GET|PATCH|DELETE (:311-315), /:index/stats GET (:316), /:index/settings GET|PATCH|POST (:317-323), /:index/settings/*subpath GET|PATCH (:324-327), /:index/_preflight POST (:328), /:index/explain POST (:329), /:index/documents nest (:330). /products/search matches NOTHING and no /:index/search subroute exists anywhere in the crate (grep zero hits); the proxy search path is the different-prefix POST /search/:index (main.rs:852 -> search.rs:124-128). Scope caveat (precision, not drift): /indexes/* is not dispatch-exempt, so a request without a valid bearer 401s before routing — that branch is equally lock-free. EMPTY.

4. GET /indexes -> 200 in 259us: LOCK SET EMPTY IN THE PROXY PROCESS, CONFIRMED (proxied-not-node-served mechanism, re-confirmed here). Extractor is Extension(Arc<Config>) ONLY (:472) — no AppState, hence no topology / session_manager / query_coalescer / result_cache / Redis. Body: constructs a fresh MeilisearchClient per request (call :474; reqwest Client::builder with 10s timeout at indexes.rs:63-67, fn new :63) — a fresh client, not a shared lock — picks config.nodes.first() (503 if empty, :476-478), awaits ONE outbound GET {node}/indexes (:479-481, the handler's only await), 2xx -> parse to JSON (parse failure degrades to {"results":[]} but STILL returns 200, :486-488); transport error -> 500; non-2xx -> forwards the node's status. EMPTY in the proxy.

ROUTE-VS-TASK TRAP (explicit): the /health ROUTE and the health-checker BACKGROUND TASK are different tokio tasks in the SAME wedged process, with disjoint lock sets in BOTH directions. The ROUTE is a fresh per-request task; for GET /health it acquires NO lock end to end (row 1). The TASK is the single long-lived loop spawned once at startup (tokio::spawn main.rs:398-400 -> run_health_checker, fn main.rs:943): each tick (interval.tick().await main.rs:954; child-1-drift-corrected from the stale :943 cite, which is the fn signature) it takes state.topology.write().await (main.rs:956 — the sole topology.write in the file) and holds that guard across the WHOLE tick body — update_shard_metrics call :1087 (fn :1119), mark_ready().await :1098, prune_expired().await :1110, which in crates/miroir-core/src/session_pinning.rs (fn :318) takes sessions.write (:319) then pending_writes.write (:320) NESTED inside the topology hold — releasing all of it only at loop-body scope exit (main.rs:1114, implicit drop; loop closes :1115). Consequences, both directions: (a) a 200 from GET /health is NOT evidence the background task is alive — in this wedge it is provably parked; (b) nothing sent to /health can release or observe the task — the route writes nothing the task reads and reads nothing the route writes. Shared-nothing boundary: /health is fully shared-nothing (zero locks); /version — the MOUNTED route is main.rs:843 -> routes/version.rs:14-22, which takes State<S> and awaits version_state locks (:20): its own lock set is disjoint from topology/sessions/pending_writes so it still shares nothing with the wedge, but it is NOT a zero-lock handler like /health (the health.rs get_version copy, :29-35, is dead code); /_miroir/ready is NOT in the class — it contends (health.rs:47).

- stage 5 debug! "tenant affinity applied" (355-360) — debug-only

Stages 3, 6, 9, 10 (skipped on single-index), 11, 12, 13, 14, 16, 19, 21, 23 emit NOTHING at any level; stage 18's success path logs nothing; stage 24's handler-side body logs nothing (its spawned task: debug! 1113 / warn! 1116). EVERY log macro in search.rs:173-1140 between the anchors, classified (info-visible = level >= INFO in an INFO-level capture):

INFO-VISIBLE (all on CONDITIONAL paths; none appears in any of the 10 wedge instances, so each of these paths is excluded by absence — but none is on the normal path, so their absence cannot shrink the normal-path bracket):
- search.rs:204, 215, 227, 238 warn! — stage 2 rate-limit/config paths

== 4. NARROWING EVIDENCE THE TIMELINE DOES CARRY (index for later children; miroir-d9bf6824 / miroir-b32bcc98 / miroir-b6b71143) ==

TICK-TIMING DEPENDENT: cycle 5's 00:14:47Z tick carries NO span rid while its 00:09:47Z tick does — an absent rid on one background line is NOT span-close evidence (miroir-d9bf6824).

- For later children to combine with this bracket (from miroir-7f4bb6da's elimination notes): only three handler awaits can wait on anything slow — search.rs:901 (stage 18 DFS; the ONLY unbounded one), 276 (stage 4; bounded by max_wait, would emit a visible warn then continue) and 416 (stage 7; bounded by node_timeout_ms, would emit debug then continue); stage 13's topology RwLock read is the one in-process lock that can legitimately block (write-preferring tokio RwLock; health-checker writer).

1 resp1 success -> proxy rejects/errs the request
2 hits.len()==1 -> merge drops/dupes rows (1 doc matches "laptop")
3 hits[0].name=="Laptop" -> wrong row served
4 scatter==before+1 -> flat: unwired metric or short-circuited miss; doubled: retry/double scatter
5 resp2 success -> repeat request fails
6 result1==result2 -> cache body corruption, wrong-entry serve, or per-request nondeterministic body fields (holds under the bypass regression by design; comment says so, deltas own that regression)
7 hits==before+1 -> repeat recorded as a miss: entry never stored/evicted/expired (host stall past 500ms ttl_ms, anchored at insert, hits never refresh), or lookup Err counting neither counter
8 scatter_after_second==scatter_after_first -> served hit still scatters (the bypass regression; only this flat counter sees it)

acceptance_2_cache_miss_triggers_fan_out
1 resp success -> request fails
2 hits.len()==1 -> merge drops/dupes (1 doc matches "mouse")
3 name=="Mouse" -> wrong row
4 misses==before+1 -> query wrongly served as a hit, or lookup Err recording neither counter
5 scatter==before+1 -> miss path short-circuits (flat) or double-scatters (doubled)
6 resp2 success -> repeat fails
7 result==result2 -> round-trip corruption / wrong-entry serve (holds on both paths; delta 8 owns the serving claim)
8 hits==before+1 -> stored entry fails to serve the repeat (never stored/evicted/ttl stall)
9 scatter_after_second==scatter_after_first -> served hit still scatters (added by fd1703f exactly for this)

acceptance_3_cache_stores_results_after_scatter_gather
1 resp1 success -> request fails
2 scatter==before+1 -> flat: short-circuit/unwired metric; doubled: retry (also keeps delta 7 from holding vacuously)
3 resp2 success -> repeat fails
4 result1==result2 -> round-trip corruption / wrong-entry serve
5 hit_count==3 -> merge drops/dupes rows on the very body being cached (3 books match "rust")
6 hits==before+1 -> insert never landed/evicted early/ttl stall -> repeat is a second miss
7 scatter_after_second==scatter_after_first -> served hit still scatters

acceptance_4_cache_reduces_upstream_meilisearch_calls
1 resp success x5 -> request fails
2 results[0]==result x4 -> round-trip corruption; a repeat served a foreign body (loop ranges [1..], no self-compare)
3 hits==before+4 -> any repeat leaks past the cache as a miss (never stored/evicted/ttl stall)
4 scatter==before+1 -> flat: first query short-circuited; >=+2: a served hit that still fans out. Independent of 3: hit-recorded-but-scattering passes 3 and fails 4

acceptance_5_different_queries_use_different_cache_keys
1-4 resp1-4 success -> request fails
5 misses==before+4 -> a collision serves a foreign entry as a hit: q2 onto q1's entry (text-ignoring key), q4 onto q2's (limit-ignoring key) -> delta falls to +3
6 scatter==before+4 -> the colliding hit short-circuits its fan-out (flat) or a retry doubles it; independent of 5
7 ne(result1.hits,result2.hits) -> collision merging q2 into q1's entry equalizes the rows
8 ne(result2.hits,result3.hits) -> same for the q2/q3 pair
   deliberate absence: no row assert separates q4 from q2 (one Desk doc -> rows equal by construction); documented in-file; delta 5 is the surviving detector
9-12 resp*_cached success -> repeat fails
13-16 resultN==resultN_cached -> repeat served out of a foreign entry with different rows, or body corruption (pair 4 blind by construction, documented; delta 5 keeps the entries distinct)
17 hits==before+4 -> a repeat not served as a hit (entry lost/ttl stall); repeats re-scattering would still pass 13-16, so this delta is the only detector
18 scatter_after_repeats==scatter_after_first_pass -> served hit still scatters

issue.close_reason: Captured live: the proxy answers the failing first search POST (POST /indexes/products/search) with 404 Not Found and an empty body. Cause family: route not found — the search handler is mounted only at POST /search/:index (main.rs:852, routes/search.rs:128); indexes::router has no /:index/search route and there is no fallback, so axum 0.7.9 returns its default 404/empty. Auth passed (valid master key) and the empty body rules out upstream passthrough, 5xx, and auth. Reproduced deterministically on v1.8.3 nodes with ports free; signature B (PUT settings -> 405) also reproduced in the same run, and the ~205ms readiness was shown to be normal, ruling out the stray-proxy hypothesis. Full note on the bead.
issue.description:
Split child 2/4 of miroir-1ec135a1, depends on child 1 (the search.rs diff verdict aims this reproduction). Scope: empirical capture of what the proxy actually returns on the first search POST that trips signature A ("assertion failed: resp.status().is_success()").

Method (either is acceptable):
- Rebuild the suite topology by hand: spawn the meilisearch node(s) the harness uses (confirm the pinned tag from testcontainers-modules 0.11.6 - expected v1.8.3), start miroir-proxy the way the harness does, then curl the first search POST the suite makes and record status plus full body.
- Or add a temporary error-body print next to the assertion at crates/miroir-proxy/tests/p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs:508 (first signature A site) and run one failing test.

Gotchas (hard-won, from memory/CLAUDE.md): the suite hard-binds ports 17770/9090 - a stray foreign miroir-proxy can pass readiness and poison the run, so check ss -ltnp first; docker.sock is the runtime (no DOCKER_HOST); /health is 200 not 204. The cargo wrapper on this box swallows stderr - when running the suite locally use ~/.cargo/bin/cargo under systemd-run if you need the panic output.

Acceptance criteria:
- A note on this bead quoting the exact HTTP status code and response body the proxy returns on the failing first search.
- The note maps that response to a cause family: upstream/node error passed through, proxy-internal 5xx, route not found, auth, or connection-level failure.
- If the reproduction does not reproduce, the note states what differed (env, image tag, ports) - that is still a closable outcome.
issue.notes:
CAPTURE (2026-09-11, live run of acceptance_1 + acceptance_10, probe print at the line-508 assertion, temp edit reverted after capture):

The proxy returns HTTP 404 Not Found with an EMPTY body on the failing first search POST (POST http://127.0.0.1:17770/indexes/products/search, Authorization: Bearer test_master_key, body {"q":"laptop","limit":10}).

Raw probe output:
  proxy ready in 205.14ms
  PROBE first-search status=404 Not Found body=
  thread panicked at p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs:514: PROBE first-search failed: status=404 Not Found body=

CAUSE FAMILY: route not found. Evidence chain: (1) auth passed first — the request carries the configured master key, and auth_middleware (auth.rs:822) runs before routing, so a 401 would have been returned instead if auth were the problem; (2) the empty body rules out upstream passthrough (Meilisearch errors are JSON: {"message","code","type","link"}) and rules out a proxy-internal 5xx; (3) the proxy mounts the search handler ONLY at POST /search/:index — main.rs:852 nests search::router at /search and routes/search.rs:128 is Router::new().route("/:index", post(search_handler)); (4) indexes::router (routes/indexes.rs:304-330) has NO /:index/search route (only /, /:index, /:index/stats, /:index/settings[/*subpath], /:index/_preflight, /:index/explain, /:index/documents), and main.rs has no .fallback(), so POST /indexes/products/search (two segments after /indexes) matches no route pattern at all; (5) axum 0.7.9 (Cargo.lock) answers an unmatched route with exactly 404 + empty body. The suite POSTs the Meilisearch-native path /indexes/{uid}/search at all 20+ search call sites (501, 538, 624, ... 1387), which is why signature A fires on the FIRST search of 9 tests.

Fix-surface implication for the parent diagnosis: plan principle 1 is "invisible federation — clients talk to one endpoint using the standard Meilisearch API", and the suite speaks that native path, so the fix surface is the PROXY (register the standard POST /indexes/:index/search route), not the tests. That call belongs to child 1/the fix bead; this capture only aims it.

Reproduction conditions: WORKING TREE WITH the uncommitted search.rs diff present (cache-key reuse rework); testcontainers getmeili/meilisearch:v1.8.3 (confirms the pinned tag); ports 17770/9090 verified free via ss -ltnp immediately before the run; docker.sock runtime. It reproduces deterministically — no environment difference to report.

Side observations from the same run: (a) signature B also reproduced verbatim — acceptance_10: "Failed to update settings on http://localhost:33170: 405 Method Not Allowed" (set_node_settings PUT to node /indexes/{uid}/settings on v1.8.3), corroborating parent lead 2 (PUT vs PATCH); (b) readiness in ~205ms reproduced with a genuine harness-spawned proxy, so the ~205ms in the captured failing-run logs was normal fast binding, NOT a foreign proxy holding the port — the stray-proxy poisoning hypothesis is ruled out for these failures (the ~6s comment at p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs:311 is stale).

issue.notes:
p13_13 scaffolding audit (read-only; no assertion edits). All ground truth verified against source at HEAD 7401f22.

== SHARED SCAFFOLDING (leaned on by acceptance_1..5) ==

S1 Fresh proxy process per test (SpawnedProxy::spawn): each test spawns its own miroir-proxy binary -> own Metrics registry (middleware.rs:620-630 counters, :598 histogram). Baselines reflect only that test's traffic; no cross-test counter contamination unless a foreign process holds the ports (see S6).

S2 Generated config (proxy_config_yaml): result_cache enabled, ttl_ms 500, max_size 1000; RF1/single group, all 3 nodes in group 0; sqlite task store; cdc overflow drop; search_ui off. Does NOT set query_coalescing -> default enabled (config.rs:625) - see S5.

S3 proxy_counter floor: absent series reads Ok(0); a dead endpoint errors the read outright (send()? precedes the fallback). Whole-token first-field match - no collision with _bucket/_sum/# HELP. Ground truth: hits/misses are unlabelled Counters; scatter_fan_out_size is an unlabelled Histogram and record_scatter_fan_out -> observe() bumps _count exactly once per fan-out EVENT (middleware.rs:1834-1836) - the tests count events, not nodes fanned to.

S4 search.rs ordering (the central ground truth):
- HIT: inc_result_cache_hits (search.rs:522) strictly precedes the early return (556); that return precedes the multi-target branch (600) and BOTH record_scatter_fan_out sites (811 single-target, 1406 multi-target) -> a served hit records +1 hit and structurally cannot fan out. Increments are awaited inline before the response is sent, so proxy_counter sees them once the client sees the response - no sleep/race window.
- MISS: inc_result_cache_misses (567) -> falls through to exactly one observe (811). Corrupt cached bytes -> miss (561) + scatter (both move; indistinguishable from a fresh miss). Cache lookup Err -> NEITHER counter + scatter (573-576); unreachable here (ResultCache::get errs only when disabled, result_cache.rs:135-137, and the config enables it).
- INSERT BEFORE RETURN: insert awaited at 944, response built at 1007 -> entry durable before resp1 reaches the client -> no race under any "repeat is a hit" bound.
- GATE: enabled && resolved_targets.len()==1 (491); direct index queries resolve to vec![index] (251-264) -> gate open.
- TTL: anchored at insert (result_cache.rs:48 expires_at=now+ttl); get never refreshes it (141-153; LRU recency bumps, expiry does not). Expired -> popped + miss.
- LRU eviction cannot fire (max_size 1000 vs <=3 distinct keys per test) - not a vacuous-bound vector.
- canonicalize_query recursively key-sorts the WHOLE body -> every field incl. limit is in the key (acc5 query3's limit-20 differentiator is real).

S5 FLAG - coalescing is inert only by sequencing. Coalescing sits BEFORE the cache lookup (search.rs:392) and is enabled by default (not disabled by S2). Its early return (465) records NO hit/miss counter and NO fan-out - a request served there is invisible to every delta. Inert only because try_coalesce is subscribe-only (idempotency.rs:194-207, no registration) and every acc1..5 query is awaited sequentially, so no identical fingerprint is ever concurrently pending. Hit-path return (556) precedes registration (885) -> no stale fingerprint leaks. If a future edit parallelizes a repeat loop, repeats coalesce and the hits delta falls short - a sequencing-lean to re-check then.

S6 FLAG - readiness is not identity; foreign-process poisoning (LIVE RIGHT NOW). /health returns {"status":"available"} unconditionally once bound (routes/health.rs), so wait_for_ready pins "a miroir-proxy answers 17770", not "this test's proxy is bound". A stray miroir-proxy holding 17770+9090 passes readiness instantly while the spawned child dies EADDRINUSE; requests then hit the foreign proxy and proxy_counter reads the foreign registry -> flat counters -> the absolute deltas FAIL loudly (never pass silently). At audit time pid 1716428 (/tmp/p13diag-1ec135a1 scratch session, up ~49 min) holds both ports - a live suite run needs it gone first (or MIROIR_TEST_SKIP_DOCKER=1). Left alone here (not this bead's process).

S7 Vacuous-pass check on the absent-metric floor: the flat-vs-flat bypass asserts (acc1:562, acc2:680, acc3:798, acc5:1077) WOULD hold vacuously if the series vanished (all reads 0) - but each is preceded in its own test by absolute deltas that 0==0 fails: acc1 scatter+1:520 and hits+1:550 before 562; acc2 635/643/667 before 680; acc3 750/785 before 798; acc5 989/1001 before 1077; acc4 is absolutes only (879, 893). No absent-metric path reaches a flat assert un-tripped.

S8 FLAG - container fixture timing: create_index/add_documents/set_node_settings do NOT poll the Meilisearch task queue; a fixed sleep(500ms) then assume applied. Row asserts lean on it: acc1 510-511, acc2 624-625, acc3 774, acc5 1011-1012 (with zero indexed rows acc5's assert_ne fails - both arrays empty-equal). Usually ample locally; a timing assumption, not ground truth.

S9 FLAG - 500 ms TTL vs pacing (the flake vector the comments name): no test sleeps between query1 and the repeat; the bounds assume the gap stays under 500 ms. A host stall expires the entry -> repeat reads as miss -> hits delta short + one extra scatter - deliberately indistinguishable from a lookup regression. Most exposed: acc4 hits+4 (879) - the 5-query loop must fit within 500 ms of query1's insert; each expired repeat re-scatters, re-inserts and resets the clock, so any single expiry breaks the +4. acc5's three repeats likewise need each entry alive from its first-pass insert.

== PER-TEST INVENTORY ==

acc1 (hit bypasses fan-out): baselines 492/495 <- S1,S3. Rows len==1/"Laptop" 510-511 <- S8. scatter_after_first==+1 520 <- S4 miss-path single-observe (detects unwired=flat, retry=doubled). result1==result2 541 - non-discriminating by design (both paths equal). hits+1 550 <- S4 hit-ordering 522<556 + insert-before-return 944<1007; pacing lean S9. scatter flat 562 <- S4 structural bypass; vacuous pre-empted by 520/550 (S7).

acc2 (miss triggers fan-out): baselines 603-610 <- S1,S3. Rows 624-625 <- S8. misses+1 635 <- S4 Ok(None)->567 (a failure detector, not a cause discriminator: "wrongly served as hit" and "lookup Err recorded neither" both fail it; the latter unreachable per S4). scatter+1 643 <- S4. hits+1 667 <- S4 insert-before-return; S9 lean. scatter flat 680 <- S4; pre-empted by 635/643/667.

acc3 (stores after scatter-gather): baselines 722-727 <- S1,S3. scatter+1 750 - deliberately BEFORE the repeat so the flat assert cannot hold vacuously <- S4. hit_count==3 774 <- S8 + fixture semantics (all 3 titles match "rust", limit 20) - pins merge row-preservation on the exact body being cached. result1==result2 771 - non-discriminating. hits+1 785 <- S4+S9 (comment names ttl_ms 500 load-bearing). scatter flat 798 <- S4.

acc4 (reduces upstream calls): baselines 840-845 <- S1,S3. 5 identical bodies 866-868 - non-discriminating. hits+4 879 <- S4+S9 (most TTL-exposed bound in the suite). scatter+1 893 <- S4; absolute, no flat pair here. The "15 vs 3 upstream calls" narrative leans on the 3-node fixture (S2) - but the pin is 1 fan-out event vs 5, since _count counts events not nodes (S3).

acc5 (different cache keys): baselines 936-944 <- S1,S3. misses+3 989 <- S4; the collision detector that survives equal rows (sequential queries; a key collision would serve q2 from q1's entry as a hit and fall short). Distinct-key fixture: different q terms; query3's limit-20 differentiator is real per S4. scatter+3 1001 <- S4. assert_ne row pairs 1011-1012 <- S8 (needs rows to exist AND differ; goes blind on an equal-rows collision, as its own comment states - 989 is the surviving detector). repeat bodies 1054-1056 - catch foreign-entry replay; non-discriminating for bypass. hits+3 1065 <- S4+S9 (each entry must survive first-pass insert -> repeat). scatter flat 1077 <- S4; pre-empted by 989/1001.

VERDICT: scaffolding is sound for acceptance_1..5. Every counter bound has a verified ground-truth fact beneath it (S4); the absent-metric floor cannot make a bound pass vacuously (S7). Four leans flagged - S5 coalescing inert-by-sequencing, S8 task-apply-by-fixed-sleep, S9 TTL-vs-pacing, S6 foreign-port poisoning (currently live) - none vacuous; all fail loudly. No assertion changes (per scope).

issue.notes:
Audited acceptance_1_cache_hit_bypasses_fan_out (tests/p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs L448-554), re-derived from the counter chain in the current tree: miroir_result_cache_hits_total increments at exactly two sites — search.rs:522 (single-index hit path) and multi_search.rs:359 (route this test never calls); the hit path returns the cached body at search.rs:556 BEFORE record_scatter_fan_out at search.rs:811, and search.rs:1406 lives in search_multi_targets (fn starts L1147), a disjoint handler the single-index request never enters (cache lookup itself gated on resolved_targets.len()==1 at :491). miroir_scatter_fan_out_size_count is the observation count of the scatter_fan_out_size histogram (middleware.rs:600), one obs per fan-out event. proxy_counter reads an absent series as 0, so a dead metrics endpoint fails the +1 deltas loudly, never silently.

Per-assert findings:
1. L500 assert!(resp1.status().is_success()) — CAN-FIRE: any regression turning the uncached search into an error response (upstream auth, 5xx, route misconfig). Gate for the row asserts.
2. L502 assert_eq!(hits.len(), 1) — CAN-FIRE: wrong row count — scatter-merge regression emitting duplicates (3 = one per node) or dropping rows (0); .as_array().unwrap() also fires if the schema drops "hits". Kept.
3. L503 assert_eq!(result1["hits"][0]["name"], "Laptop") — CAN-FIRE: content regression — ranking/typo change promoting Phone/Tablet for q="laptop", wrong field projection. Kept.
4. L507-514 assert_eq!(scatter_after_first, scatter_before + 1) — CAN-FIRE, load-bearing: fires on fan-out recorded per node instead of per event (+3 with 3 nodes) and on any first-query short-circuit that serves rows without a fan-out (+0). Also keeps the flat bypass check at L547-553 non-vacuous: without it a dropped/doubled counter makes the bypass assert pass trivially. Kept.
5. L526 assert!(resp2.status().is_success()) — CAN-FIRE: hit path returning non-2xx (deserialize failure surfaced as 5xx, or a regression re-running the scatter on the hit path and propagating an upstream error).
6. L531 assert_eq!(result1, result2) — CAN-FIRE: cache round-trip corruption (serialize/deserialize asymmetry, partial write served) or key collision serving a different entry. In-file comment already documents it as insufficient alone; the deltas carry the bypass proof. Kept.
7. L537-544 assert_eq!(hits_after, hits_before + 1) — CAN-FIRE, load-bearing: the "hit recorded as a hit" pin. Baseline placement correct — query 1 is a fresh-cache miss and the miss branch increments misses_total (search.rs:567), not hits, so the +1 is attributable solely to query 2. Fires on store-key/lookup-key mismatch (repeat becomes a miss), hits incremented on the wrong side, or double-increment. The in-file TTL caveat verified accurate: the hit path only calls get() (search.rs:516-556) and never refreshes the entry, so a >500ms stall reads as a miss and fires — a documented flakiness edge, not a never-fires issue. Kept.
8. L547-553 assert_eq!(scatter_after_second, scatter_after_first) — CAN-FIRE, load-bearing: this IS the acceptance. Fires on any regression that records a hit but still executes the fan-out (hit return at :556 removed, cache lookup moved after planning, fan-out recording hoisted above the lookup). The only regression that passes it while bypassing the cache — a short-circuit that neither hits nor fans out — already fails assert 7. Kept.

Soundness checks that found nothing: baselines sit immediately before query 1 with no intervening traffic (health probes do not touch either counter); the query coalescer cannot absorb query 2 (query 1 completes before query 2 is sent) and would fail assert 7 anyway; no absurd-extreme or self-equality comparisons exist — the two scatter reads are distinct counter samples.

VERDICT: NOTHING FOUND — no replacement bounds or 3ca59fe-style comments needed; no edits made. Matches the miroir-77a3dce4 prior verdict, independently re-derived: prior L503-507/L533-537/L543-546 map to current L507-514/L537-544/L547-553 (log-tail commits shifted the test ~11 lines down).

issue.notes:
=== p13_13 ROOT-CAUSE DIAGNOSIS (consolidated) ===
Compiled 2026-09-11 by miroir-b978b544 from split children 1-3: miroir-9ce8c5d7 (search.rs diff vs signature A), miroir-10842a18 (live status/body capture), miroir-49ae723b (settings PUT 405 vs meilisearch v1.8.3). Fix surface is aimed at fix bead miroir-fcc10451.

Context: all three 2026-09-11 live runs (04:56, 05:22, 05:52 logs; quoted below so the diagnosis survives /tmp cleanup) ended 0 passed / 10 failed in ~14s with proxy readiness ~205ms every time. Infrastructure is NOT the cause — both signatures are deterministic code/API mismatches.

NOTE ON LINE NUMBERS: the three logs show shifted panic lines for the same failures because the harness grew between runs (fd1703f 04:24, 8c1b2db 05:47, 7401f22 06:22 — all after earlier captures). Canonical numbers below are from the freshest 05:52 run; current-file anchors are given alongside.

--- SIGNATURE A — 9/10 tests: the FIRST proxy search POST returns 404 (route never existed) ---

Symptom (quoted from /tmp/p13_13-live-2026-09-11.log, 05:52):

    ---- acceptance_1_cache_hit_bypasses_fan_out stdout ----
    proxy ready in 205.30ms
    thread 'acceptance_1_cache_hit_bypasses_fan_out' panicked at crates/miroir-proxy/tests/p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs:508:5:
    assertion failed: resp1.status().is_success()

Same assert-panic at the first search of acceptance_1/2/3/4/5/6/7/8/9 (05:52-log lines 508/622/738/858/959/1023/1068/1135/1196; current-file first-search asserts are 508/622/738/858/973/1121/1166/1233/1294). acceptance_8 adds the secondary JoinError re-panic (quoted):

    thread 'acceptance_8_concurrent_cache_access' panicked at crates/miroir-proxy/tests/p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs:1135:13:
    assertion failed: resp.status().is_success()
    thread 'acceptance_8_concurrent_cache_access' panicked at crates/miroir-proxy/tests/p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs:1146:35:
    called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: JoinError::Panic(Id(296), "assertion failed: resp.status().is_success()", ...)

ROOT CAUSE: route contract mismatch. The suite POSTs the Meilisearch-native path /indexes/{uid}/search to the proxy; the proxy serves search ONLY at POST /search/:index and has no fallback, so axum answers 404 with an empty body on every test's very first search.

Evidence chain (each step verified live or in-source):
1. Test call site — p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs:501 (assert at 508):
       .post(format!("{}/indexes/products/search", setup.proxy_url))
2. Proxy registration — crates/miroir-proxy/src/routes/search.rs:128:
       axum::Router::new().route("/:index", axum::routing::post(search_handler))
   nested at "/search" in crates/miroir-proxy/src/main.rs:852. The indexes router (crates/miroir-proxy/src/routes/indexes.rs:304-330) registers /, /:index, /:index/stats, /:index/settings (+/settings/*subpath), /:index/_preflight, /:index/explain, /:index/documents — NO /:index/search. `git log -S ':index/search' -- crates/miroir-proxy/src/routes/indexes.rs` is EMPTY: the route never existed in history.
3. Empirical capture (child 2, live suite run with a temporary probe print at the 508 assert, reverted after capture):
       proxy ready in 205.14ms
       PROBE first-search status=404 Not Found body=
   on POST http://127.0.0.1:17770/indexes/products/search with valid bearer auth and body {"q":"laptop","limit":10}.
4. Independent curl (child 1) against a standing miroir-proxy:
       POST /indexes/products/search  ->  HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
                                         x-request-id: 39aeaca4
                                         content-length: 0
   while POST /search/products on the same process was ACCEPTED by the router. The empty body + auth passing first (auth_middleware runs before routing) = router 404 — NOT upstream passthrough (Meilisearch errors are JSON {"message","code","type","link"}), NOT a proxy-internal 5xx, NOT auth (that would be 401).
5. Symmetry note: the proxy itself SPEAKS the native path outbound — crates/miroir-proxy/src/main.rs:712 formats "{}/indexes/{}/search" for scatter calls to real nodes. The suite is addressing the proxy the way the proxy addresses upstreams.

RULED OUT — the uncommitted search.rs working-tree diff (26 insertions / 58 deletions, cache-key reuse rework) does NOT cause A. Child 1 read all five hunks: (1) a pure `let mut result_cache_key: Option<...> = None;` declaration; (2) an infallible `result_cache_key = Some(cache_key.clone());` capture; (3)+(4) deletions of two clones consumed only by the deleted store block; (5) the ~50-line store rewrite whose every path is error-swallowed (`if let Some(cache_key)`, `if let Ok(response_bytes)`, insert Err → debug!) with no `?`/unwrap/early return, running after response content is fixed. The status decisions (503 at search.rs:790, 500 at search.rs:910, 200 at search.rs:1008) sit outside every hunk. Structural argument: a handler panic would drop the connection and fail at `.send().await.unwrap()`; the observed `assertion failed: resp.status().is_success()` requires a well-formed non-2xx response — the proxy deliberately answered 4xx.

Scope of A: 21 `.post(format!("{proxy}/indexes/.../search"))` call sites in p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs alone (501, 529, 615, 652, 731, 759, 851, 948, 957, 966, 1017, 1026, 1035, 1113, 1159, 1175, 1226, 1287, 1318, 1378, 1394); child 1 counted 23 across the test tree. Other suites also address the proxy with the native path: integration_test.rs:158, phase2_integration_test.rs:113 — and fixtures assume the path is real: p7_5_structured_logging.rs:68/235 expects the log line "GET /indexes/products/search 200", p10_6_csrf_posture.rs:403 classifies "/indexes/products/search" as a real request path.

--- SIGNATURE B — acceptance_10 only: settings PUT 405 (plain harness bug) ---

Symptom (quoted from the 05:52 run):

    ---- acceptance_10_cache_with_complex_query stdout ----
    proxy ready in 205.08ms
    thread 'acceptance_10_cache_with_complex_query' panicked at crates/miroir-proxy/tests/p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs:1268:10:
    called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: Failed to update settings on http://localhost:33107: 405 Method Not Allowed

The other two runs show the identical 405 at their per-run ephemeral container ports: localhost:33077 (05:22 log), localhost:33016 (04:56 log).

ROOT CAUSE: harness bug. set_node_settings (p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs:401) PUTs {url}/indexes/{uid}/settings DIRECTLY to each node (the .put at line 405; index management bypasses the proxy per the comment at ~398-400), bails at line 412 on non-success, and the suite's ONLY caller — acceptance_10's filterableAttributes setup at line 1361 — unwraps the Err into the panic.

Why PUT 405s: the spawned nodes are getmeili/meilisearch:v1.8.3 (testcontainers-modules 0.11.6 pins TAG v1.8.3 in its meilisearch module; the test uses Meilisearch::default().with_master_key(...) with no with_tag override; confirmed live: GET /version -> {"pkgVersion":"1.8.3","commitSha":"7d699532676b6ad3a692130fe721c88565cf7bc3"}). Meilisearch replaced PUT with PATCH on settings routes in v1.8.0. On v1.8.3 the aggregate settings route registers only patch/get/delete (meilisearch/src/routes/indexes/settings.rs @ tag v1.8.3, generate_configure! macro, lines 651-653: web::patch().to(SeqHandler(update_all)) / web::get() / web::delete() — no web::put).

Empirical curl (child 3, spawned v1.8.3 node):
    PUT   /indexes/probe/settings -> 405 Method Not Allowed   (response header: allow: PATCH, GET, DELETE)
    PATCH /indexes/probe/settings -> 202 Accepted             (settingsUpdate task)
Reproduced identically on the standing diagnosis-topology node. Nuance: only the AGGREGATE settings route is PATCH-only on v1.8.3; per-setting sub-routes (e.g. /settings/search-cutoff-ms via make_setting_route!) still accept PUT — irrelevant to acceptance_10, which fails on the aggregate route.

RULED OUT: the proxy — acceptance_10's settings update never touches it (direct-to-node request). This is a one-token test fix, not a proxy bug.

--- OTHER FINDINGS ---

1. Readiness ~205ms is GENUINE, not a foreign-squatter artifact. Child 2 reproduced 205.14ms with a genuine harness-spawned proxy after verifying 17770/9090 free via ss -ltnp. The "~6s spawn time" expectation in the wait_for_ready doc comment (test file line 310) is stale. Caveat kept on record: a stray diag miroir-proxy WAS found squatting 127.0.0.1:17770 + 0.0.0.0:9090 during the diagnosis window and it passes the exact-body /health check, so port-squatting remains a real hazard for this fixed-port suite (check ss -ltnp before live runs; a squatter would also answer readiness and poison a run) — but it cannot explain these failures: a squatter 404s the same unregistered route, so signature A reproduces on ANY build.
2. search.rs working-tree diff disposition: do NOT revert it as part of the fix — it is unrelated to both signatures; its only semantic change is cache-store correctness (store under the lookup-time key/version instead of re-deriving post-scatter).
3. Fixing B alone does NOT make acceptance_10 pass: its first search POST (line 1378) would then hit signature A's 404 exactly like the other nine tests. Both fixes are required for 10/10.

--- FIX SURFACE (for miroir-fcc10451) ---

BOTH sides, one change each:

1. PROXY — signature A (the real fix): register the Meilisearch-compatible route POST /indexes/:index/search.
   - Option a (recommended): add `.route("/:index/search", post(...))` to the router at crates/miroir-proxy/src/routes/indexes.rs:304-330, delegating to the existing handler (search_handler, crates/miroir-proxy/src/routes/search.rs; its current router sits at search.rs:122-129). Mind the path-param position change (/search/:index becomes /indexes/:index/search — middle segment).
   - Option b: nest a search sub-router under /indexes in crates/miroir-proxy/src/main.rs:850-853 with an adapter for the moved param.
   Why the proxy, not the tests: plan principle 1 — invisible federation, clients talk to one endpoint using the standard Meilisearch API (the suite speaks exactly that); 21 call sites in this suite plus native-path callers/fixtures in integration_test.rs, phase2_integration_test.rs, p7_5_structured_logging.rs, p10_6_csrf_posture.rs would all need edits otherwise; and the proxy already uses the native path outbound (main.rs:712), so accepting it inbound is symmetric.
2. TEST HARNESS — signature B (one token): crates/miroir-proxy/tests/p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs:405 `.put(` -> `.patch(` inside set_node_settings (the bail at 412 and the caller at 1361 stay unchanged).
3. NOT the fix: reverting the search.rs working-tree diff (ruled out above).

issue.notes:
p13_13 first-search + control CAPTURED against child 2's running topology (miroir-454e8c77), then torn down. Raw artifacts: ~/scratch/p13_13_first_search_capture.logs/{capture-20260912T000519Z.log, control-attempt2-20260912T000519Z.log, proxy-logs-20260912T000519Z.log}. Provenance: HEAD 09b7866, worktree search.rs pre-dirty ( M crates/miroir-proxy/src/routes/search.rs, present before dispatch, not mine), binary built 2026-09-11 16:42, same binary as prior cycles.

=== 1) NATIVE PATH (the path the p13_13 suite POSTs) — VERBATIM ===
POST /indexes/products/search, Authorization: Bearer test_master_key, body {"q":"laptop","limit":10}, answered in <1s:

HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
x-request-id: 6577bfec
content-length: 0
date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 00:05:19 GMT

(empty body — content-length: 0)

=== 2) CONTROL (POST /search/products, same process, same key, same body) — NO RESPONSE EVER ===
DIVERGENCE from prior cycles (which answered 200 + x-miroir-degraded + 55-byte body in the same second as the native 404). Tonight the control request WEDGES: connection ESTABLISHED, zero response bytes, handler never completes. Attempt 1 (00:05:20) was still pending at teardown — killed after 15:16 elapsed, 0 bytes received; its capture section is empty because there was literally nothing to write. Attempt 2 on a fresh connection, bounded -m 150 (verbatim):

curl: (28) Operation timed out after 150002 milliseconds with 0 bytes received

The process was alive throughout the wedge — cross-checks on the SAME process: GET /health -> HTTP/1.1 200 OK in 14 ms (00:13:02, request_id 81f0188f); POST /nope (unknown path) -> HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found in 5 ms (00:18:30, request_id 2c9fc976). So the wedge is specific to the registered /search/:index handler, not the listener or router.

=== 3) PROXY'S OWN LOG LINES (request-id cross-check) ===
Native 6577bfec — MATCHES the response x-request-id above, verbatim from proxy.stdout.log:

{"timestamp":"2026-09-12T00:05:19.999942Z","level":"WARN","pod_id":"unknown","request_id":"6577bfec","message":"POST 404 Not Found","duration_ms":0,"status":404,"method":"POST","path_template":"/indexes/products/search","target":"miroir.request","span":{"method":"POST","path_template":"/indexes/products/search","pod_id":"unknown","request_id":"6577bfec","name":"request"}}

Control — there is NO miroir.request completion line and no response, hence no x-request-id to match. But the proxy DID accept and route it: at 00:09:47 two background-worker WARN lines (mode_a_coordinator "peer discovery failed ... SRV lookup failed for _http._tcp.miroir-headless.default.svc.cluster.local"; drift_reconciler "failed to refresh peer set") carry the STILL-OPEN request span, verbatim:

{"timestamp":"2026-09-12T00:09:47.192214Z","level":"WARN","message":"peer discovery failed: discovery error: SRV lookup failed for _http._tcp.miroir-headless.default.svc.cluster.local: no record found for name: _http._tcp.miroir-headless.default.svc.cluster.local type: SRV class: IN","target":"miroir_core::mode_a_coordinator","span":{"method":"POST","path_template":"/search/:index","pod_id":"unknown","request_id":"abf9606e","name":"request"}}

request_id abf9606e = the control request; span path_template /search/:index proves the route matched (unlike the native path, which 404s at the router). The open span leaking onto background lines 4.5 min after arrival is direct evidence the handler was parked, not slow. Corroborating state at capture time: miroir-tasks.db-wal growing ~1.6 KB/s (anti-entropy writing; 1.7->2.1 MB over the window); leader_lease row "rebalance:default" renewing every few seconds; anti-entropy pass ("16 shards to scan") had started at 23:59:47, ~32s after proxy spawn. Candidate mechanism for child 4/umbrella: once the first anti-entropy pass is mid-flight, the /search/:index handler blocks indefinitely (peer-discovery/shard-map wait with no fail-fast), where freshly-spawned topologies degrade to 200. The p13_13 suite keeps one proxy across many tests, so later tests' first search POSTs hit exactly this mature-topology wedge.

=== 4) TEARDOWN CONFIRMED (2026-09-12T00:20:36Z) ===
- kill -TERM 2439395 -> proxy gone (TERM sufficient, no KILL needed).
- docker rm -f p13_13-topo-meili-20260911T235933Z -> removed (docker ps -a filter returns empty).
- rm -rf /tmp/p13_13-topo.M5oBEi (proxy cwd/config/task db).
- Verification: `ss -ltn` shows NO listener on 17770 or 9090; `pgrep -a -x miroir-proxy` empty and no miroir* process at all; container gone. My attempt-1 curl (2444053) killed with it.

No repo file changes — capture-only work; nothing to commit.

ROUND-11 CHILD-2 — PER-ROUTE LOCK SETS IN THE WEDGED PROXY PROCESS (read-only derivation; no source modified).

SCOPING RULE: every answer below is the lock set held IN THE WEDGED PROXY PROCESS — the single process hosting the parked POST /search/:index handler (span open on /search/:index), parked at state.topology.read().await search.rs:667 [re-verified at :667 in the working tree @ HEAD 316b0ec; the foreign uncommitted search.rs diff (26+/58-) starts at :476 and touches neither :667 nor any route-registration site].
