Input: audit miroir-959307ee (closed); every load-bearing line cited below was independently re-verified in the tree.

## 1. GET /health -> 200 (cycle 5 00:13:02.996957Z, req 81f0188f; RUN B at t+0.9/40/82/115s)
LOCKS: NONE.
- Route main.rs:842 -> get_health routes/health.rs:22 — ZERO extractors (no State, no Extension), no await points, returns the constant Json {"status":"available"} [audit §1; re-verified health.rs:22-26].
- Middleware: csrf skips GET (auth.rs:930, fn :925) [re-verified]; auth dispatch-exempts GET /health (is_dispatch_exempt auth.rs:549-550 -> next.run :828; auth_middleware fn :822) so the revoked_sessions DashMap :844 is never touched [re-verified]; session_pinning (:170-184) and request_id (:138-164) are header/extension only; telemetry (:1683-1785) takes NO application lock — ZERO .read()/.write()/.lock() calls in all of middleware.rs [re-verified by grep]. The wedged POST holds none of these either; it only bumped requests_in_flight at entry (middleware.rs:1716 per audit).

## 2. /nope -> 404
LOCKS: NONE.
- Router-level: /nope matches no registered route (full table, audit §1) and the main router has NO .fallback — the only .fallback in the crate is GET-scoped inside the /ui/search nest (search_ui.rs:150) [re-verified by grep] -> axum default unmatched-route 404. No handler is entered, so no extractor runs and no lock is taken.
- Scope condition preserved from round-10: "router-level miss" is the AUTHENTICATED branch (the cycle-5 capture; x-request-id present). Unauthenticated /nope 401s in dispatch BEFORE routing (pure string ops; is_admin_path false so the DashMap is never touched) — also lock-free. Both branches: EMPTY.

## 3. POST /indexes/products/search -> 404
LOCKS: NONE.
- No /:index/search route exists on the proxy [audit §4; re-verified: crate-wide grep finds only test-string comments client.rs:646/650, no registration]. The /indexes nest (main.rs:850 -> indexes.rs:304-330 [re-verified]) registers: / (POST+GET), /:index (GET/PATCH/DELETE), /:index/stats, /:index/settings (+ /*subpath), /:index/_preflight, /:index/explain, /:index/documents — "/products/search" matches nothing. The proxy's search route is POST /search/:index (search.rs:128 under the /search nest main.rs:852) — different prefix, cannot match.
- The 404 is produced entirely by axum match machinery: search_handler (fn search.rs:173-174) is never entered, so it never acquires the topology.read at search.rs:667 that the wedged request holds, never awaits session_manager/query_coalescer/result_cache, and issues no node call.

## 4. GET /indexes -> 200 in 259us
LOCKS: NONE IN THE PROXY — plus MECHANISM DRIFT vs this bead's expected claim.
- DRIFT: the expected answer says "served by the NODE process", implying the proxy has no such route. FALSE — GET /indexes IS registered on the proxy (indexes.rs:309, nest main.rs:850) and the proxy handler runs. Round-10 corrected this first; re-verified.

It builds a fresh reqwest::Client per request and awaits ONE outbound GET {first-configured-node}/indexes (503 if no nodes; parse failure degrades to empty results but still 200; transport error 500; non-2xx forwarded). The node produces the index list; the proxy registers, authenticates, and proxies the response. 259us is consistent with a local node round-trip.
- Either way the lock set in the wedged proxy process is EMPTY; node-side locks are a different process and cannot host the proxy park.

## ROUTE-VS-TASK TRAP (explicit)
The /health ROUTE is NOT the health-checker BACKGROUND TASK; their lock sets share nothing.

issue.description:
Auto-split child 1 of 4 of umbrella miroir-72fdd68d (itself the failed grandchild 4 of miroir-5ef5070d). Read-only static verification — change NOTHING in the source; evidence is grep/read output only.

SCOPE: Attribute every lock acquisition reachable in the FIRST TWO middleware layers of grandchild 1's ordered stack (miroir-5ef5070d):
- csrf layer (auth.rs:925): record each lock object, guard kind (read/write), and file:line. State EXPLICITLY that GET/HEAD/OPTIONS requests skip this layer (auth.rs:930-931) and what that means for those methods' reachable lock set.
- auth layer (auth.rs:822): record each lock object, guard kind, and file:line. State EXPLICITLY that the dispatcher exempts GET /health (auth.rs:546, :548-550 -> :828) and what that means for /health's reachable lock set.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- A note on THIS bead (`bead update <id> --notes "..."`) lists the csrf and auth layer lock sets with lock object, guard kind, and file:line.
- The GET/HEAD/OPTIONS skip (:930-931) and the GET /health dispatch exemption (:546/:548-550 -> :828) appear explicitly with coordinates.
- Close only after the note is set; a closed bead with empty notes fails verification.
issue.notes:
Lock attribution, first TWO middleware layers of the ordered stack (csrf outer/runs first, auth second — main.rs:858-861 "Last layer() call = outermost = runs first"; wiring main.rs:885-895 auth then csrf). Evidence: static read of HEAD 10e412d2517de46c7a2757edec38ebe94490ed5b; crates/miroir-proxy/src/auth.rs clean vs HEAD. No source changed.

== Layer 1 — csrf (auth.rs:925 csrf_middleware) ==

Reachable lock set: EXACTLY ONE acquisition.

1. Lock object: RedisTaskStore.pool.manager = Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<ConnectionManager>> (crates/miroir-core/src/task_store/redis.rs:24-25; tokio Mutex import redis.rs:12).
   Guard kind: EXCLUSIVE (tokio Mutex has no read mode).
   Acquisition: manager.lock().await at redis.rs:2404, inside get_admin_session (redis.rs:2397), called from auth.rs:993 (`redis_store.get_admin_session(&session_id)`). Guard is held across the Redis HGETALL network round-trip (redis.rs:2405-2408) and released when get_admin_session returns; get_admin_session runs on a dedicated thread + fresh current_thread runtime via block_on (redis.rs:57-73).
   Reachable only if ALL gates pass: method NOT GET/HEAD/OPTIONS (auth.rs:930-931), admin path /_miroir/ (auth.rs:935 -> is_admin_path :620-622), not dispatch-exempt (auth.rs:940 -> :546), no X-Admin-Key (auth.rs:945 -> check_x_admin_key :784-789), session cookie present AND no bearer (auth.rs:950-956), X-CSRF-Token present (auth.rs:959 -> extract_csrf_token :339-341), redis_store is Some (auth.rs:985-991), and AdminSessionId extension present (auth.rs:971-982 — set by the auth layer, so this lock is only ever reached AFTER the auth layer has already authenticated the cookie). Because the manager Mutex is process-wide (one per RedisTaskStore), a slow Redis round-trip serializes all concurrent admin-session csrf validations that reach this point.

GET/HEAD/OPTIONS SKIP (auth.rs:930-931): `if matches!(method, Method::GET | Method::HEAD | Method::OPTIONS) { return next.run(req).await; }` — explicit: for GET/HEAD/OPTIONS the csrf layer acquires ZERO locks; its reachable lock set is EMPTY. Every later gate (:935-:1029, including the redis.rs:2404 Mutex at auth.rs:993) is unreachable for those methods; the request proceeds straight to the auth layer with nothing held or touched.

Lock-free callees verified in this layer: extract_csrf_token auth.rs:339-341 (header parse), constant_time_csrf_compare auth.rs:344-346 -> constant_time_compare :630-632 (subtle ct_eq), revoked/expiry field checks :1007-1020 (pure reads on the returned row).

== Layer 2 — auth (auth.rs:822 auth_middleware) ==

Reachable lock set: EXACTLY ONE acquisition.

1. Lock object: AuthState.revoked_sessions = Arc<DashMap<String, ()>> (auth.rs:211; dashmap 6.2.1 per Cargo.lock).
   Guard kind: READ — DashMap shards key-space across per-shard RwLocks; contains_key resolves to get(), which takes a read guard on only the single shard owning the key.
   Acquisition: auth.rs:844 `state.revoked_sessions.contains_key(&session_id)`. Synchronous, shard-local, dropped before any await — never held across next.run.
   Reachable only via the admin-session-cookie branch: admin path (auth.rs:839 -> :620-622), cookie present (auth.rs:840 -> extract_admin_session_cookie :802-811), unseal succeeds (auth.rs:841-842 -> unseal_admin_cookie :814-819 -> admin_session::unseal_session, admin_session.rs:190-193 — XChaCha20-Poly1305, zero locks; grep for Mutex/RwLock/lock() in admin_session.rs: none).

GET /health DISPATCH EXEMPTION (auth.rs:546; :548-550 -> :828): is_dispatch_exempt (:546) returns true for (GET, "/health") at :548-550, so auth_middleware hits `if is_dispatch_exempt(&method, &path) { return next.run(req).await; }` at :827-828 — explicit: for GET /health the auth layer acquires ZERO locks; its reachable lock set is EMPTY. The DashMap read at :844 and dispatch_bearer at :873 are unreachable. is_dispatch_exempt itself (:546-594) is pure string matching — no locks. (Same empty-set reasoning applies to every other dispatch-exempt entry at :552-583: GET /version, GET /_miroir/ready, GET /_miroir/ui/search/locale/*, POST /_miroir/admin/login, GET /_miroir/ui/search/{idx}/session, GET /ui/search/{idx}.) Consequence for the probe path: the /health liveness/readiness check bypasses BOTH layers' locks — csrf by method skip (:930-931), auth by dispatch exemption (:548-550 -> :828) — so /health cannot wedge on either.

== (1) Search-serving routes at the current tree (file:line) ==

- POST /_miroir/indexes/{index}/explain — admin.rs:74, via main.rs:849 nest. Same explain handler. Rule 3 match (auth.rs:768-771, if at 769) -> Authenticated(MasterKey) -> next.run() -> router resolves -> no route matches -> axum default unmatched-route 404. Confirmed NO .fallback() on the main router: single Router::new() at main.rs:841 through .with_state() at main.rs:896, no .fallback(), no .merge(). Crate-wide grep for .fallback( in crates/*/src returns exactly one hit: search_ui.rs:150 `.fallback(axum::routing::get(serve_spa))` — GET-scoped, inside the /ui/search nest (main.rs:856), cannot affect /nope.

Unauthenticated branch: no bearer -> dispatch Rule 4 (auth.rs:735) -> InvalidAuth -> auth_middleware returns MeilisearchError::new(MiroirCode::InvalidAuth, "The provided authorization is invalid.") (auth.rs:903-906) WITHOUT calling next.run() — router never consulted. Status: MiroirCode::InvalidAuth -> 401 (test-pinned api_error.rs:533; ApiError::http_status 401 arm at line 137).

LOCK SET in the WEDGED PROXY process (the process whose POST /search/products wedges holding the read guard acquired at search.rs:667): EMPTY / LOCKS NONE on BOTH branches. No handler executes (router-miss 404, or 401 pre-routing), and the middleware itself acquires no coordination lock: dispatch_bearer operates on &AuthState via constant-time compare (no async lock); revoked_sessions is consulted only for admin paths. The 404/401 neither waits on nor extends the topology.read guard the wedged request holds — it completes independently of the wedge.

Scope condition: same as row 1 — 404 holds for the authenticated branch; unauthenticated gets 401 first.

- "/:index" GET/PATCH/DELETE (310-315) — single segment, cannot match the two-segment /products/search remainder

- "/:index/settings" GET/PATCH/POST (317-322)
- "/:index/settings/*subpath" GET/PATCH (323-326)
- "/:index/_preflight" POST (327)
- "/:index/explain" POST (328)
- nest "/:index/documents" (329) -> documents.rs:143-151: "/" POST/PUT/DELETE, "/:id" DELETE
Second-segment literals under /indexes/: {stats, settings, _preflight, explain, documents}. "search" matches none.

Crate-wide grep (not assertion): every .route( registration containing "search" in crates/*/src = search.rs:128 (POST /:index under the /search nest, main.rs:852 -> full path POST /search/:index — different prefix), multi_search.rs:706 (POST /multi-search, top-level main.rs:845-848), search_ui.rs:144-149 (session/config/beacon/static under /ui/search), indexes.rs:328 (explain), admin.rs:74 (/_miroir/indexes/{index}/explain). No `/:index/search` route exists in any crate. Wildcard sweep: the only wildcard routes are /settings/*path (any, under the /settings nest — different prefix), /ui/search/static/*path (GET), /_miroir/admin/*path (GET), /indexes/:index/settings/*subpath (GET/PATCH). None can match POST /indexes/products/search. metrics_router (middleware.rs:1788, GET /metrics only) is a separate router not merged into app (main.rs:917). No other Router::new in main.rs.

Corroborating nuance: the AUTH layer anticipates this exact path shape — action_for_method_path (auth.rs:643-652) maps POST /indexes/{idx}/search -> "search" scope action, and dispatch_bearer with a products-scoped search JWT on that path returns Authenticated (test auth.rs:2156-2172). PER-ASSERT VERDICTS (line numbers at HEAD 7401f22, re-derived independently of the parent's read-through):
- status is_success x3 L973-975 and x3 L1042-1044: live HTTP statuses on responses the test itself issued — fire on proxy/node failure.
- misses_after_third == misses_before + 3 L989-993: the collision detector. Baselines are runtime reads; a key collision makes query2/3 hits and the delta falls short (+1). Unwired metric cannot pass: proxy_counter's absent-series fallback is Ok(0) (documented L449), so both reads read 0 and 0 == 0+3 fires. Lookup-Err fail-open (search.rs records neither counter) also trips it. Not vacuous.
- scatter_after_third == scatter_before + 3 L1001-1005: fan-out exactly once per query; retry doubles it, short-circuit flattens it, unwired reads 0==3. Not vacuous.
- assert_ne row pairs L1011-1012: deliberate row-level pins ('laptop'/'desk'/'chair' over docs Laptop/Desk/Chair return distinct hit arrays); compared Values come from separate responses, not self-equality. Their shadowing (a collision serving equal rows) is stated in the L1007-1010 comment per the 3ca59fe convention and is covered by the misses delta.
- round-trip assert_eq x3 L1054-1056: two independently parsed bodies per pair; catch a repeat served from a foreign entry. Not self-equality.
- hits_after == hits_before + 3 L1065-1069: any repeat leaking past cache (never stored, evicted, host stall past the 500 ms ttl_ms — hits never refresh an entry, result_cache.rs) reads as a miss and the delta falls short. TTL comment present L1058-1061.
- scatter_after_repeats == scatter_after_third L1077-1080: two distinct reads of a monotonic counter; the first is pinned at baseline+3 by L1001, so this is not 0==0 — a hit that still scatters increments between the reads and fires. Closes the test.

issue.description:
## Phase 10 Epic — Security + Secrets

Ships the plan §9 secret-handling contract: inventory, Model B key separation, zero-downtime rotations, JWT dual-secret overlap, CSRF posture, `miroir-ctl` credential loading. Integrates with ESO + OpenBao on the cluster.

## Why A Separate Phase

Secrets-related code lives inside Phase 2 (auth handlers), Phase 5 (JWT, scoped keys), Phase 6 (Redis password), Phase 8 (K8s Secret templates). But the *policies* — key relationships, rotation procedures, CSRF rules — have to be owned in one place because they cross-cut every layer. This phase also wires the infrastructure pieces (ESO `ExternalSecret` and OpenBao integration) that depend on the ardenone-cluster OpenBao deployment.

## Scope (plan §9)

**Secret inventory — 9 entries**
- `master_key` (client-facing)
- `node_master_key` (Miroir → Meilisearch admin-scoped key)
- `meilisearch_master_key` (per-node startup master key — fixed at process start)
- `admin_api_key` (operators + miroir-ctl)
- `ADMIN_SESSION_SEAL_KEY` (64-byte; seals Admin UI cookies via HMAC-SHA256 + XChaCha20-Poly1305; must be shared across multi-pod)
- `SEARCH_UI_JWT_SECRET` (signs end-user JWTs; plus `SEARCH_UI_JWT_SECRET_PREVIOUS` during rotation)
- `search_ui_shared_key` (only when `search_ui.auth.mode: shared_key`)
- `ghcr_credentials` (Kaniko push)
- `github_token` (gh CLI for Releases)
- `redis_password` (optional)

**Key relationship models**
- Model A — shared master everywhere (dev/simple)
- Model B — separated: clients use `master_key`; Miroir re-signs to `node_master_key` (recommended prod)

**Rotations (zero-downtime where possible)**
- `nodeMasterKey` (admin-scoped child of Meilisearch startup master): `POST /keys` new → update Secret → rolling restart → `DELETE /keys/{old_uid}`
- Startup `MEILI_MASTER_KEY` is **not** zero-downtime (fixed at process start) — documented separately
- `SEARCH_UI_JWT_SECRET` dual-secret overlap: primary + `_PREVIOUS`; 5-step rotation; recommended quarterly, on-leak-immediately shorten overlap; optional CronJob driving `miroir-ctl ui rotate-jwt-secret`
- Search UI scoped Meilisearch key rotation (§13.21) — leader-coordinated with Redis hash, per-pod observation beacon, 120s drain before revocation

**CSRF posture**
- Admin UI: secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookies; `X-CSRF-Token` double-submit on state-changing requests
- Bearer tokens and `X-Admin-Key` bypass CSRF (can't be set by cross-origin HTML)
- Origin checks: `admin_ui.allowed_origins` (default same-origin), `search_ui.allowed_origins`
- SPA static GETs are CSRF-free

**K8s Secret templates** (plan §9) — `miroir-secrets`, `meilisearch-secrets`, separate as needed

**ESO ExternalSecret** (plan §6) — pulls from `kv/search/miroir` in OpenBao via `openbao-backend` ClusterSecretStore

**miroir-ctl credential loading**
- Priority: `MIROIR_ADMIN_API_KEY` env → `~/.config/miroir/credentials` TOML → `--admin-key` flag (flagged as script-unsafe)

**Not handled (documented explicitly)** — tenant JWT tokens (forwarded to nodes as-is), per-index key scoping (forwarded unchanged), key creation API (broadcast)

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Every secret in the inventory has a Helm `values.yaml` hook + ESO `ExternalSecret` path or documented manual-only exception
- [ ] Node-key rotation rehearsed end-to-end on a staging cluster within a single maintenance window without client impact
- [ ] JWT rotation CronJob shipped with the chart at `suspend: true`; `miroir-ctl ui rotate-jwt-secret` sequences all 5 steps
- [ ] Scoped-key rotation drain-and-revoke sequence tested against a 3-pod deployment with artificial pod-loss mid-rotation
- [ ] Admin UI login → logout → revoked-cookie replay returns 401 across every pod (propagated via `miroir:admin_session:revoked` Pub/Sub)
- [ ] CSP + CORS templates rejected when `csp_overrides.*` contains a wildcard that is not additive
- [ ] OpenBao store policy scoped to least-privilege for the miroir role

## What

Document + wire the plan §9 secret inventory (9 entries):

| Secret | Consumer | Rotation |
|--------|----------|----------|
| `master_key` | Miroir proxy | manual/infrequent |
| `node_master_key` | Miroir → Meilisearch | admin-scoped child key rotation flow (P10.2) |
| `meilisearch_master_key` | Meilisearch startup | planned-maintenance (process restart) |
| `admin_api_key` | Operators, `miroir-ctl` | rotate alongside `ADMIN_SESSION_SEAL_KEY` |
| `ADMIN_SESSION_SEAL_KEY` | Miroir proxy | P10.4 |
| `SEARCH_UI_JWT_SECRET` | Miroir proxy | P10.3 dual-secret overlap |
| `search_ui_shared_key` | Miroir + host apps | only in `shared_key` mode |
| `ghcr_credentials` | Kaniko (iad-ci) | infrastructure; not in scope for Miroir |
| `github_token` | gh CLI (iad-ci) | infrastructure; not in scope |
| `redis_password` | Miroir proxy | optional |

Ship `examples/eso-external-secret.yaml` (plan §6) pointing at the `openbao-backend` ClusterSecretStore.

## Why

Plan §1 principle 6 + §9: "All secrets are read from environment variables in production — never baked into config files or images." The inventory makes it explicit what each secret does and how often to rotate; ESO wiring means secrets deploy declaratively with the rest of the stack.

## Details

**ESO keys layout** in OpenBao at `kv/search/miroir`:
```
master_key
node_master_key
admin_api_key
admin_session_seal_key
search_ui_jwt_secret
search_ui_jwt_secret_previous       # only during rotation
search_ui_shared_key                # only in shared_key mode
redis_password                      # only if redis_auth_enabled
```

**Startup env loading**: `miroir-proxy` reads each env var exactly once at startup. A missing critical secret (`SEARCH_UI_JWT_SECRET` when `search_ui.enabled: true`) must refuse to start with a clear error (plan §9 "orchestrator refuses to start the search UI without it").

**Not handled in Miroir** (plan §9):
- Tenant JWT tokens — forwarded to nodes as-is
- Per-index API key scoping — forwarded unchanged
- Key creation API — broadcast; requires all nodes available

## Acceptance

- [ ] ESO ExternalSecret deploys cleanly against ardenone-cluster's OpenBao
- [ ] Missing `SEARCH_UI_JWT_SECRET` with `search_ui.enabled: true` → refuse-to-start with explicit error
- [ ] `examples/eso-external-secret.yaml` documents every key in the inventory

issue.description:
## What

Implement the plan §9 "Rotation flow for the admin-scoped `nodeMasterKey` (zero-downtime)":
1. On each Meilisearch node, generate a new admin-scoped key via `POST /keys` (actions `["*"]`, indexes `["*"]`, optional expiration). Old + new coexist.
2. Update ESO source / K8s Secret `miroir-secrets.nodeMasterKey` with the new key value.
3. Rolling-restart Miroir pods so each pod picks up the new key. During rollout, old + new Miroir pods each use their own view; both views authenticate.
4. Once all Miroir pods on new key, `DELETE /keys/{old_key_uid}` on every node.

## Why

Plan §9 is explicit: Meilisearch CE has **one startup master key** per process, fixed for the life of the process. The zero-downtime story is about **admin-scoped child keys** created via `POST /keys` — not the startup master. Clarifying this is the #1 source of confusion.

## Details

**Terminology clarification** (plan §9):
- `MEILI_MASTER_KEY` (startup env var) — fixed at process start. Rotation REQUIRES process restart.
- Admin-scoped child keys (via `POST /keys` with `actions: ["*"]`) — multiple can exist simultaneously. Rotation is zero-downtime.

The "`nodeMasterKey`" in Miroir config is actually the second kind.

**CLI support**: `miroir-ctl key rotate-node-master` sequences the 4 steps above via admin API + ESO secret update (best-effort; operators may prefer manual steps when deploying via ArgoCD).

**Startup master rotation** (NOT zero-downtime, plan §9): update K8s Secret → rolling restart each Meilisearch StatefulSet pod → recreate admin-scoped child keys against the new master → then run the zero-downtime flow to rotate `nodeMasterKey`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] On a staging cluster, execute the 4-step rotation end-to-end without client impact — measure with continuous write + search traffic
- [ ] Mid-rotation a pod restart does NOT fail because one pod is on old key, another on new (both valid concurrently)
- [ ] `miroir-ctl key rotate-node-master --dry-run` prints the plan without executing
- [ ] Startup-master rotation documented as a separate runbook with a maintenance window
issue.title: P10.2 node_master_key zero-downtime rotation flow

issue.description:
## What

Implement the plan §9 "JWT signing-secret rotation" flow:
- **Primary**: `SEARCH_UI_JWT_SECRET` env var (required when `search_ui.enabled: true`)
- **Optional rollover**: `SEARCH_UI_JWT_SECRET_PREVIOUS` env var, present only during rotation window
- **Signing**: new tokens always signed with primary; `kid` header identifies secret
- **Validation**: accept EITHER primary OR previous; accept if either HMAC verifies
- **Steady state**: only primary is loaded

5-step rotation procedure (plan §9):
1. Generate new 64-byte random secret
2. Set `SEARCH_UI_JWT_SECRET_PREVIOUS = current primary`, `SEARCH_UI_JWT_SECRET = new`
3. Rolling restart — both active; new tokens sign with new, old tokens verify via previous
4. Wait `session_ttl_s + buffer` (default 15 min + 5 min = 20 min)
5. Remove `SEARCH_UI_JWT_SECRET_PREVIOUS` and rolling restart

CronJob + `miroir-ctl ui rotate-jwt-secret` automate end-to-end.

## Why

Plan §9: "tokens are short-lived (default `session_ttl_s: 900`, i.e. 15 min) but still long enough to straddle a rollout, Miroir supports a dual-secret overlap window so rotation is zero-downtime."

## Details

**Leak response**: set `SEARCH_UI_JWT_SECRET_PREVIOUS` to empty string + redeploy → old tokens become invalid immediately at the cost of already-issued-but-valid session tokens being rejected.

**Cadence**: recommended once per 90 days (configurable via CronJob schedule); suspend default = true (operators opt-in to automation).

**`miroir-ctl ui rotate-jwt-secret`** sequences:
1. Generate new secret via `openssl rand -base64 64` (called inline)
2. Write via the configured secret backend (ESO ExternalSecret writable mode, or Sealed Secrets, or manual K8s Secret patch)
3. Trigger first rolling restart via `kubectl rollout restart deployment/miroir`
4. Wait
5. Clear `SEARCH_UI_JWT_SECRET_PREVIOUS`
6. Trigger second rolling restart

**CronJob** manifest shipped in chart:
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: miroir-rotate-jwt
spec:
  suspend: true                # operators opt-in
  schedule: "0 3 1 */3 *"      # 03:00 first-of-quarter
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
            - name: miroir-ctl
              image: ghcr.io/jedarden/miroir:latest
              command: [miroir-ctl, ui, rotate-jwt-secret]
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] Rotation end-to-end on 2-pod staging: tokens minted pre-rotation still validate post-rotation until step 5
- [ ] Leak-response: clearing PREVIOUS invalidates old tokens within one redeploy cycle
- [ ] CronJob schedule (suspended by default) renders correctly in Helm output
issue.title: P10.3 SEARCH_UI_JWT_SECRET dual-secret overlap rotation

Startup generates random key with warning if env var unset. Metric miroir_admin_session_key_generated tracks this. Test compilation fixed in 1ea0597.
issue.description:
## What

Implement plan §9 admin session cookie sealing:
- **Key**: `ADMIN_SESSION_SEAL_KEY` — 64 bytes, env var loaded at pod startup
- **Sealing**: HMAC-SHA256 for integrity + XChaCha20-Poly1305 for confidentiality of the session ID
- **Fallback on missing**: Miroir generates a random key at startup AND logs a warning; multi-pod deployments MUST set the same value across all pods, otherwise cookies sealed on one pod fail verification on others and users are logged out on every request hitting a different pod
- **Cookie format**: `Set-Cookie: miroir_admin_session=<sealed>; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict`

## Why

Plan §9 + §13.19 + §4 admin_sessions: the admin session cookie must be unforgeable (HMAC) and its content must not leak via browser inspection (encrypted). Without both, a compromised browser or middlebox could reconstruct a session ID and impersonate the admin.

## Details

**Crate choice**: `ring` or `ring-compat` + `chacha20poly1305` + `hmac` + `subtle` (constant-time compare). Avoid pure-JS-style "sign, then encrypt" anti-patterns — use an AEAD primitive that provides both at once.

**Cookie structure** (decoded):
```
[12-byte nonce][sealed_session_id_ciphertext][16-byte tag]
```

**Key loading**: if env unset, generate `ring::rand::SystemRandom` 64 bytes + log a warning "generated random ADMIN_SESSION_SEAL_KEY; multi-pod deployments must set this manually to a shared value." Record a metric `miroir_admin_session_key_generated` that alerts if > 0 in HA deployments.

**Logout propagation** (plan §4 admin_sessions + §13.19): cookie stores session ID; `admin_sessions.revoked` flipped on logout; every pod re-checks `revoked` on each cookie-auth'd request; Redis Pub/Sub `miroir:admin_session:revoked` notifies in-memory caches.

**Rotation**: because cookies are short-lived (TTL `admin_ui.session_ttl_s`, default 1h), rotating this key is **not** zero-downtime — sessions sealed under old key fail verification when the new key is deployed. Rotate alongside `admin_api_key` during scheduled maintenance (or during a "log everyone out" moment).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Cookie tampering (modify any byte) → verification fails; request returns 401
- [ ] Cookie issued on pod-A verifies on pod-B when `ADMIN_SESSION_SEAL_KEY` shared; fails with ERROR log when keys differ (HA bug)
- [ ] Logout: `miroir_admin_session_revoked_total` metric ticks; subsequent cookie replay → 401
- [ ] Startup with unset env var generates key + logs warning + sets `miroir_admin_session_key_generated` gauge to 1
issue.title: P10.4 ADMIN_SESSION_SEAL_KEY: HMAC + XChaCha20-Poly1305 cookie sealing

issue.close_reason: Scoped Meilisearch key rotation implemented in commits ee3ef23, 8e39c6c, and 76f1cd1. Leader-lease coordination with per-index beacon tracking. Redis hash stores primary_uid/previous_uid/generation. Schema validation in Helm values.schema.json rejects rotate_before_expiry_days >= max_age_days. Test compilation fixed in 1ea0597.
issue.description:
## What

Implement the search UI scoped-key rotation from plan §13.21 "Scoped-key rotation coordination":
- Redis hash `miroir:search_ui_scoped_key:<index>` with fields `{primary_uid, previous_uid, rotated_at, generation}`
- Leader-lease `search_ui_key_rotation:<index>` (Mode B, §14.5)
- Per-pod beacon `miroir:search_ui_scoped_key_observed:<pod>:<index>` {generation, observed_at} with 60s EXPIRE, refreshed on every use
- Revocation safety gate: leader enumerates live peers (from peer-discovery channel), checks every live peer has reported the new generation before `DELETE /keys/{previous_uid}`
- Drain wait: `scoped_key_rotation_drain_s` (default 120s) for stragglers

Automatic trigger: `scoped_key_rotate_before_expiry_days` (default 30d) before `scoped_key_max_age_days` (default 60d).
Manual trigger: `POST /_miroir/ui/search/{index}/rotate-scoped-key` admin-gated; `force: true` bypasses timing gate.

## Why

Plan §13.21: "Rotation is a multi-pod handoff that must never revoke the old key while any peer is still serving requests against it." A premature revoke causes every in-flight search from old-key-holding peers to 403.

## Details

**Schema validation** (plan §13.21 "Config validation"): `values.schema.json` rejects `scoped_key_rotate_before_expiry_days >= scoped_key_max_age_days` at install time — would cause continuous rotation loop.

**Config values**:
```yaml
search_ui:
  scoped_key_max_age_days: 60
  scoped_key_rotate_before_expiry_days: 30
  scoped_key_rotation_drain_s: 120
```

**Rotation sequence** (leader):
1. Mint new scoped Meilisearch key via admin-level `POST /keys` (actions `["search"]`, indexes scoped to UID)
2. Write `miroir:search_ui_scoped_key:<index>` with `primary_uid=<new>, previous_uid=<old>, generation++`
3. All pods: on next request, read hash → substitute `primary_uid`; fallback to `previous_uid` if hash not yet in cache
4. All pods: write beacon with new `generation` every time they use primary_uid
5. Leader: check beacons; all live peers report new generation?
6. If yes after `scoped_key_rotation_drain_s`: `DELETE /keys/{previous_uid}`; set `previous_uid = null`
7. If no: retry on next tick

**Missing peer tolerance**: a pod that disappears (restart) is tolerated — its next startup reads the hash fresh, skipping old UID entirely.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Rotation on 3-pod deployment: zero 403 responses during the overlap window
- [ ] Kill one pod mid-rotation: leader waits `scoped_key_rotation_drain_s`, then retries; revocation eventually completes
- [ ] `force: true` manual rotation: old key revoked within minutes regardless of timing gate
- [ ] Schema rejection: `rotate_before_expiry_days: 90, max_age_days: 60` → helm lint fails with clear error
issue.title: P10.5 Scoped Meilisearch key rotation (§13.21 coordination)

issue.close_reason: Implemented P10.6 CSRF posture acceptance tests (§9). All 20 tests pass, validating: cookie-auth CSRF enforcement (missing/mismatch tokens), bearer/X-Admin-Key bypass, origin validation, CSP header merging, wildcard rejection, middleware exemption logic, session cookie extraction, and cross-pod seal verification. Commit 3a61c94 adds crates/miroir-proxy/tests/p10_6_csrf_posture.rs with comprehensive coverage.
issue.description: ## What Implement plan §9 "CSRF posture": **Admin UI sessions** (cookie-auth): - Secure, HttpOnly, `SameSite=Strict` cookies (issued by admin login form) - Separate CSRF token double-submitted via `X-CSRF-Token` header on state-changing requests (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) - Token rotated on each login, bound to the session cookie - Mismatch → 403 **Bearer tokens** and **`X-Admin-Key`** bypass CSRF checks (cannot be set by cross-origin forms / `` tags; non-simple header forces CORS preflight). **Origin checks**: - Admin UI enforces `admin_ui.allowed_origins` (default `same-origin`) on session endpoint + cookie-auth mutations - Search UI session endpoint enforces `search_ui.allowed_origins` (default `["*"]` in `public` mode, empty otherwise) - Mismatched `Origin` → 403 before any auth check **CSP**: default Search UI `default-src 'self'; img-src 'self' https:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'`. `csp_overrides.*` merged into the corresponding directives at render time; additive only, never permissive replacement of base template. ## Why Plan §9: "Admin UI and the search UI session endpoint both have browser-initiated paths to state-changing requests, so CSRF must be addressed explicitly." These two pages are the only browser-facing ones; everything else is API-only. ## Details **CSRF token**: - Generated at login; stored alongside session cookie value - Transmitted to JS via response body at `POST /_miroir/admin/login` - JS stores in memory (not localStorage — XSS risk) - Sent on every state-changing request as `X-CSRF-Token` - Server-side: validate against session's bound token **Admin UI SPA code**: CSRF enforcement is applied per endpoint handler; a middleware would be simpler but overly broad (would falsely block Bearer-authenticated requests). **Base CSP template** for Admin UI (stricter than search UI): ``` default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; connect-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none' ``` **`cors_allowed_origins`** separate from `allowed_origins` — different RFC semantics (CORS `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` vs. Origin-header enforcement on the session endpoint). ## Acceptance - [ ] Cookie-auth POST without `X-CSRF-Token` → 403 `missing_csrf` - [ ] Cookie-auth POST with wrong token → 403 `csrf_mismatch` - [ ] Bearer-auth POST without `X-CSRF-Token` → 200 (bearer bypasses CSRF) - [ ] Session endpoint with Origin not in allowed_origins → 403 before credential check - [ ] `csp_overrides.script_src: ['https://cdn.example.com']` merges into `script-src 'self' https://cdn.example.com` - [ ] Wildcard (`*`) in csp_overrides rejected by config validation
issue.title: P10.6 CSRF posture: Admin UI + search UI origin + CSP checks

issue.close_reason: Implemented P10.7 admin login rate limiting acceptance tests (plan §9). The rate limiting functionality was already implemented in session.rs and redis.rs. Added comprehensive acceptance tests covering: rate limit (10/minute), exponential backoff (10m → 20m → 40m → ... up to 24h cap), successful login reset, multi-pod shared state via Redis, and Helm schema constraint validation. Tests require Docker for Redis testcontainers. Commit: 6f1abee
issue.description:
## What

Plan §4 admin login endpoint (`POST /_miroir/admin/login`):
- Rate limit: 10/minute per source IP, backed by `miroir:ratelimit:adminlogin:<ip>` in Redis when `miroir.replicas > 1`
- Failed-login exponential backoff: after 5 consecutive failed attempts from the same IP, backoff window doubles per attempt (10m, 20m, 40m, ...) up to 24h cap
- Tracked in `miroir:ratelimit:adminlogin:backoff:<ip>` hash `{failed_count, next_allowed_at}`
- Successful login resets both counters

## Why

Plan §4 + §9: "HA deployments must use shared state for the rate limiter because otherwise per-pod buckets let attackers evade the limit by round-robin'ing across pods." Helm `values.schema.json` rejects local-only admin-login rate-limiting in HA.

## Details

**Helm schema constraint** (§P3.5 cross-reference): multi-replica deploys must use Redis backend.

**Failed counter increment on**: wrong `admin_key`, expired cookie, revoked session (not just "auth failure" vaguely).

**Successful login reset**: clears both `miroir:ratelimit:adminlogin:<ip>` AND `miroir:ratelimit:adminlogin:backoff:<ip>`.

**Integration with P2.7 auth dispatch**: the `/_miroir/admin/login` endpoint is dispatch-exempt (plan §5 rule 5) — the handler does its own rate-limit check before any other credential comparison.

**Config**:
```yaml
admin_ui:
  rate_limit:
    per_ip: "10/minute"
    failed_attempt_threshold: 5
    backoff_start_minutes: 10
    backoff_max_hours: 24
    backend: redis       # redis | local (schema rejects local when replicas > 1)
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] 11 login attempts in 60s from same IP → 11th returns 429
- [ ] 5 failed attempts → next attempt blocked for 10m; next attempt after that (also failed) blocked for 20m, etc.
- [ ] Successful login resets counters
- [ ] 2-pod deployment with `backend: redis`: attempts against pod-A count against the same bucket as attempts against pod-B
- [ ] Helm lint rejects `backend: local` with replicas > 1
issue.title: P10.7 Admin login rate limiting + exponential backoff

2. Determine which methods meilisearch v1.8.3 accepts on /indexes/{uid}/settings. Meilisearch replaced PUT with PATCH on settings routes around v1.8 - check the v1.8 changelog/source, and empirically if cheap: curl -X PUT and -X PATCH the settings route on a spawned v1.8.3 node and record both status codes.
3. Verdict: is the 405 a plain harness bug (set_node_settings must use PATCH for v1.8.3), or does something else explain it?

issue.notes:
VERDICT: RULED IN - plain harness bug. Fix is PUT -> PATCH at crates/miroir-proxy/tests/p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs:405 (set_node_settings, .put(...) -> .patch(...)).

1) Container tag CONFIRMED v1.8.3. Vendored source ~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/testcontainers-modules-0.11.6/src/meilisearch/mod.rs:9-10 pins NAME="getmeili/meilisearch", TAG="v1.8.3"; Cargo.lock pins testcontainers-modules 0.11.6 (checksum 4d43ed4e8f58424c3a2c6c56dbea6643c3c23e8666a34df13c54f0a184e6c707). The test calls Meilisearch::default().with_master_key(...) with NO with_tag override (test file lines 272-274), so the spawned tag is the module default. Empirically a spawned node's GET /version returns {"pkgVersion":"1.8.3","commitSha":"7d699532676b6ad3a692130fe721c88565cf7bc3"} - and the v1.8.3 git tag on meilisearch/meilisearch points to exactly that commit. Child-2's standing topology (p13diag-1ec135a1-meili{,2,3} on 17831-17833) also runs getmeili/meilisearch:v1.8.3 at the same commitSha, so it can be reused for verification.

2) Methods accepted by v1.8.3 on /indexes/{uid}/settings: PATCH (update), GET (read), DELETE (reset). Source (meilisearch/src/routes/indexes/settings.rs @ tag v1.8.3, generate_configure! macro, lines 651-653): 'web::resource("").route(web::patch().to(SeqHandler(update_all))).route(web::get().to(SeqHandler(get_all))).route(web::delete().to(SeqHandler(delete_all)))' - no web::put(). Empirical curl on a spawned v1.8.3 node: PUT /indexes/probe/settings -> 405 Method Not Allowed with response header 'allow: PATCH, GET, DELETE'; PATCH same route -> 202 Accepted with a settingsUpdate task. Reproduced identically on the standing child-2 topology node (17831): PUT -> 405 (allow: PATCH, GET, DELETE), PATCH -> 202. This exactly matches signature B ("Failed to update settings on http://localhost:33107: 405 Method Not Allowed"), which is the test's own bail at line 412 on the direct-to-node request (index management bypasses the proxy per the comment at lines 399-400). The PUT->PATCH swap happened in v1.8.0; the v1.8.0 release notes' settings example uses '-X PATCH http://localhost:7700/indexes/movies/settings'.

Nuance for the fixer: only the AGGREGATE settings route is PATCH-only in v1.8.3; the per-setting sub-routes (e.g. /settings/search-cutoff-ms via make_setting_route!) still take PUT on this version - irrelevant to acceptance_10, which fails on the aggregate route.

issue.description:
Child 1 of the miroir-77a3dce4 umbrella split. Produces the counter mapping every later sweep child reasons from.

SCOPE: In crates/miroir-proxy (src/routes/search.rs + tests/p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs), record on this bead: the three test-visible counters (miroir_result_cache_hits_total, miroir_result_cache_misses_total, miroir_scatter_fan_out_size_count) - where each increments in search.rs, the hit-path short-circuit that returns the cached response BEFORE both record_scatter_fan_out call sites, the fail-open paths (a cache lookup error records neither counter; the proxy_counter Ok(0) fallback for a dead metrics endpoint turns a dead series into a failed delta, never a silent pass), and ttl_ms behavior (the entry is written on the miss and hits never refresh it).

NOTE: the parent bead's consolidated note cites line numbers that read roughly 14 lines low against the current working tree - re-anchor every citation before recording.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Mapping recorded on this bead with search.rs anchors re-verified against the current tree.
- Each counter states its increment condition AND the regressions that would leave it flat, so a later sweep child can tell a live delta from a dead one.
- This is a mapping-only child: no test-file edits expected. If an edit proves necessary, stop and record why on the bead instead.
issue.notes:
COUNTER MAPPING (miroir-4d614d5b, 2026-09-11) — every anchor below re-verified against the CURRENT working tree, which carries the umbrella's uncommitted landing changes to both files. Anchor status vs the parent's consolidated note (miroir-77a3dce4): the search.rs citations there are EXACT against the current tree (522 / 556 / 561 / 567 / 573-576 / 811 / 941-944 / 1406 all confirmed verbatim); the p13_13 TEST-file citations read uniformly +14 low — the working tree added exactly 14 lines above the proxy_counter doc (module-doc port-binding note +7, PROXY_METRICS_PORT doc +4, config-yaml doc +2, `cdc.overflow: drop` line +1), so current line = parent line + 14 for every test citation. All anchors below are current-tree.

== THE THREE COUNTERS ==

1) miroir_result_cache_hits_total — Counter (middleware.rs:620-624, "Total number of result cache hits"), incremented by Metrics::inc_result_cache_hits (middleware.rs:1848-1850).
   Increment site: search.rs:522 — inside the cache-lookup block's Ok(Some(cached_bytes)) arm, and only in the inner Ok(response_body) arm. Full increment condition: result_cache.enabled AND resolved_targets.len() == 1 (both :491) AND canonicalized query non-empty (:507) AND get() returned Some (:516) AND the cached bytes deserialize as JSON (:519). The increment precedes the cached response build/return at :556.
   Regressions that leave it FLAT:
   - result_cache disabled, multi-target alias, or canonicalization failure (:496-505 stores an empty string; :507 skips the whole block) — lookup never runs.
   - Entry not stored / stored under a different key: the store at :941-944 reuses result_cache_key captured at :514, so any key-recomputation regression turns the repeat into a miss (misses +1, hits flat).
   - TTL expiry past ttl_ms: core pops the entry and returns Ok(None) → miss (:567), hits flat.
   - Cached bytes fail JSON deser: :558-562 records a MISS instead (hits flat, misses +1, request re-fans out).
   - Metric unwired/renamed/unregistered: absent series → proxy_counter Ok(0) → `hits_after == hits_before + 1` fails (0 == 1). Delta fails loudly, never silently passes.

2) miroir_result_cache_misses_total — Counter (middleware.rs:626-630), incremented by Metrics::inc_result_cache_misses (middleware.rs:1852-1854).
   Increment sites: TWO in search.rs. :561 — Ok(Some) but cached bytes fail to deserialize ("treat as cache miss"); :567 — Ok(None), the genuine miss, which INCLUDES TTL-expired entries (core pops them and returns None, result_cache.rs:141-147). Nuance: the core's internal hits/misses counters (result_cache.rs) are a separate non-Prometheus stat and do NOT count the deser-failure path — the Prometheus series is route-level.
   Regressions that leave it FLAT: the same three lookup gates as above; the query wrongly served as a hit (movement shifts to hits_total — acceptance_2's miss delta :624-631 fails while its hits delta moves); a coalesced serve returning at search.rs:465 (coalescing short-circuits BEFORE the cache lookup and records NONE of the three counters — the acceptance tests are immune only because their queries are strictly sequential and the prior registration is unregistered at :1003).
   Keying nuance for sweep children: acceptance_2 reads the miss delta after ONLY the first query (:624; the repeat comes at :642), so a store-key mismatch does NOT show there — query 1 was a genuine miss. It surfaces as the repeat being a SECOND miss: misses would read +2 with no assert on it, and the hits delta at :656-663 fails.

3) miroir_scatter_fan_out_size_count — the Prometheus _count series of Histogram "miroir_scatter_fan_out_size" (middleware.rs:598-605, buckets [1,2,3,5,10,20,50]), recorded via Metrics::record_scatter_fan_out → observe(node_count) (middleware.rs:1834-1836). proxy_counter matches the _count token as a whole exposition token, so it cannot collide with the same histogram's _bucket/_sum lines or # HELP/# TYPE metadata (test :426-428; parent cited :412-420).
   Call sites: search.rs:811 (single-target search_handler; node_count = plan.shard_to_node.len() at :808, recorded immediately after planning and BEFORE dfs execution at :901) and search.rs:1406 (search_multi_targets; node_count at :1403, reached only via the multi-target dispatch at :603). Aliases default ENABLED (miroir-core config.rs:621), but a plain index resolves to itself (search.rs:251-264), so resolved_targets.len() == 1 for the acceptance tests — only :811 is live for them.
   Semantics: _count moves by exactly 1 per planned fan-out; node_count itself lands in _sum/_buckets. `scatter_before + 1` pins "exactly one fan-out observation", not "one node". Ordering nuance: the record precedes dfs_query_then_fetch_search, so a scatter that subsequently FAILS still moved _count — a fan-out delta alone does not prove a successful scatter (the tests assert HTTP success separately).
   Regressions that leave it FLAT: the hit short-circuit — BY DESIGN (acceptance_1's bypass assert :554-560 REQUIRES it flat on a served hit); early returns upstream of :811 — invalid unavailable_shard_policy 500 (:694-698), version-floor no-covering-set 503 (:789-792), rate-limit 429 (:219-246), tenant-reject 403 (:369-372), coalesced serve (:465); or the metric unwired (absent series → Ok(0) → `before + 1` fails). A doubled/retried scatter reads >=2, which the exact == also catches.

== HIT-PATH SHORT-CIRCUIT ==
The cached response is returned at search.rs:556 — BEFORE both record_scatter_fan_out call sites (:811 and :1406). A served hit therefore cannot increment the fan-out counter unless the short-circuit itself regresses (the hit arm fails to return early). This is exactly what acceptance_1's `scatter_after_second == scatter_after_first` (:554-560) pins, and it is why acceptance_2's scatter delta is attributable solely to its miss query.

== FAIL-OPEN PATHS ==
- Cache lookup Err (search.rs:573-576): debug-logged, NEITHER hits nor misses recorded, request proceeds uncached — and because result_cache_key was already captured at :514, the response would STILL be stored at :941. With the CURRENT core this arm is defensively dead: result_cache.rs constructs no Err anywhere (the "Err if the cache is disabled" doc on get/insert is stale — disabled returns Ok(None)/Ok(()), result_cache.rs:134-136 and :166-168). The contract stands: if a backend error is ever wired in, no counter moves and the request proceeds uncached.
- Canonicalization failure (search.rs:496-505): empty canonical string skips the whole block (:507) — no hit, no miss, no key capture, no store.
- Cached-bytes deser failure (:558-562): NOT silent — degrades to a recorded miss and a fresh fan-out.
- Store-side failures: insert Err (:951-953) and response serialization failure (:943 `if let Ok`) are debug-logged/silent and record no counter; the observable effect is downstream — the next identical query is a miss (acceptance_2's hits delta :656-663 fails). The store also only happens after a SUCCESSFUL scatter: a dfs error returns 500 at :907-913 before :941, so a failed scatter never files a serving entry.
- proxy_counter Ok(0) fallback (fn test :432-449, doc :423-431): an absent series on a LIVE metrics endpoint reads as 0, so every acceptance delta (exact `before + 1` equality) fails loudly; a dead ENDPOINT fails harder — the GET errors and the unwrap panics. Neither can pass silently.

== ttl_ms BEHAVIOR ==
- Test config: result_cache { enabled: true, ttl_ms: 500, max_size: 1000 } (test :230; parent cited :216). Core default ttl_ms = 500 (result_cache.rs:337).
- The entry is WRITTEN on the miss: after a successful scatter, :941-956 inserts the merged body under result_cache_key — the lookup-time key (:514; see the plan §13.10.1 comment :479-486 explaining the reuse and the settings-version pin). The entry is stamped expires_at = now + ttl at INSERT time (result_cache.rs:170-171, CacheEntry::new :45-49).
- Hits NEVER refresh it: get (result_cache.rs:133-159) checks is_expired (:53-55, `now >= expires_at`) and returns data without touching expires_at. Lifetime runs from the MISS that wrote it; each fresh miss re-inserts and re-stamps. Expired → popped + Ok(None) → Prometheus miss (:567).
- Load-bearing for acceptance_1 (:540-543 comment; parent cited :526-529): the 500ms window between query 1 and query 2 is the entry's whole life — a host stall past it makes the repeat a fresh miss and the hits delta fails, reading exactly like a lookup regression. LRU eviction at max_size 1000 (result_cache.rs:179-185) is irrelevant at test scale. Also: the served hit echoes the settings_version captured at LOOKUP time (:543-548), not store time.

== TEST-SIDE ANCHORS (current tree; = parent citation + 14) ==
- acceptance_1_cache_hit_bypasses_fan_out: attribute :455, fn :456, body :455-561 (parent L441-547). Row count :509 / content :510; scatter_after_first == before+1 :514-521; result1 == result2 :538; hits delta :544-551; bypass assert :554-560; 3ca59fe-style comments :488-490 (deltas over body equality), :512-513 (exactly-once fan-out), :536-537 (body equality cannot detect the bypass), :540-543 (TTL stall), :553 (served hit must short-circuit).
- acceptance_2_cache_miss_triggers_fan_out: attribute :563, fn :564, body :563-664 (parent L549-650). Baselines :598-606 — hits_before read BEFORE the first query (:601-603), so its delta also proves the miss query itself recorded no hit; miss delta :624-631; scatter delta :632-639; repeat :642-649; body equality :655; hits delta :656-663; comments :595-597 (miss-side pinned by deltas), :622-623 (miss + fan-out are the two halves), :653-654 (body equality cannot prove the entry was filed); proxy_counter + Ok(0) doc :423-449 (parent L409-417).
- Deliberate omission, observation not a defect: acceptance_2 has no post-hit scatter-flat assert — the short-circuit half of the pair is acceptance_1's :554-560.

MAPPING-ONLY: no file edits made, no commit. The dirty working-tree state of both files belongs to the umbrella's landing work (miroir-add6da8c), not this bead.

issue.notes:
Verification pass done; semantics checked against the implementation, not just the comments. ResultCache (crates/miroir-core/src/result_cache.rs): ttl anchored at insert, hits never refresh it (expired lookup pops + counts a miss), LRU at max_size; search.rs: hit->hits counter + serve cached bytes, miss/deserialize-fail->misses counter + scatter, lookup Err->NEITHER counter; fan-out histogram _count +1 per scatter-gather; PATCH settings runs the two_phase broadcast (default strategy) whose commit bumps the settings_version inside the cache key. All prior sweep comments verified TRUE against this code.

Per-assertion regression map (file: crates/miroir-proxy/tests/p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs @ 0f3bfd9):

SHARED: proxy_counter() reads an absent series as 0, so a removed/renamed/stopped metric breaks every delta loudly instead of passing silently (comment in place; token-match verified free of _bucket/_sum/# collisions).

a1 cache_hit_bypasses_fan_out: status success -> endpoint/auth broken. hits==1 & name==Laptop -> merge drops or misorders rows. scatter==+1 -> flat: miss path short-circuited or metric unwired; doubled: re-scatter retry. body equality -> foreign-entry serve or corrupted byte round-trip (commented: blind to bypass, deltas pin). hits==+1 -> repeat recorded as miss: entry never stored / LRU-evicted early / host stall past the 500ms ttl (comment names the ttl lean; hits-don't-refresh verified). scatter flat after hit -> the bypass regression itself.

a2 miss_triggers_fan_out: row asserts -> row correctness. misses==+1 -> query wrongly served as hit, or lookup Err recording neither counter (Err arm verified). scatter==+1 -> miss short-circuited/doubled. body eq -> foreign serve. hits==+1 -> miss never filed a serving entry. scatter flat -> bypass.

a3 stores_results: hit_count==3 -> merge drops/dups on the very body cached. scatter==+1 -> precondition: nothing to cache otherwise (flat/doubled). body eq -> foreign serve. hits==+1 -> insert never landed or evicted early. scatter flat -> bypass.

a4 reduces_upstream_calls: 5 identical bodies -> mid-loop foreign serve or unstable merge (commented: holds both paths). hits==+4 -> ANY repeat leaking past cache (no-store/evict/ttl stall; stall risk named). scatter==+1 -> flat: first query short-circuited; doubled: retry; alone pins the 5x3 -> 1x3 upstream reduction.

a5 distinct_cache_keys: misses==+4 -> key collision: text-ignoring key merges q2 into q1's entry, limit-ignoring merges q4 into q2's; colliding query arrives as a hit and the delta falls short (the detector that survives equal rows; q4 rows == q2 rows by construction). scatter==+4 -> per-query short-circuit/double. assert_ne pairs -> cross-query row contamination on the miss path (fires while collided rows differ; documented). repeat body eqs -> repeat served a foreign entry (pair 4 blind by construction; documented). hits==+4 -> entries not filed / ttl stall. scatter flat -> bypass.

a6 graceful_cache_failure (STRENGTHENED this bead): previously only status+len==1 -> general proxy breakage, i.e. no cache-flow regression could fail it, and the trailing TODO comment admitted it. With the in-process cache there is no failure to inject (every get/insert path returns Ok), so it now pins the degrade flow: misses==+1 -> cache layer aborting/bypassing lookup accounting while still serving; scatter==+1 -> graceful path serving without gathering; comment scopes real failure injection to p13_12's unit suite. New deltas deterministic: enabled cache, single target, fresh process.

a7 ttl_expiration: body eq -> commented blind to no-expiry. misses==+2 -> repeat hit = entry outlived its ttl (expiry broken). scatter==+2 -> unexpired serve bypassed the fan-out. 600ms sleep > 500ms ttl measured from insert -> stall only makes the entry more expired (monotone-safe, documented).

a8 concurrent: NO counter bounds, deliberately (commented): coalesced in-flight duplicates make any hit/miss split flake; 10 identical bodies -> divergent rows under the race; len==1 -> row drop. Intentional absence documented in place.

a9 invalidation_on_settings_change: PATCH success asserted -> broadcast failure is a broken run, not a pass (its commit versions the key; two_phase commit verified). body eq -> commented blind (one doc = same rows). misses==+2 -> stale entry survived the version bump. scatter==+2 -> stale hit also bypassed the fan-out.

a10 complex_query: facetDistribution.is_object -> merge/forward drops facets. scatter==+1 -> complex query short-circuited (pins the later flat assert against holding vacuously). body eq incl. facetDistribution -> foreign serve / facet loss in round-trip. hits==+1 -> complex body never stored or looked up under a different key (old facet self-compare removed as implied; documented). scatter flat -> bypass.

Failure direction: every cache-flow bound is an == on a delta against a pre-read baseline; an inverted refactor (swapped hit/miss counters, skipped observe, flipped lookup) moves the read off the expected value and fails with the message. No >=/<= unsigned non-bounds remain (the p13_12-style vacuous comparisons are gone from this file). Nothing deleted: every assertion maps to a regression no neighbour covers.

Strengthened: a6 only. Commented intentional bounds were already in place from the sweep links and were re-verified for accuracy. Suite compiles, rustfmt-clean, clippy -D warnings clean on the test target, and all 10 tests skip cleanly under MIROIR_TEST_SKIP_DOCKER=1. Commit 0f3bfd9 pushed to Forgejo origin.

issue.description:
Third link of the miroir-db588c65 split; depends on the acceptance_1..5 sweep so the two sweeps apply one consistent standard.

TARGET: acceptance_6_searches_succeed_with_cache_disabled through acceptance_10_cache_with_complex_query in crates/miroir-proxy/tests/p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs (~lines 725-1070). Pay attention to acceptance_8_concurrent_cache_access, which already carries a comment at ~line 849 that it deliberately asserts no cache counters (query coalescing) — preserve that intent rather than "fixing" it.

LOOK FOR (the p13_12 lesson from commit 3ca59fe): assertions that can never fail — min/max comparisons on unsigned or bool values, len() >= 0, comparisons against a type's own MIN/MAX, self-equality, and asserts on state the test never varies. Reason from semantics (TTL expiration, cache-disabled passthrough, invalidation on index update, concurrent access), not from the lint.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Zero never-firing comparisons remain in acceptance_6..10; every replacement bound can fail on a plausible regression (expired entry still served, disabled cache still fan-outing, stale entry surviving invalidation).
- Intentional but non-obvious bounds get a one-line comment in the p13_12 commit-3ca59fe style.

- The suite compiles and still skips cleanly without Docker.
issue.notes:
Sweep complete; commit 0e20c0b on main (pushed to Forgejo). Note: the task's line refs were stale — at HEAD the block was acceptance_6..10 at lines 1127-1451, and acceptance_8 carried no counter comment at ~849 (added it).

Per-test findings:
- acceptance_6 (graceful_handling_of_cache_connection_failure): NOTHING FOUND. Both assertions (status success; hits len == 1) can fire. Coverage gap, out of scope, left as-is: the in-process result cache has no external connection to break, so no cache failure is ever simulated — the test is effectively a cold-miss smoke test.
- acceptance_7 (cache_ttl_expiration): FIXED. assert_eq!(result1, result2) held whether the repeat re-scattered or was served an entry that outlived its TTL — blind to the acceptance's own regression. Now pinned by misses+2 and scatter+2 deltas (q1 cold miss; q2 must miss past the 500ms ttl_ms and re-scatter), equality kept with a blindness comment; sleep anchoring documented (measured from q1 completion, so a stall only makes the entry more expired).
- acceptance_8 (concurrent_cache_access): NO COMPARISON CHANGES — deliberately counter-free preserved. Ten racing identical queries land as an arbitrary coalesced-waits/hits/misses mix, so any hit/miss split would flake; the present asserts (identical bodies, hits len == 1) can fire. Added the one-line intent comment the split expected to find there.
- acceptance_9 (cache_invalidation_on_index_update): FIXED, two defects. (a) The "if let Ok(resp)" wrapper around the settings PATCH response swallowed transport errors and skipped the entire acceptance while the test still passed — PATCH is now unconditional (unwrap + status assert), which is the test's declared intent since the inner status assert already fired on 5xx. (b) assert_eq!(result1, result2) cannot see a stale entry surviving invalidation (one document -> identical rows on both paths). Now pinned by misses+2 and scatter+2: the two-phase commit bumps the global settings version synchronously (crates/miroir-core/src/settings.rs:239) and the search path keys on that version (search.rs:497), so a broken invalidation leaves q2 a hit and the deltas fall short.
- acceptance_10 (cache_with_complex_query): FIXED. assert_eq!(result1["facetDistribution"], result2["facetDistribution"]) was implied by the whole-body equality two lines above — never fires independently — removed. Replaced with hits+1 (complex repeat must be served from the entry), plus acceptance_1's exactly-one-fan-out pin after q1 and the flat bypass check.

Verification: suite compiles; all 10 tests skip cleanly with MIROIR_TEST_SKIP_DOCKER=1 (0.00s, exit 0); clippy -D warnings clean on the test target (edition 2021 rustfmt clean). Live runs NOT exercised — the control path is wedged today (POST /search/products hangs on every attempt since 22:27Z, see miroir parent-bead captures).

Caveat for the first live run: the new hit-delta in acceptance_10 (like the already-committed acceptance_1..5 hit deltas) only passes with the store-side cache-key reuse currently UNCOMMITTED in the working tree of crates/miroir-proxy/src/routes/search.rs. Static analysis (not live-verified): HEAD's store path rebuilds the key with ranking_score=Some(false) while lookups serialize rankingScore=null for these bodies (field has no skip_serializing_if; CacheKey hashes the canonical string verbatim — result_cache.rs:80), so repeats miss and every hits delta in the suite falls short until that fix lands. The miss/scatter deltas in acceptance_7/9 do not depend on it.

issue.description:
Child 1/4 of the miroir-14dcb98f split (container runtime precondition). Establishes that testcontainers can actually start the exact Meilisearch image the p13_13 suite requests before any suite time is spent on it.

testcontainers-modules 0.11.6 pins getmeili/meilisearch:v1.8.3 (NAME/TAG consts in its meilisearch module). The suite's check_docker_available uses /var/run/docker.sock by default and honors an explicit DOCKER_HOST (rootless podman path documented in the test file header).

Steps:
1. Confirm the runtime path: /var/run/docker.sock exists and answers (docker info), or record the DOCKER_HOST value the run must use (e.g. unix:///run/user/1001/podman/podman.sock after systemctl --user start podman.socket).
2. Spawn the pinned image for real: docker run -d --rm -p 127.0.0.1:<ephemeral>:7700 getmeili/meilisearch:v1.8.3 --master-key key0 (or podman equivalent), poll /health until 204, then remove it.
3. If the image is absent locally, pre-pull it so the suite run does not pay the pull.

Acceptance criteria:
- One real container of getmeili/meilisearch:v1.8.3 started and answered /health (HTTP 204) on this box
- The runtime decision (default socket vs explicit DOCKER_HOST and its value) recorded as a note on this bead
- Container cleaned up afterwards; no leftover container or bound port 7700
issue.notes:
VERIFIED on lab box 2026-09-11. Runtime decision: DEFAULT /var/run/docker.sock works — no DOCKER_HOST needed. uid 1001 is in the docker group; socket answers (Docker 27.5.1, overlay2). Rootless podman fallback NOT required.

Image: getmeili/meilisearch:v1.8.3 present locally (d1fb40664b6d), pull confirmed up-to-date at digest sha256:65a5f42dbcdcac37eb5015289dba2a24a047a8101a4a017c3ff0d7e9589183d5 — suite pays no pull.

Real spawn with the suite's EXACT config (env-only, per testcontainers-modules 0.11.6 meilisearch module + p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs): MEILI_NO_ANALYTICS=true, MEILI_MASTER_KEY=key0, default CMD, 127.0.0.1:<ephemeral>:7700. Container 1fdf20cd8a46 started first try; /health answered HTTP 200 with body {"status":"available"} in ~1s (host port 32777). Master-key env mechanism verified: GET /indexes -> 401 unauthenticated, 200 with Bearer key0.

Two corrections to the bead description: (1) /health on v1.8.3 returns 200, not 204 — which is exactly what the module's wait strategy expects (HttpWaitStrategy: status 200 + body {"status": "available"}), so the suite is consistent with reality; the description's 204 is wrong. (2) The description's 'docker run ... --master-key key0' arg form FAILS on this image — ENTRYPOINT is 'tini --' and CMD is a shell command, so CLI args make tini exec '--master-key' (exit 127, '[FATAL tini] exec --master-key failed: No such file or directory'). The suite already avoids this by using with_master_key (env), documented at p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs:268-273.

Cleanup: probe container removed (--rm), no leftover container, no host listener on 7700. Note: box carries ~15 OTHER pre-existing meilisearch containers from earlier/parallel runs (p13probe-node*, repro-diag-*, p13diag/p13repro-meili, 7 random-named, up 2-11h) publishing ports 17990-17999/32768-32774/33115-33123 — none collide with the suite's 17770/9090, left untouched as they are not mine. Local ephemeral-port exhaustion is the only plausible risk if that population keeps growing; worth a glance before a full suite run.

=== GET /indexes ROW — MECHANISM: PROXIED, NOT NODE-SERVED (correction CONFIRMED) ===

The route EXISTS on the proxy: .route("/", post(create_index_handler).get(list_indexes_handler)) (indexes.rs:309) on the /indexes nest (.nest("/indexes", indexes::router::<UnifiedState>()) at main.rs:850). The original claim "served by the NODE process" (implying the proxy has no such route) is MECHANISM DRIFT, as the parent's consolidated note records (drift item 1); this verification confirms the correction against source: PROXIED, NOT BYPASSED. Lock conclusion UNCHANGED.

Handler mechanism, all cites EXACT in the current tree (indexes.rs:471-492):
- Signature (471-473): async fn list_indexes_handler(Extension(config): Extension<Arc<Config>>) — the ONLY extractor. Extension<Arc<Config>> resolves to the main.rs:883 layer (.layer(axum::Extension(state.admin.config.clone()))); AppState.config is Arc<MiroirConfig> (admin_endpoints.rs:421) and pub type Config = MiroirConfig (miroir-core/src/config.rs:110) — exact type match. NO AppState extractor: the handler structurally cannot touch topology, session_manager, query_coalescer, result_cache, or Redis (grep: ZERO occurrences of query_coalescer/result_cache/session_manager/redis anywhere in indexes.rs).
- :474 — builds a FRESH MeilisearchClient per request from config.node_master_key. MeilisearchClient is indexes.rs-local (struct :57-60; new :63-70 = fresh reqwest::Client with hardcoded 10s timeout :65; auth_header :72-74 = "Authorization: Bearer {node_master_key}"). Note the DISTINCT NODE KEY: the harness config carries master_key test_master_key (client-facing) vs node_master_key key0 (capture script :70-71, config template :339-340) — the outbound call authenticates to the node with the NODE key, further proof of the proxy hop.
- :475-478 — address = config.nodes.first(); 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE if the node list is empty.
- :479-485 — ONE outbound GET {first-node}/indexes via client.get_raw (indexes.rs:134-146); this is the handler's ONLY await. Transport error -> map_err -> 500.
- :486-488 — 2xx -> parse body to JSON; parse failure degrades to {"results":[]} but STILL returns 200.
- :489-491 — non-2xx -> forwards the node's status (StatusCode::from_u16, 500 fallback).
No scatter/fan-out, no join_all (contrast the broadcast handlers in the same file), no queueing, no shared client state.

Auth/middleware path for GET /indexes (each step lock-free):
1. csrf_middleware (outermost, wired main.rs:889-895): GET short-circuit auth.rs:930-932 — next.run before any admin-path/redis_store access. LOCKS NONE.
2. auth_middleware (wired main.rs:885-888): /indexes is NOT dispatch-exempt (is_dispatch_exempt auth.rs:546-594 covers only /health, /version, /_miroir/ready, /_miroir/ui/search/locale/*, /_miroir/admin/login, /_miroir/ui/search/{index}/session, /ui/search/{index}) -> dispatch RUNS: master key -> Rule 3 (auth.rs:769), JWT -> Rule 1. Dispatch is synchronous string ops; revoked_sessions is consulted only for admin paths (is_admin_path false for /indexes, auth.rs:620-621). LOCKS NONE.
3. Extension layers + DefaultBodyLimit (main.rs:880-884): no locks.
4. session_pinning_middleware (middleware.rs:170-182): x-miroir-session header parse + extensions insert only. LOCKS NONE.
5. request_id_middleware (middleware.rs:138-164): header/extension only. LOCKS NONE.
6. telemetry_middleware (wired main.rs:869-875): atomics + prometheus label-map lock held only within the lookup, never across the next.run await. LOCKS NONE held during the request.

EMPTY — LOCKS NONE. GET /indexes acquires no std/tokio Mutex/RwLock anywhere on its path: the handler body has exactly one await (the outbound node GET, bounded by the client's 10s reqwest timeout — it cannot park indefinitely, worst case 10s -> 500), and no middleware on the route holds a coordination lock across an await. Consistent with cycle-5 live behavior: control routes answered promptly during the wedge while the search wedge persisted. Consistent with the corrected proxied mechanism. Shared objects: the ONLY state the /health request path shares with the task is Metrics (task writes gauges main.rs:1083/1087/1091/1102; middleware observes middleware.rs:1727-1734 and :1656) — prometheus-crate atomics; with_label_values takes only the crate-internal short label-map RwLock with no .await held under it, so it cannot host a park. The task's await-held locks (topology.write :956, sessions/pending_writes.write via :1110) are touched by NO part of the /health path. Verdict: route + completion middleware share NO lock with the background task; sole shared state is lock-free metric counters.
Trap contrast: GET /_miroir/ready DOES take state.topology.read() (health.rs:47) — the readiness route would contend with the task's write guard; /health does not. Health ≠ readiness.

CHECK 2 — /indexes scoping: LOCKS NONE in the proxy process.
Route main.rs:850 (.nest("/indexes", indexes::router::<UnifiedState>())); GET / → list_indexes_handler (indexes.rs:309; handler :471-492; comment :468 "list indexes (proxy to first node)"). It extracts only Extension<Arc<Config>> (:472 — an Arc clone, no lock), builds a fresh MeilisearchClient per request (:474) and forwards get_raw to config.nodes.first() (:475-481; client GET at indexes.rs:134-148). The 200 response body is produced by the NODE process; the proxy merely relays bytes and holds no topology/session/task-registry lock anywhere on this path. issue.description:
Child 2/4 of the miroir-14dcb98f split (port precondition). The p13_13 suite hard-binds proxy port 17770 and Prometheus port 9090; a foreign miroir-proxy holding either passes wait_for_ready against the wrong process and produces silently wrong evidence. This has actually happened on this box (see the p13-13-fixed-ports-contention project memory).

Steps:
1. Run ss -ltnp | grep -E '17770|9090' and record the result.
2. For each holder, apply the ownerless-stray discrimination from the project memory: (a) parent chain ends at systemd --user, (b) holder ancestry excludes every live claude/needle process, (c) proxy request log shows no HTTP lines for 30+ min while periodic ticks continue. All three -> SIGTERM the stray (it exits gracefully). Any check fails -> the holder belongs to a live worker: do NOT kill it, record the holder and mark this bead blocked with a note.
3. Re-run the ss check and confirm both ports are free.

Acceptance criteria:
- Pre/post ss -ltnp output recorded as notes on this bead
- Every holder classified orphaned vs live, with the evidence for the verdict
- Ports 17770 and 9090 are free immediately before hand-off (or the bead documents a live-holder block instead of killing someone else's process)
issue.notes:
PORT PRECONDITION VERIFIED 2026-09-11 — both ports free, zero holders, nothing killed.

PRE-CHECK (step 1):
$ ss -ltnp | grep -E '17770|9090'
(no output, grep exit 1 — no listening socket on either port)
Context: full listener table had 79 sockets, none matching.

HOLDER CLASSIFICATION (step 2): vacuous — ZERO holders of 17770/9090, so there was no orphaned-vs-live verdict to make and no SIGTERM was issued. Corroborating evidence for 'no holder':
- ps -eo pid,ppid,etime,cmd | grep -iE 'miroir|meilisearch' shows NO miroir-proxy process of any kind. Matches were only: (a) ~40 pairs of tini/meilisearch container processes (foreign, etimes 47m-19h), (b) podman system service on /tmp/podman-miroir.sock (foreign, ~20h), (c) my own needle run + claude process.
- docker ps: none of the ~40 running containers publishes 17770 or 9090 (their host ports are 331xx/327xx/1799x/17781), so no container holds either port via DNAT/userland-proxy either.

POST-CHECK (step 3), all free:
$ ss -ltnp | grep -E ':(17770|9090)[[:space:]]' -> exit 1
$ ss -tan | grep -E ':(17770|9090)[[:space:]]' -> exit 1 (no socket in ANY state, incl. TIME_WAIT)
Bind probe (no SO_REUSEADDR, strictest form) — all six succeeded:
  FREE 0.0.0.0:17770 / 127.0.0.1:17770 / [::]:17770
  FREE 0.0.0.0:9090  / 127.0.0.1:9090  / [::]:9090

VERDICT: precondition satisfied; ports 17770 and 9090 are free immediately before hand-off. Live p13_13 run can proceed without the foreign-proxy poisoning risk.

SIDE OBSERVATION (out of scope, not acted on): the box currently carries the large stray-meilisearch-container population the project memory warns about (~40 containers, oldest ~19h). None touch 17770/9090, but if the live run spawns more nodes, ephemeral-port exhaustion is the plausible failure mode. Left untouched — other workers' containers.

This child covers the HOLD side of Section 3 (STAGE-13 SPECIAL CHECK): the hold span, the health-checker writer cadence and its guard span, and the probe bound. Note on known drift already recorded by the prior consolidation: "capture.sh" resolves to scripts/p13-13-first-search-capture.sh; config.rs is crates/miroir-core/src/config.rs; main.rs gauges actually span 1080-1091, sync_rebalancer_metrics :1094, mark_ready 1096-1099, implicit guard release ~1114.

STEPS:

2. Re-verify the hold: topology.read() at crates/miroir-proxy/src/routes/search.rs:667 is a write-preferring (tokio) RwLock read guard held to line 917 (explicit drop), spanning planning and the whole DFS call. Confirm the span and guard type on the current tree; note clean-HEAD equivalents if the dirty cache-key refactor shifts lines.
3. Re-verify the writer: health checker takes state.topology.write().await at src/main.rs:956. Re-check the tick interval both ways and keep them SEPARATED: ~200ms harness (scripts/p13-13-first-search-capture.sh:352) vs 5000ms default (crates/miroir-core/src/config.rs:248).
4. Re-verify the write guard spans the WHOLE tick body: probe send().await main.rs:988, gauges 1080-1091, sync_rebalancer_metrics main.rs:1094, mark_ready 1096-1099, prune_expired().await main.rs:1110, implicit guard release ~1114 (no explicit drop). Confirm each coordinate; list drift.
5. Re-verify the probe bound: health.timeout_ms = 1000ms harness (capture script :353) vs 2000ms default (config.rs:249), and that the bound is the per-tick reqwest client timeout on the health client built at main.rs:974 — NOT main.rs:702 (that is the canary client on scatter.node_timeout_ms, 5000ms default).

- A note on this bead records tree state and confirms or corrects every coordinate above, listing drift explicitly.
- Harness vs default numbers are separated explicitly (200ms tick / 1s probe bound harness; 5000ms tick / 2s probe bound defaults).
