issue.notes:
Stage enumeration of `search_handler` (crates/miroir-proxy/src/routes/search.rs:173-1141). All line numbers are WORKING-TREE coordinates (uncommitted result-cache store-key refactor applied) — the diff shifts ~+10 lines in the 479-580 region vs HEAD; see "Diff intersection" at the end. Await-target implementations verified in miroir-core source, cited per stage.

Unless stated otherwise: every in-process await below is a tokio RwLock read/write (uncontended fast path, no timeout possible) and NONE of them carries a timeout. The only timeouts in the whole handler are: (1) the coalesced-wait tokio::time::timeout, (2) session-wait max_wait, (3) the per-node reqwest total-request timeout (`scatter.node_timeout_ms`) baked into HttpClient at stage 17.

Handler-level span: `#[tracing::instrument]` at search.rs:172 wraps the whole fn (the "/search/:index" span seen open in the wedge captures).

STAGE 1 — Entry & request extraction — search.rs:173-197
- Path index, AppState/SessionId/JwtClaims extensions, HeaderMap, Json body already decoded by axum before the fn body runs.
- Awaits: none.
- Logs: none.

STAGE 2 — Search-UI rate limit — search.rs:199-247
- Awaits: none. redis `check_rate_limit_search_ui` (search.rs:212 -> task_store/redis.rs:3065) and the local limiter `check` (233-236) are SYNCHRONOUS blocking calls run inline on the tokio worker.
- Logs: warn! "search UI rate limited (redis)" 215-218; warn! "failed to check search UI rate limit" 227; warn! "search UI rate limited (local backend)" 238-241. Early 429 returns at 219-222 / 242-245.

STAGE 3 — Alias resolution — search.rs:249-264
- Await: search.rs:252 `state.alias_registry.resolve(&index).await` — aliases RwLock READ (alias/mod.rs:200-205). No timeout.
- Logs: none (metric `inc_alias_resolution` at 253 only).

STAGE 4 — Session pinning — search.rs:266-327
- Await: search.rs:268 `get_pinned_group` — sessions RwLock READ (session_pinning.rs:270-287). No timeout.
- Await (Block strategy only): search.rs:276-280 `wait_for_write_completion` (session_pinning.rs:204-264) — poll loop; sleeps via `tokio::time::sleep` with 25ms->500ms-cap exponential backoff; HAS TIMEOUT: `max_wait` = `session_manager.max_wait_duration()`; on expiry emits warn! "session pin wait timeout" (session_pinning.rs:247-252) and returns Err -> handler routes best-effort to pinned group (295-301).
- Logs: debug! "session pinning applied" 321-326 (only when a strategy label was produced). Metrics observe_session_wait_duration / inc_session_pin_enforced / inc_session_wait_timeout at 284-299, 306.

STAGE 5 — Tenant affinity — search.rs:329-377
- Await: search.rs:342-346 `tenant_affinity_manager.resolve_from_headers(&headers_map, false).await`. No timeout.
- Logs: debug! "tenant affinity applied" 355-360; warn! "tenant affinity resolution failed" 368. Early 403 return 369-372 on reject policy.

STAGE 6 — Pin combination — search.rs:379-388
- Sync. Metric `inc_tenant_session_pin_override` 383. No logs.

STAGE 7 — Query coalescing SUBSCRIBE — search.rs:390-477
- Awaits: search.rs:394 `settings_broadcast.current_version()` — settings_version RwLock READ (settings.rs:84-86); search.rs:403-407 `query_coalescer.try_coalesce` — pending RwLock WRITE (idempotency.rs:194-207). No timeouts.
- If coalesced, the wait: search.rs:416-418 `tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_millis(scatter.node_timeout_ms), rx.recv())` — broadcast::Receiver recv — HAS TIMEOUT (= scatter.node_timeout_ms).
  - Hit path: await search.rs:440-444 `is_in_flight` (in_flight RwLock READ, settings.rs:294-296), then early return; info!(target "miroir.search_coalesced") "coalesced search completed" 458-463.
  - Channel closed: debug! "coalesced query channel closed, proceeding with normal scatter" 469.
  - Timeout: debug! "timeout waiting for coalesced query, proceeding with normal scatter" 473.

STAGE 8 — Result cache LOOKUP — search.rs:479-579 (early-return exit on hit)
- Awaits: search.rs:493 `current_version()` (settings_version RwLock READ); search.rs:516 `result_cache.get(&cache_key)` — LruCache RwLock WRITE (result_cache.rs:134-171); on hit search.rs:535-539 `is_in_flight` (in_flight RwLock READ). NO timeouts on any of them.
- Logs: info!(target "miroir.search_cache_hit") "result cache hit - bypassing scatter-gather" 523-528; debug! "failed to deserialize cached result" 560; debug! "result cache miss" 568-571; debug! "result cache lookup error" 575.
- Metrics: inc_result_cache_hits 522; inc_result_cache_misses 561/567.
- Boundary value for timeline matching: on a normal miss the LAST log before the scatter region is debug! "result cache miss" (568).

STAGE 9 — Header extraction (min settings version, over-fetch) — search.rs:581-595 — sync, no logs. (min_settings_version extracted here is SHADOWED by a duplicate re-extraction at 660-664.)

STAGE 10 — Multi-target dispatch — search.rs:597-613
- Only when resolved_targets.len() > 1. Await: search.rs:603-612 `search_multi_targets(...)` (fn body 1147-1538 — its internal stages mirror 2/4/11/14/16/19 with target fan-out and NO result cache). Normal single-index requests skip this entirely.

STAGE 11 — Scoped-key resolution — search.rs:615-633
- SYNCHRONOUS blocking redis: `get_search_ui_scoped_key` (redis.rs:3105) + `observe_search_ui_scoped_key` (redis.rs:3173). No awaits, no logs.

STAGE 12 — JWT filter injection — search.rs:635-658 — sync, no logs.

STAGE 13 — Topology read + query planner — search.rs:666-687
- Await: search.rs:667 `state.topology.read().await` — tokio RwLock READ, **held across planning AND the whole DFS call, dropped only at search.rs:917**. No timeout. NOTE: tokio RwLock is write-preferring — this read blocks if a writer (health checker) is queued.
- Await: search.rs:679-682 `query_planner.plan(...)` (query_planner.rs:95). No timeout. No logs.

STAGE 14 — Shard-policy parse — search.rs:689-699 — sync; early 500 return 694-698 on invalid config.

STAGE 15 — Scatter planning — search.rs:701-811
- Awaits (mutually exclusive branches, ALL no-timeout):
  - pinned: search.rs:725-734 `plan_search_scatter_for_group`; fallback search.rs:743-752 `plan_search_scatter_with_narrowing`.
  - version floor: search.rs:758-777 `plan_search_scatter_with_version_floor` — its version closure (search.rs:770-773) runs `tokio::task::block_in_place` + `Handle::block_on(node_version)` — nested RwLock READs (settings.rs:93-99) on a blocking thread.
  - normal: search.rs:797-806 `plan_search_scatter_with_narrowing`.
- Spans: `scatter_plan` info_span created and IMMEDIATELY dropped at 713-724 (`drop(_plan_span)` before any await) — emits nothing.
- Logs: warn! "pinned group unavailable, falling back to normal routing" 739-742. Early 503 return 789-792 when no covering set.
- Metric: record_scatter_fan_out 811.

STAGE 16 — Request build — search.rs:813-861
- Sync. Metrics inc_vector_search_over_fetched / inc_vector_merge_strategy 824-828. HttpClient::new(search_key, scatter.node_timeout_ms) 854-857 <- the ONLY timeout the node calls will have. No logs.

STAGE 17 — Coalescing REGISTER — search.rs:863-898
- Awaits: search.rs:867 `current_version()` (RwLock READ); search.rs:885 `query_coalescer.register` — pending RwLock WRITE (idempotency.rs:212-233). No timeouts.
- Logs: debug! "too many pending queries, proceeding without coalescing registration" 892. Metric inc_query_coalesce_subscribers(1) 887.

STAGE 18 — DFS scatter-gather EXECUTION — search.rs:900-914  *** the only long-duration await on the hot path ***
- Await: search.rs:901-904 `dfs_query_then_fetch_search(plan, &client, search_req, &topo, policy, &strategy)` (scatter.rs:1197-1206). Internal sequence, all inside the `/search/:index` span:
  a. `execute_preflight` (scatter.rs:1150-1194): fan-out `preflight_node` per node, collected by `futures_util::future::join_all` (scatter.rs:1181) — waits for ALL nodes, no quorum; returns early with empty IDF when the query has no terms (scatter.rs:1163-1170). Same per-node reqwest timeout as (b).
  b. `scatter_gather_search` (scatter.rs:1081-1119) -> `execute_scatter` (scatter.rs:907-1078): per-node `search_node` spawned as join_all tasks (scatter.rs:955-962), each under a `scatter_node` info_span (node_id, address, shard_count; scatter.rs:945-951); Fallback policy retries failed shards SERIALLY across groups/replicas (scatter.rs:1015). Merge runs under a `merge` info_span (scatter.rs:1105-1111).
- Timeout: ONLY the per-node reqwest total-request timeout (`client.rs:25` .timeout(node_timeout_ms)) surfacing as NodeError::Timeout -> failed_shards / degraded. There is NO tokio-level timeout wrapping preflight or scatter, and no overall deadline: join_all waits for every node's own timeout individually. If a node future never yields to reqwest's timer or the deadlock is in-process, this await parks forever.
- Logs: on Err — error!(target default) "search failed" search.rs:908 + 500 return 909-912. On success — NOTHING is logged by this stage itself; the next handler log is stage 21/26.

STAGE 19 — Topology release + hit stripping + body assembly — search.rs:916-935 — sync (`drop(topo)` 917, strip_internal_fields 920-922). No logs.

STAGE 20 — Result cache STORE — search.rs:937-956  *** REWRITTEN BY THE WORKING-TREE DIFF ***
- Await: search.rs:944 `result_cache.insert(cache_key, response_bytes)` — LruCache RwLock WRITE (result_cache.rs:165-191). No timeout.
- Logs: debug! "result cached successfully" 946-949; debug! "failed to store result in cache" 952.

STAGE 21 — Canary query capture — search.rs:958-984
- Await: search.rs:962-984 `query_capture.capture(...)` — session RwLock READ then queries RwLock WRITE (canary.rs:545-577). No timeout. No logs. No-op unless a capture session is active.

STAGE 22 — Coalesced-result broadcast — search.rs:986-1004
- Sync `broadcast_tx.send` 995; Await: search.rs:1003 `query_coalescer.unregister` — pending RwLock WRITE (idempotency.rs:235-238). No timeout.
- Logs: debug! "broadcast search result to coalesced queries" 996-1000.

STAGE 23 — Response header assembly — search.rs:1006-1047
- Awaits: search.rs:1012-1015 `is_in_flight` (RwLock READ); search.rs:1021 `current_version()` (RwLock READ). No timeouts.
- Logs: none. Metric inc_scatter_partial_responses 1027. Headers: X-Miroir-Settings-Inconsistent 1017, X-Miroir-Settings-Version 1023, X-Miroir-Degraded 1038/1040.

STAGE 24 — Shadow dispatch — search.rs:1049-1125
- `tokio::spawn` at search.rs:1061 — FIRE-AND-FORGET, the handler does NOT await it (cannot park the request). Inside the spawned task: awaits `shadow_mgr.shadow_search(...)` per target 1101-1109 (upstream HTTP, no handler-visible timeout). Logs (from the spawned task): debug! "shadow request completed" 1113; warn! "shadow request failed" 1116-1121.

STAGE 25 — Completion log + return — search.rs:1127-1140
- info!(target "miroir.search") "search completed" with index/duration_ms/node_count/estimated_hits/degraded, 1130-1138. This is the terminal event; its absence in a capture with an open /search/:index span means the request parked at or before stage 18's await (or inside stages 19-24's awaits, all of which are in-process RwLocks with no I/O).

DIFF INTERSECTION (git diff -- crates/miroir-proxy/src/routes/search.rs; 26+/58-):
- Hunk 1: new `result_cache_key: Option<CacheKey>` declaration at 479-487 — stage 8 (lookup region).
- Hunk 2: `result_cache_key = Some(cache_key.clone())` at 514 — stage 8.
- Hunks 3+4: comment change + removal of `facets_for_cache` (~814) and `capture_body_for_cache` (~834) — stage 16 (request build).
- Hunk 5: store-site rewrite 937-956 (recomputes nothing; reuses the lookup-time key) — stage 20.
- The diff changes NO await points, NO log lines, and NO timeout structure; it only changes which CacheKey the store uses and deletes two dead clones. Stage 18 (DFS execution) and every pre-scatter stage are untouched by the diff, so a wedge timeline captured pre- or post-diff localizes identically against this enumeration.

ELIMINATION NOTES FOR CHILD 3 (park-point localization):
- Only three awaits in the handler can wait indefinitely on anything slow: 901 (DFS: joins ALL nodes; per-node reqwest timeout is the only bound), 276 (session wait — bounded by max_wait, would emit "session pin wait timeout" then CONTINUE), 416 (coalesced wait — bounded by node_timeout_ms, would emit "timeout waiting for coalesced query" then CONTINUE). Both bounded awaits leave a debug! trace when they expire, so a silent infinite park with no debug lines points at 901 or at an in-process RwLock in stages 13/15/17/20/21/23 (all uncontended in the normal case; stage 13's topology read is the one that can legitimately block on the health-checker writer).
- Log-marker skeleton for timeline matching, in order: "result cache miss" (568, stage 8) -> [scatter_plan span: silent] -> [scatter_node spans + merge span, inside DFS] -> "result cached successfully" (946) -> "broadcast search result..." (996, conditional) -> "search completed" (1130). A capture that ends after "result cache miss" with an open /search/:index span parks in stages 13-18; one that ends after "result cached successfully" parks in 21-23.

issue.description:
Child 4 of the miroir-3422cbe6 split; depends on miroir-213efe5d. Without this, both Agentation scripts are blocked at runtime no matter how correct the HTML is: the toolbar loads react/react-dom/agentation from https://esm.sh, but the CSP defaults do not permit it.

Current defaults (crates/miroir-core/src/config/advanced.rs):
- admin_ui.csp (line ~677): "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; connect-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'" — script-src and connect-src both exclude esm.sh.
- search_ui.csp (line ~789): "default-src 'self'; img-src 'self' https:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'" — no script-src/connect-src directives at all, so default-src 'self' governs and blocks esm.sh module loads.

Task: add https://esm.sh to script-src and connect-src in BOTH defaults (adding the directives explicitly for search_ui rather than widening default-src). Update any config examples / docs that inline these defaults, and update or extend the tests that assert CSP values (crates/miroir-proxy/tests/p10_6_csrf_posture.rs and the build_csp_header unit tests in crates/miroir-proxy/src/auth.rs assert on these strings).

Acceptance criteria:
- Default admin_ui.csp contains script-src and connect-src entries allowing https://esm.sh; frame-ancestors 'none' and all other existing directives preserved.
- Default search_ui.csp explicitly allows https://esm.sh for script-src and connect-src without loosening default-src.
- All CSP-related tests pass locally: cargo test -p miroir-core -p miroir-proxy (matches on CSP strings updated where they assert the new defaults).
- Config documentation (wherever admin_ui.csp/search_ui.csp are documented) notes esm.sh is required for the Agentation toolbar and how to override via csp_overrides.
- Commit only the files this child touches; the working tree has unrelated in-flight changes.
issue.notes: Done in commit 47bb921 (pushed to origin/main). Both CSP defaults now allow https://esm.sh: admin_ui.csp gains it under script-src+connect-src (frame-ancestors 'none' and all other directives preserved); search_ui.csp gains explicit script-src/connect-src directives with default-src 'self' untouched. Docs updated: docs/plan/plan.md (config examples + Agentation CSP rationale paragraph), charts/miroir/values.yaml (search_ui.csp example + override guidance; verified the chart renders neither ui section into config.yaml, so these blocks document binary defaults). CHANGELOG Unreleased/Changed entry added — staged surgically via git apply --cached so the unrelated in-flight kafka-sink CHANGELOG line stayed out of this commit. issue.description:
Child of miroir-8aa32cab (umbrella), blocked by the dockerless-skip sibling. Owns the container-invocation defect: testcontainers 0.23 with_cmd REPLACES the image Cmd, so Meilisearch::default().with_cmd(["--master-key=keyN"]) made the getmeili/meilisearch:v1.8.3 image run "tini -- --master-key=keyN", which dies with [FATAL tini (2)] exec --master-key=... failed: No such file or directory (reproduced on podman 5.4.1). Because of this the tests failed in EVERY environment, docker or not.

State at split time: the working tree already drafts the fix - Meilisearch::default().with_master_key(NODE_MASTER_KEY), the testcontainers-modules 0.11 env API instead of with_cmd. It is unverified: this lab box has no /var/run/docker.sock (podman CLI exists, no docker socket).

Work:
1. Give testcontainers a reachable runtime on this box - podman rootless socket (systemctl --user start podman.socket, then DOCKER_HOST=unix:///run/podman/podman.sock for the run) or a docker-enabled host. Nothing in repo CI or declarative-config changes for this.
2. Prove the invocation: one node started exactly as the tests do must answer on its mapped 7700 port - 200 with Authorization Bearer key0, rejected without the key (401/403) - and container logs must contain no tini FATAL.
3. If the env API proves insufficient, fall back to a full cmd that appends args AFTER the binary (with_http_addr style) and re-verify.
4. Run the full target with the runtime up: all 3 nodes per test must start and become ready (wait_for_ready passes). Failures after ready belong to the next sibling, not this one.

Acceptance criteria:
- A node started by the test construction answers authenticated and rejects unauthenticated
- No tini FATAL in container logs
- Full target run reaches ready state
- Close reason records the exact runtime bring-up commands so later siblings reuse them.

issue.close_reason: Read-only ground-truth analysis complete; no repo files changed (verification-only, nothing to commit). All three counters traced to exhaustive increment sites with file:line: hits (search.rs:511, multi_search.rs:359), misses (search.rs:550,556; multi_search.rs:373,380), fan-out _count (search.rs:800 single-index post-cache-hit early-return, :1438 multi-target). Key derivation documented (SipHash u64 of index+canonicalized query+settings_version, no collision guard) plus can-catch/cannot-distinguish per counter. Headline finding, empirically verified via a faithful replica of both derivations (~/scratch/p13-13-key-parity, serde 1.0.229 vs workspace 1.0.228): the single-index store key (search.rs:936-953) never equals the lookup key (search.rs:486-503) - the rebuild reads q/offset/limit/filter from the serde-flatten rest (which lacks named-field keys) and forces rankingScore:Some(false) where the lookup canonicalizes rankingScore:null - so POST /search can never record a hit, every request misses and scatters, and acceptance_1..5's hits>=1 / fan-out==1 / misses==3 bounds are unsatisfiable as written (a5's misses==3 would actually read 4). Multi-search key parity is symmetric and unaffected. TTL 500ms pinned at insert, never refreshed on hit, lazily expired-and-counted-as-miss on access. Also flagged: result_cache_size/evictions metrics and ResultCache::stats() have no callers.
issue.description:
Child 1 of the miroir-48954e4a split (umbrella: sweep p13_13 acceptance_1-5 assertions for comparisons that can never fire).

Establish the semantic ground truth the per-test sweeps will reason from, BEFORE any test body is touched.

TARGET: trace miroir_result_cache_hits_total, miroir_result_cache_misses_total and miroir_scatter_fan_out_size_count from crates/miroir-proxy/src to their increment sites, and read the ResultCache hit/miss path the acceptance tests exercise.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Each of the three counters is traced to the exact source location(s) that increment it, recorded as notes on this bead (file:line plus one sentence on when it fires).
- For each counter, notes state at least one plausible regression it CAN catch (cache serving without short-circuiting fan-out; hit recorded as a miss; a repeat query leaking past the cache) and one thing it CANNOT distinguish.
- Notes cover how the cache key is derived (what acceptance_5's misses == 3 actually counts), and the 500 ms TTL / no-refresh-on-hit behavior acceptance_4 leans on, with file:line evidence.

issue.notes:
GROUND TRUTH for the p13_13 sweep (read-only analysis; no repo files touched; key-parity claim verified empirically in ~/scratch/p13-13-key-parity, serde 1.0.229 ~= workspace 1.0.228).

=== 1. miroir_result_cache_hits_total (Counter, declared middleware.rs:620-624, registered :692, method inc_result_cache_hits middleware.rs:1848-1850) ===
Increment sites (exhaustive):
- routes/search.rs:511 - single-index POST /search/{index}: only when result_cache.get returns Ok(Some) AND the cached bytes deserialize as JSON Value. Handler then returns the cached body at :545, BEFORE scatter.
- routes/multi_search.rs:359 - per multi-search sub-query: Ok(Some) AND bytes deserialize as SearchResponse.
CAN catch: hit-recorded-as-miss (hits drops, misses rises by the same amount); with the fan-out count, a hit that fails to short-circuit (hits constant while scatter _count rises) - the exact regression acceptance_1's comment describes.
CANNOT distinguish: which index/query hit (counter is unlabeled); a cache hit from a query-coalescer serve (search.rs:392-476 returns before lookup, increments inc_query_coalesce_hits instead - so coalescer absorption silently suppresses hits+misses, nondeterministic under concurrency, see acceptance_8's comment); correct rows from a colliding entry; cache-disabled (0 forever) from cache-enabled-but-never-hits (also 0 forever) - acceptance_6 asserts the same 0/0 that a permanently-broken lookup produces.

=== 2. miroir_result_cache_misses_total (Counter, middleware.rs:626-630, registered :693, method :1852-1854) ===
Increment sites (exhaustive):
- routes/search.rs:550 - cached bytes present but deserialize failed (poisoned entry counted as miss).
- routes/search.rs:556 - lookup Ok(None) (absent, or expired-then-popped).
- routes/multi_search.rs:373 - multi-search deserialize failure; :380 - multi-search Ok(None).
NOT incremented (each silently shrinks misses below request count): lookup backend Err (search.rs:562-565 fail-open, debug-log only; ResultCache::get never actually returns Err - result_cache.rs:134-160 - so dead today); canonicalization failure (search.rs:490-495 -> empty string -> whole lookup block skipped, no counter); multi-target alias path (guard search.rs:481 requires resolved_targets.len()==1); coalesced followers (return at :465 before lookup); cache disabled (same guard). ResultCache's own internal misses counter (result_cache.rs:145,156) is separate and consumed nowhere in the proxy.
CAN catch: a repeat query leaking past the cache (misses grows with repeats - the bound acceptance_4's misses==1 leans on); an entry served after it should have expired (misses stops growing).
CANNOT distinguish: absent-miss vs expired-miss vs deserialize-fail-miss (acceptance_7's misses==2 counts one absent + one expired-pop; a poisoned-entry miss would also read 2); first-time miss from repeat-leak miss; misses != lookups on the skip paths above, so 'misses == N requests' undercounts the moment any request skips the cache block.

=== 3. miroir_scatter_fan_out_size_count (Histogram count; declared middleware.rs:598-605, buckets [1,2,3,5,10,20,50], registered :689, method record_scatter_fan_out :1834-1836) ===
Increment sites (exhaustive):
- routes/search.rs:800 - single-index path, AFTER the cache block: observes plan.shard_to_node.len() (node_count, :797). A cache hit returns at :545 BEFORE this line -> a hit observes nothing.
- routes/search.rs:1438 - multi-target alias path (search_multi_targets), same post-planning position; that path never touches the result cache at all (guard :481, and no lookup/store below :589).
Semantics: _count = scatter EXECUTIONS (1 per scatter regardless of width); each observed VALUE = planned shard->node assignments (16 under the suite's shards:16/RF:1 topology -> bucket 20; p13_13 reads only _count, never _sum/buckets). Planning failure returns 503 at :778-781 BEFORE :800 -> no observation.
CAN catch: cache serving without short-circuiting the fan-out (the pairing partner for hits/misses); repeat query leaking past the cache.
CANNOT distinguish: single-index scatter from multi-target-alias scatter (same unlabeled histogram); a fan-out whose nodes all failed; width 1 vs width 16 in _count (only _sum/buckets would); anything about cache state when the cache block was skipped (multi-target/disabled/coalesced).

=== 4. Cache key derivation - what acceptance_5's misses == 3 actually counts ===
Key = DefaultHasher (SipHash) u64 of (index_uid, canonicalized-query-string, settings_version) - result_cache.rs:80-88. No collision guard: a u64 collision serves another query's rows and no counter moves.
Canonicalization = recursive key-sort + compact serialize (result_cache.rs:289-322): insensitive to key ORDER only; sensitive to absent-vs-null, array order, whitespace, extra keys.
settings_version = S13.5 global settings-broadcast version, read at lookup (search.rs:483) and RE-read at store (search.rs:932). Mid-request commit stores under the NEW version while the content was merged pre-commit - a subsequent hit under the new key can serve pre-change rows (no counter distinguishes this; relevant to acceptance_9).
CRITICAL DIVERGENCE (verified by executing a faithful replica of both derivations): single-index lookup canonicalizes the PARSED SearchRequestBody (search.rs:486-488) - fields have no skip_serializing_if (search.rs:133-143), so it always emits q/offset/limit/filter/facets and rankingScore:null when the client omits it. The store path REBUILDS the body from body.rest (search.rs:806 -> :827 -> :936-953): q/offset/limit/filter are re-extracted from the serde-flatten remainder, which does NOT retain named-field keys, so they serialize as null; and rankingScore is forced to Some(...) (:951). For {q:laptop,limit:10}:
  lookup canon: {"facets":null,"filter":null,"limit":10,"offset":null,"q":"laptop","rankingScore":null}
  store  canon: {"facets":null,"filter":null,"limit":null,"offset":null,"q":null,"rankingScore":false}
Keys differ for EVERY body shape tested (including one with explicit rankingScore). Consequence: on POST /search the store key never matches any later lookup key - hits can NEVER increment on this path, every request increments misses and runs a full scatter, and the store side is degenerate (all facet-less bodies collapse to one LRU key). Direct consequences for acceptance_1..5: hits==1 (a1/a2/a3), hits==4 (a4), hits==1 (a5), hits==1 (a10) and fan-out _count==1 (a1/a2/a4) can never pass; a5's misses==3 actually counts 4 (4 lookups x 1 miss) - misses counts LOOKUPS, not distinct keys, so ==3 is only correct if the repeat can hit, which it cannot. Contrast: the multi-search path builds its cache JSON symmetrically from the same cloned query at lookup and store (multi_search.rs:335-341 vs :540-546, clone at :453) - key parity holds there; p13_11's suite is not affected by this finding.

=== 5. TTL / no-refresh-on-hit (acceptance_4 and acceptance_7 lean on this) ===
ttl_ms: 500 pinned in the suite's generated yaml (p13_13 test :179); default 500/1000-entry (miroir-core/src/config.rs:37-38 doc, asserted :758-759). Cache instance shared via AppState (admin_endpoints.rs:1043-1045).
expires_at = now + ttl fixed at INSERT (result_cache.rs:45-50; Duration::from_millis(config.ttl_ms) at :170-171). The hit path (result_cache.rs:150-153) never touches expires_at - no refresh-on-hit (LRU recency does move on hit, affecting eviction order only). Expiry is lazy, checked only on access (result_cache.rs:141-148): expired entry is popped and counted an internal miss, the route sees Ok(None) and increments the Prometheus miss (search.rs:556). No background sweeper - a stale entry occupies LRU capacity until touched. acceptance_4's hits==4 additionally assumes 5 sequential HTTP round-trips complete within 500ms of the first insert; if the sweep fixes the key divergence, that window becomes load-bearing (a local-container stall fails it as misses==5/hits==0, indistinguishable from a TTL-too-short regression).

=== 6. Dead-but-adjacent telemetry (do not lean assertions on these) ===
set_result_cache_size (middleware.rs:1856-1858) and inc_result_cache_evictions (:1860-1862) have NO callers outside their definitions - miroir_result_cache_size and miroir_result_cache_evictions_total are permanently 0/absent-value regardless of cache health. ResultCache::stats() internal hits/misses/evictions (result_cache.rs:216-234) are consumed nowhere in the proxy. The test helper metric() takes the first line whose prefix matches and parses (p13_13 :305-320); prometheus crate exports no _created series here, and histogram _bucket/_sum lines fail the f64 parse for a _count query, so prefix collision is not a live hazard.

SWEEP IMPLICATIONS (for miroir-48954e4a): the never-fire hazard in acceptance_1..5 is not only tautologies - several bounds are UNSATISFIABLE (can never pass) because of the lookup/store key divergence in S4. Any replacement bound that assumes hits can fire on POST /search is dead until that divergence is fixed; a5's misses==3 documents a 'distinct keys' property misses cannot express (it counts lookups). acceptance_7/9's hits==0 assertions pass trivially today for the same reason and would become load-bearing only post-fix.

## Phase 9 Epic — Testing

Delivers the plan §8 test suite: unit tests in `miroir-core` with coverage gate, integration tests with docker-compose (3-node Meilisearch + Miroir), API-compatibility tests against real Meilisearch, chaos tests, performance benches with criterion, and SDK smoke tests in four languages.

## Why A Phase, Not Just Per-Feature

Tests *within* each feature are written by Phase 1/2/4/5. This phase:

- Stands up the test **harness** (docker-compose, testcontainers, fixtures) that every other phase reuses
- Implements the cross-cutting suites (compatibility, chaos, SDK smoke) that can't live inside any single feature
- Locks down the coverage + perf gates before v1.0 per plan §8 coverage policy

## Scope (plan §8)

**Unit tests** (`cargo test --all`)
- Router correctness suite (determinism, minimal reshuffling, uniform distribution, RF>1 placement)
- Merger suite (global sort, offset/limit after merge, score stripping, facet counts, estimatedTotalHits)
- Task registry (persistence across open/close, status aggregation, TTL prune)
- Primary key extraction (missing → reject, string/int values, nested paths)
- `miroir-core` coverage ≥ 90% measured via `cargo-tarpaulin`, reported in CI, gates merges from v1.0

**Integration tests** (`tests/integration/`, `--test-threads=1`)
- docker-compose with 3 Meilisearch nodes + Miroir
- Document round-trip, search-covers-all-shards, facet aggregation, offset/limit paging, settings broadcast, task polling, node failure with RF=2

**API-compatibility tests**
- Run same scenarios against a real single-node Meilisearch vs. Miroir; assert semantic equivalence
- Every Meilisearch error code replayed against both, assert identical `{message,code,type,link}` shape
- `examples/sdk-tests/` in **Python, JavaScript, Go, Rust** — create/index/search/settings/delete round-trip
- Against both `docker-compose-dev.yml` and a plain Meilisearch instance

**Chaos tests** (`tests/chaos/`, manual/scripted)
- Kill 1 of 3 nodes (RF=2) — continuous search; degraded writes warn via header
- Kill 2 of 3 nodes (RF=2) — shard loss; 503 or partial per policy
- Kill 1 of 2 Miroir replicas — zero client-visible downtime
- `tc netem delay 500ms` on one node — search slows, no errors
- Restart a killed node — Miroir detects within health interval
- Kill a node mid-rebalance — pause + resume; no data loss

**Performance benchmarks** (`benches/`, criterion)
- Rendezvous (64 shards, 3 nodes, 10K docs) < 1 ms total
- Merger (1000 hits, 3 shards) < 1 ms
- End-to-end search latency < 2× single-node
- Ingest throughput > 80% single-node
- CI comment when a PR increases p95 by > 20% vs. last release

## Dependencies

This phase cannot finish until Phase 2 (integration tests need a running proxy), Phase 4 (chaos tests need rebalance), and Phase 5 (compatibility suite exercises §13 features). But the **harness** (docker-compose files, testcontainers fixtures, CI wiring) can and should be stood up early.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Full `cargo test --all` green on iad-ci Argo Workflow
- [ ] `miroir-core` coverage ≥ 90%, published as a CI artifact
- [ ] Every Meilisearch error code in plan §5 table verified byte-identical in the compat suite
- [ ] All 4 SDK smoke tests pass against docker-compose-dev
- [ ] All 6 chaos scenarios documented with runbooks in `tests/chaos/`
- [ ] Benches green against the targets in plan §8
- [ ] PR-latency check bot posts delta vs. last release

## What

Plan §8 "Unit tests" + "Coverage policy":
- Stand up `cargo test --all` in CI (Phase 8 pipeline already runs this)
- Integrate `cargo-tarpaulin` for line coverage; gate merges from v1.0 at ≥ 90% `miroir-core` coverage
- Publish coverage report as a CI artifact (HTML + XML)
- Add a PR comment showing coverage delta

## Why

Plan §8 "Coverage policy" explicitly requires ≥ 90% on `miroir-core` with CI gating from v1.0 forward. Without this, the coverage target is aspirational; with it, drops below 90% fail merges.

## Details

**Why 90% on miroir-core specifically**: `miroir-core` is the pure library — routing, merging, topology. Easy to reach ≥ 90% because there's no I/O. Dropping below 90% usually means a new code path wasn't tested, which is exactly what a unit-test gate is for.

**No coverage gate on miroir-proxy / miroir-ctl**: those have I/O, handlers, and main loops that require integration tests. Plan §8 asks for "integration test coverage for happy paths and key error paths" rather than a percentage.

**Tarpaulin invocation**:
```bash
cargo tarpaulin --workspace \
  --exclude-files 'crates/miroir-proxy/*' 'crates/miroir-ctl/*' \
  --out Html --out Xml --output-dir target/tarpaulin/
```

**PR comment**: use `actions/upload-artifact` equivalent in Argo — artifact is accessible via `https://argo-ci.ardenone.com/workflows/.../artifacts/...`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] First green CI run publishes a tarpaulin report
- [ ] PR that drops coverage below 90% fails the gate
- [ ] Report diffable across commits (operators see which lines stopped being covered)

**Delta computation**: compare current PR's bench output vs. the most recent `main` run's stored bench output. `critcmp` is the typical tool.

**Gating vs. commenting**: plan §8 says "review comment," not "block merge." Keep the tool advisory — operators trigger reruns for transient noise.

**End-to-end search latency bench** needs a running docker-compose stack; run as part of integration benches, not unit benches.

issue.description:
Owns crates/miroir-proxy/tests/p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs — the sole target keeping 'cargo test --workspace' red in the current chain (10 failing tests, classified (b) by miroir-d33b1d88 because the file carries an ownerless uncommitted guard edit that miroir-faf5bccb is contractually barred from touching; disposition handed off here per that triage).

TWO independent defects, both verified 2026-09-10:

1. No graceful docker skip. Every test does CacheFlowTestSetup::new().await.unwrap()/expect(), and setup calls check_docker_available() first (the uncommitted guard) — on any host without /var/run/docker.sock all 10 tests panic instead of skipping. Repo convention is skip-on-Err (eprintln + return), as landed in docker_compose_integration.rs, p10_7_admin_login_rate_limit.rs, p13_21_search_ui_rate_limit.rs and, as of a3f5fc3, p5_1_f_reshard_progress_integration.rs. Convert setup to return the skip signal and have each test skip on it.

2. Broken container invocation — the tests fail in EVERY environment, docker or not. Each test starts 3 nodes via Meilisearch::default().with_cmd(["--master-key=key{i}"]). testcontainers 0.23 with_cmd REPLACES the container Cmd; the getmeili/meilisearch:v1.8.3 image has Entrypoint [tini --] and Cmd [/bin/sh -c /bin/meilisearch], so the container runs 'tini -- --master-key=key0' and dies: reproduced on podman 5.4.1 — '[FATAL tini (2)] exec --master-key=... failed: No such file or directory'. Fix by dropping with_cmd and using the module env API (testcontainers-modules 0.11 Meilisearch::with_master_key) — or with_cmd(["--http-addr", ...]) style args appended AFTER the binary via a full cmd. Note p5_1_f's Meilisearch::default() (no cmd override) starts fine, so the image itself is healthy.

Evidence: full --no-fail-fast run 2026-09-10, /home/coding/scratch/miroir-test-logs/03-faf5bccb-nofailfast.log — 78 targets, only these 10 (p13_13, 0 passed 10 failed) plus 2 in p5_1_f fixed by miroir-faf5bccb in a3f5fc3. Until this bead lands, cargo test --workspace cannot exit 0 in any tree state, so it blocks the chain's final green run (miroir-ad7f62a0) and miroir-645bc884's re-walk. dockerless hosts: skip (convention). With docker: after fix 2 the 10 tests should genuinely run (3 Meilisearch nodes per test — 30 starts; consider trimming, but not required).
issue.notes:
READY-STATE RESULT from miroir-55edb26a (full-suite run, runtime up) — node readiness PASSES everywhere; the remaining blocker is proxy startup, with exact diagnosis below so you can fix in one edit.

Run: systemctl --user start podman.socket; DOCKER_HOST=unix:///run/user/$(id -u)/podman/podman.sock cargo test -p miroir-proxy --test p13_13_cache_flow_integration → 0 passed / 10 failed in 308s. Every panic is at the post-setup wait_for_ready().unwrap() (lines 329/404/465/529/588/673/719/779/847/921), which structurally proves CacheFlowTestSetup::new() returned Ok in all 10 tests, i.e. all 30 Meilisearch node starts (10 tests x 3 nodes) passed the testcontainers wait strategy. Had any node start failed, setup would have returned Err and the test would have hit the skip branch ('Skipping test:', repo convention) instead of panicking. The with_cmd fix from miroir-65b9802c is verified live: no tini FATAL, nodes healthy.

Defect #3 (new, blocks all 10 post-ready): the config generated by proxy_config_yaml (p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs:139) fails MiroirConfig::validate, so the spawned miroir-proxy exits 1 immediately and wait_for_ready times out at 30s in every test. Reproduced manually with the test's exact YAML: 'Error: Failed to load config: validation error: cdc.buffer.overflow = \'redis\' requires task_store.backend = \'redis\''. Root cause: defaults cdc.enabled=true (config/advanced.rs:30 area) and cdc.buffer.overflow='redis' (config/advanced.rs:456 Default), and the validate rule at crates/miroir-core/src/config/validate.rs:56-58 rejects overflow=redis unless task_store.backend=redis; the suite pins sqlite (single-writer constraint, see its own topology comment). Fix shape (verified on this box): append one stanza to proxy_config_yaml — 'cdc:\n  buffer:\n    overflow: drop' — after which the proxy started and /health returned {"status":"available"} within ~6s against the p13diag-meili node. After that lands, expect the real cache-flow assertions to run; those results are yours.

Also for your ledger (residue carried from miroir-65b9802c): crates/miroir-proxy/tests/integration_test.rs:29 still builds nodes with with_cmd([--master-key=keyN]) — same tini defect, outside p13_13 scope. TEMPORARY proof artifact p13_13_node_invocation_proof.rs was DELETED by miroir-55edb26a per its decision (suite itself is the regression test; fix-site comment records the tini signature).

issue.description:
Confirm that the miroir-write-policy exists in OpenBao on ardenone-cluster and grants write on the miroir key paths, before any token is minted and bound to it. Second link in the split of umbrella bf-416qo. Note: the read-only miroir-policy was already verified under closed bead bf-3ll0r; the write policy is a separate artifact.

Steps:
1. Using the working cluster-admin kubeconfig from miroir-2c5e342d, reach the OpenBao service (kubectl port-forward svc/<openbao> 8200:8200 -n <namespace> or the established route) and point the bao CLI at it.
2. Authenticate to OpenBao with cluster-admin/root access obtained through the established setup channel. Do not persist that credential anywhere in git.
3. Run: bao policy read miroir-write-policy (or confirm presence via bao policy list).
4. Check coverage: the policy must grant create/update (write) on ardenone-cluster/miroir/keys and ardenone-cluster/miroir-dev/keys — using the KV v2 data/metadata path layout of the actual mount.
5. If the policy is absent: author it (HCL granting write plus read on both key paths, default-deny everything else), save it next to docs/operations/openbao-policy.hcl as a documented write-policy variant, and apply it with: bao policy write miroir-write-policy <file>

## Acceptance Criteria
- miroir-write-policy exists in OpenBao (bao policy read succeeds), or was authored and applied within this bead
- Policy grants write (create/update) on both ardenone-cluster/miroir/keys and ardenone-cluster/miroir-dev/keys
- Policy is default-deny elsewhere: no wildcards beyond those two path families
- Bead comments capture the policy read output (policy HCL is not a secret and may be recorded)

## Notes
Reference docs/operations/openbao-policy.hcl and docs/operations/secrets-setup.md for path and capability conventions.

issue.notes:
ROUND-11 CHILD 2 — GET /indexes NODE-PROCESS SCOPING + ROUTE-VS-TASK (miroir-90a6044f, 2026-09-13). Read-only static verification in /home/coding/miroir; NO source files modified by this bead. All cites re-checked fresh against the working tree @ HEAD 316b0ec. Pre-existing dirty set (other workers / harness, untouched here): routes/search.rs, tests/p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs (+ new p13_22 test), CHANGELOG.md, Dockerfile, k8s yaml, .beads internals — NONE of the files cited below are dirty, so every cite is valid for HEAD and the working tree identically.

SCOPE: the lock set held IN THE WEDGED PROXY PROCESS — the single miroir-proxy process hosting the wedged POST /search/:index parked forever in state.topology.read().await (search.rs:667 in the current dirty tree / search.rs:656 @ HEAD 316b0ec; that delta is the foreign in-flight diff, not a coordinate error).

=== CLAIM 1 — GET /indexes -> 200 in 259us: LOCKS NONE in the proxy ===

VERDICT: lock conclusion CONFIRMED (empty lock set in the proxy). The claim's mechanism wording "served by the NODE process" is DRIFT — corrected below — without changing the lock or scoping conclusion.

- The route EXISTS on the proxy: `.nest("/indexes", indexes::router::<UnifiedState>())` (main.rs:850) -> indexes::router (indexes.rs:304-330) -> `.route("/", post(create_index_handler).get(list_indexes_handler))` (indexes.rs:309). GET /indexes is handled by the proxy process; it is not bypassed to the node.
- Handler `list_indexes_handler` (indexes.rs:471-492) extracts ONLY `Extension(config): Extension<Arc<Config>>` (472-473) — no State/AppState, hence no topology.read, no session_manager, no query_coalescer/result_cache, no Redis. It builds a fresh MeilisearchClient per request (474; reqwest Client with a 10s timeout, indexes.rs:63-70), picks `config.nodes.first()` (475-478; 503 if empty), and awaits ONE outbound GET {node}/indexes with the node master key (479-481). 2xx -> parse the node JSON; parse failure degrades to {"results":[]} but STILL returns 200 (486-488); transport error -> 500 (482-485); non-2xx -> the node's status is forwarded (490-491). The outbound call is the handler's only await.
- Middleware on this path is lock-free in the proxy: csrf_middleware skips safe methods (auth.rs:929-932); auth_middleware does NOT dispatch-exempt /indexes (is_dispatch_exempt auth.rs:546-594 lists /health, /version, /_miroir/ready, locale fetches, admin/login, ui-search session, SPA entry — no /indexes entry), so dispatch_bearer runs (auth.rs:722-775): pure computation over &AuthState (auth.rs:201-213 — Strings, SealKey, and one DashMap touched only on the admin cookie flow, unreachable here). A valid bearer is required or the request 401s before routing; the observed 200 is the authenticated branch. request_id/session_pinning are header-only; telemetry uses prometheus atomics (middleware.rs:1683-1785; InFlightGuard at middleware.rs:1716) and never holds an app lock across an await.
- MECHANISM DRIFT (the same correction round-10 recorded, re-confirmed at current HEAD): "served by the NODE process" is false as literal mechanism — the proxy registers, authenticates, and serves the response; the node only PRODUCES the index list. Corrected reading: proxied by the proxy's lock-free list_indexes_handler to the first configured node.
- SCOPING CONCLUSION CONFIRMED: node-side locks (Meilisearch-internal index/LMDB locks) live in the node's OS process — a DIFFERENT process from the wedged miroir-proxy — and therefore cannot HOST the proxy park; the park is a tokio task parked at search.rs:667/656 topology.read INSIDE the proxy process. Supporting contrast from source: this handler's outbound await is bounded by the client's 10s timeout (indexes.rs:65), so even a hung node could not reproduce the search's unbounded park. The 259us figure itself is cycle-5 capture evidence (empirical, not statically derivable) and is consistent with a healthy local node round-trip through this handler.

=== CLAIM 2 — ROUTE-VS-TASK TRAP: /health ROUTE vs health-checker BACKGROUND TASK ===

They are distinct tokio tasks in the same process with DISJOINT lock sets, in both directions. The route and the task SHARE NOTHING.

- THE ROUTE: `.route("/health", get(health::get_health))` (main.rs:842) -> `get_health` (health.rs:22-26): ZERO extractors (no State, no Extension), ZERO await points, returns the constant {"status":"available"}. Each request is a fresh per-request tokio task running csrf -> auth (dispatch-exempt: auth.rs:548 -> next.run auth.rs:828) -> extensions -> session_pinning -> request_id -> telemetry -> handler, acquiring NO app lock anywhere.
- THE TASK: `run_health_checker` (fn signature main.rs:943) spawned ONCE at startup via tokio::spawn (main.rs:398-400). Per tick: `interval.tick().await` (main.rs:954; interval built at 944-945 from health.interval_ms); takes `state.topology.write().await` (main.rs:956 — the SOLE topology.write in main.rs; tokio RwLock per admin_endpoints.rs:39 import and :422 field `pub topology: Arc<RwLock<Topology>>`) and HOLDS that guard across the ENTIRE tick body: per-node /health probes each bounded by health.timeout_ms (main.rs:973-988), metrics updates, `mark_ready().await` (main.rs:1098), and `session_manager.prune_expired().await` (main.rs:1110 -> session_pinning.rs:318-320, taking sessions.write + pending_writes.write NESTED under the still-held topology write guard), releasing only at loop-body scope exit (main.rs:1114).
- SHARED NOTHING, both directions: the route touches none of the task's state (no topology, no session manager); the task reads nothing the route writes (the route writes nothing at all). Consequences: a 200 from GET /health is NOT evidence the background task is alive, and nothing sent to /health can release or observe the task. In the wedged process the checker task is ITSELF parked at topology.write().await (main.rs:956) behind the wedged reader (tokio RwLock, write-preferring) — it holds nothing, so it does not block /health; it is simply wedged too.
- Boundary of the shared-nothing class: /version (health.rs:29-35, zero-parameter) is in it; GET /_miroir/ready is NOT — `get_ready` takes State and awaits `state.topology.read().await` (health.rs:40-47), the one control probe that WOULD contend with the checker's write guard in the wedge.

=== COORDINATE DRIFT (explicit) ===

1. "main.rs:943 tick" — 943 is the run_health_checker fn SIGNATURE (exact as a fn cite); the actual `interval.tick().await` is main.rs:954 (+11); the interval is constructed at main.rs:944-945.
2. "topology.write main.rs:956" — EXACT, and it is the sole topology.write in main.rs (guard held to main.rs:1114).
3. "prune_expired main.rs:1110" — EXACT; definition at miroir-core session_pinning.rs:318.
4. "~200ms cadence" — the tick fires every health.interval_ms; the code DEFAULT is 5000ms (config.rs:248; timeout default 2000ms at config.rs:249). ~200ms is the p13_13 HARNESS override (scripts/p13-13-first-search-capture.sh:352 `interval_ms: 200`, :353 `timeout_ms: 1000`); the integration test leaves health interval/timeout at their serde defaults (tests/p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs:248-252). The "per miroir-51d281e7" attribution carries no cadence authority — round-10 already recorded that misattribution; that bead's note records coordinates, not cadence.
5. "GET /indexes served by the NODE process" — mechanism drift (proxied by the proxy's lock-free handler, not node-served; route exists at indexes.rs:309 under the main.rs:850 nest); the LOCKS-NONE and different-process scoping conclusions are unchanged.
6. Context coordinate: the wedged-park cite is search.rs:667 in the current dirty tree vs search.rs:656 at HEAD 316b0ec (foreign in-flight diff to that file; none of this note's other cited files are dirty). Minor: get_version is health.rs:29-35 (round-10 cited 27-33).

NET: GET /indexes holds an EMPTY lock set in the wedged proxy process — its fast 200 during the wedge is fully explained by source (nothing shared with the parked search, and the node answering proves node liveness); the /health ROUTE and the health-checker TASK share nothing, so route liveness is not task liveness. Both round-10 conclusions survive re-derivation at current HEAD 316b0ec; the only drift is the re-confirmed mechanism wording plus the tick/cadence cites itemized above.

issue.description:
Second link in the split of miroir-db6d2741 (after the precondition check in miroir-c54fda5b). Mint the dedicated least-privilege writer token — the cluster-admin/root credential must not be used for the population work itself — and persist it exactly once. Minting and storing share this bead so the token id never needs an insecure handoff between steps.

Steps:
1. With OpenBao cluster-admin access, run:
   bao token create -policy=miroir-write-policy -ttl=168h -explicit-max-ttl=336h -orphan -renewable -format=json
   (7-day ttl, renewable up to a 14-day hard ceiling; -orphan detaches it from the issuing token. docs/operations/secrets-setup.md sets no separate convention for this writer token — its ttl=24h applies to the kubernetes auth role for ESO reads — so keep 168h/336h.)
2. mkdir -p ~/.openbao && chmod 700 ~/.openbao
3. Write the token id once to ~/.openbao/miroir-writer.token — pipe it from the create output without echoing it — then chmod 600 ~/.openbao/miroir-writer.token. The path is outside any git worktree.
4. Verify permissions only: stat -c '%a' ~/.openbao/miroir-writer.token prints 600. Record the accessor (safe to handle) and the stat output in a bead comment — never the token id.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Token created with -policy=miroir-write-policy, -ttl=168h, -explicit-max-ttl=336h, -orphan, -renewable

issue.notes:
VERDICT: RULED OUT. The search.rs working-tree diff (26+/58-) cannot produce a non-2xx on the first search POST. Signature A's actual cause is a route contract mismatch: the suite POSTs to /indexes/{uid}/search, a route the proxy has never registered (it serves POST /search/:index). Live-reproduced 404 below.

== 1. Diff hunks (all five), search request/response path relevance ==

Hunk 1 (~line 486, insertion before the cache-lookup block):
    +    let mut result_cache_key: Option<miroir_core::result_cache::CacheKey> = None;
Pure declaration. No behavior.

Hunk 2 (~line 514, inside the existing lookup block):
    +            result_cache_key = Some(cache_key.clone());
Infallible capture of the lookup-time key. On a first-search miss the lookup returns Ok(None) (unchanged arms) and execution proceeds to scatter exactly as before.

Hunk 3 (~line 813, comment + deletion):
    -    let facets_for_cache = body.facets.clone(); // Additional clone for cache storage
Removes a clone that only the deleted store block consumed. No behavior change.

Hunk 4 (~line 837, deletion):
    -    let capture_body_for_cache = rest_body.clone(); // Additional clone for cache storage
Same. No behavior change.

Hunk 5 (~lines 936-955, the ~50-line rewrite): the old post-scatter store block (re-derive SearchRequestBody, re-canonicalize, re-compute CacheKey with a fresh settings_version read, insert) is replaced by:
    +    if let Some(cache_key) = result_cache_key {
    +        if let Ok(response_bytes) = serde_json::to_vec(&body) {
    +            match state.result_cache.insert(cache_key, response_bytes).await {
    +                Ok(_) => { debug!(index = %effective_index, "result cached successfully"); },
    +                Err(e) => { debug!(error = %e, "failed to store result in cache"); }
Every path is error-swallowed: `if let Some`, `if let Ok`, insert errors -> debug!. No `?`, no unwrap/expect, no early return, no panic source. The block runs after the response content is determined and feeds only the cache store - the nearest status decisions (503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE at search.rs:790, 500 at search.rs:910, 200 OK at search.rs:1008) are outside every hunk. Semantic change is cache-correctness only (store under the lookup-time key/version so a mid-request settings commit invalidates, instead of re-deriving both post-scatter).

Why not even a panic could yield the observed signature: a handler panic drops the connection, and the test would die at `.send().await.unwrap()` with an Err-unwrap message. The observed `assertion failed: resp.status().is_success()` requires a well-formed non-2xx HTTP response - i.e. the proxy deliberately answered 4xx/5xx.

== 2. Actual cause of signature A: route mismatch (confirmed) ==

The test calls (p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs:496-507, assert at 508):
        .post(format!("{}/indexes/products/search", setup.proxy_url))
The proxy registers search ONLY at POST /search/:index:
  - crates/miroir-proxy/src/routes/search.rs:128: `.route("/:index", axum::routing::post(search_handler))`
  - crates/miroir-proxy/src/main.rs:852: `.nest("/search", search::router::<UnifiedState>())`
indexes::router (crates/miroir-proxy/src/routes/indexes.rs:304-330) registers /, /:index, /:index/stats, /:index/settings(+/settings/*subpath), /:index/_preflight, /:index/explain, /:index/documents - NO /:index/search. `git log -S ':index/search' -- .../indexes.rs` is EMPTY: the route never existed in history. `/indexes/products/search` (two segments under the /indexes nest) matches no route -> axum 404.

LIVE REPRODUCTION against a miroir-proxy running on 127.0.0.1:17770 (pid 1716428, started 06:37 by the parent-bead diag, cwd /tmp/p13diag-1ec135a1; its upstream node 17831 has a `products` index):
    POST /indexes/products/search  ->  HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
                                       x-request-id: 39aeaca4
                                       content-length: 0
Empty body = router 404 (middleware ran, no route matched), NOT a propagated upstream index_not_found (that would be JSON). Cross-check: POST /search/products on the same process was ACCEPTED by the router (request accepted; that diag-owned process hangs scattering rather than answering - irrelevant to this diagnosis).
The proxy itself uses the /indexes/{uid}/search style only for OUTBOUND scatter calls to real Meilisearch nodes (main.rs:710-714: `let url = format!("{}/indexes/{}/search", address.trim_end_matches('/'), index_uid)`). The suite is calling the proxy with the upstream-style URL.
Scope note: 23 call sites across the test tree use the same `{proxy}/indexes/.../search` style (grep post(format!) - 18x products, 2x {}, 2x books, 1x proxy_url variant) - all 404 identically. Fix direction is the parent bead's call: either the tests move to POST /search/{index}, or the proxy gains a Meilisearch-compatible POST /indexes/:index/search route (given 23 call sites and the proxy's Meilisearch-compatible facade intent, the route is the likelier intent).     test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 10 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 14.25s

- Upstream node error: excluded - create_index/add_documents hit the same containers directly and succeeded before the first search (their failure mode is anyhow::bail, which would print "Skipping test"/bail text, not the 508 assert); an upstream-propagated error would carry a JSON body.

## Phase 2 Epic — Proxy + API Surface

Wires the Phase 1 primitives into a live HTTP proxy. After this phase, a client pointing a Meilisearch SDK at `http://miroir:7700` can CRUD indexes, write documents, search, and poll tasks — with documents actually sharded across nodes.

## Why This Sits Here

Plan §1 principle 1 (**invisible federation**) and plan §5 (**API Surface and Compatibility**) are the product. Phase 1 gave us math; this phase turns the math into behavior a Meilisearch client sees as drop-in. Every downstream phase assumes these HTTP surfaces exist and return shapes that match the Meilisearch spec exactly, so §8 "API compatibility tests" can pin the contract from here on.

## Scope (plan §3 Lifecycle + §5 API Surface)

- `axum` server listening on `server.port` (default 7700) and metrics on 9090
- **Write path** (plan §2 write path) — hash primary key, inject `_miroir_shard`, fan out to `RG × RF` nodes, per-group quorum (`floor(RF/2)+1`), `X-Miroir-Degraded` on any group missing quorum, 503 `miroir_no_quorum` only when no group met quorum for a shard
- **Read path** (plan §2 read path) — pick group via `query_seq % RG`, build intra-group covering set, scatter, merge by `_rankingScore`, strip `_miroir_shard` always + `_rankingScore` if client didn't request, aggregate facets + estimatedTotalHits, report max processingTimeMs, group-fallback when a covering set has holes
- **Index lifecycle** (plan §3) — create broadcasts + atomically injects `_miroir_shard` into `filterableAttributes`; settings sequential apply-with-rollback (§3 legacy; §13.5 replaces in Phase 5); delete broadcasts; stats aggregate `numberOfDocuments` + merge `fieldDistribution`
- **Tasks** — per plan §3 task ID reconciliation; `GET /tasks`, `GET /tasks/{uid}`, `DELETE /tasks/{uid}`
- **Error shape** — every error matches Meilisearch `{message,code,type,link}`; new `miroir_*` codes per plan §5
- **Reserved fields contract** — `_miroir_shard` always-reserved; `_miroir_updated_at` / `_miroir_expires_at` reserved only when their feature flag is on (Phase 5)
- **Auth** — master-key/admin-key bearer dispatch per §5 "Bearer token dispatch" rules 2–5; JWT path stubbed (Phase 5)
- **/health + /version + /_miroir/ready + /_miroir/topology + /_miroir/shards** + **/_miroir/metrics** (admin-key gated mirror of port 9090 /metrics per plan §10)
- **Middleware** — structured JSON log per plan §10; Prometheus metrics (`miroir_request_duration_seconds`, etc.)
- **Scatter-gather dispatcher** — per-node retries with orchestrator-side retry cache keyed by `sha256(batch || target_node || idempotency_or_mtask)` (plan §4 note on `scatter.retry_on_timeout`)

## Out of Scope (moved to later phases)

- Two-phase settings broadcast (→ Phase 5 / §13.5)
- Persistent task store (→ Phase 3)
- Rebalancer (→ Phase 4)
- Any §13 feature (→ Phase 5)
- Multi-replica coordination / Redis / HPA (→ Phase 6)

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Integration test: 1000 documents indexed across 3 nodes, each retrievable by ID (plan §8)
- [ ] Integration test: unique-keyword search finds every doc exactly once (plan §8)
- [ ] Integration test: facet aggregation across 3 color values sums correctly (plan §8)
- [ ] Integration test: offset/limit paging preserves global ordering (plan §8)
- [ ] Integration test: write with one group completely down still succeeds on remaining group and stamps `X-Miroir-Degraded`
- [ ] Error-format parity test: every `invalid_request`/`not_found`/`document_*` code matches Meilisearch output byte-for-byte on equivalent input
- [ ] `GET /_miroir/topology` matches the shape in plan §10

issue.description:
## What

Flesh out `miroir-proxy::main`:
- Load `Config` (file + env + CLI args overlay)
- Initialize tracing (JSON-to-stdout per plan §10 log format)
- Start two axum listeners: `:7700` (client API) + `:9090` (metrics, unauthenticated, pod-internal)
- Signal handlers for graceful shutdown (SIGTERM → stop accepting new requests → drain in-flight → exit)
- Implement: `GET /health`, `GET /version`, `GET /_miroir/ready`, `GET /_miroir/topology`, `GET /_miroir/shards`, `GET /_miroir/metrics`

## Why

These are the minimum-viable endpoints Kubernetes needs to probe and operators need to inspect. `GET /health` is Meilisearch-compatible — the K8s liveness probe — and must return 200 immediately regardless of internal state (Meilisearch semantics). `GET /_miroir/ready` is the readiness probe and *blocks* 503 until a covering quorum is reachable on first startup (plan §10).

## Details

**`/health`** (plan §10) — returns `{"status":"available"}`. Never gate on internal state.

**`/version`** — per plan §5 "Orchestrator-local": return the Meilisearch version from any healthy node. Cache at ~60s TTL.

**`/_miroir/ready`** — 503 during startup; 200 once Miroir has loaded config + verified a covering quorum of nodes is reachable. This is specifically where the "there's at least one full covering set somewhere in the topology" check lives.

**`/_miroir/topology`** — shape exactly per plan §10 JSON sample: `shards`, `replication_factor`, `nodes[]` with `id/status/shard_count/last_seen_ms[/error]`, `degraded_node_count`, `rebalance_in_progress`, `fully_covered`.

**`/_miroir/shards`** — shard → node mapping table for the current topology (useful for runbooks and for §13.20 explain).

**`/_miroir/metrics`** — admin-key-gated mirror of port 9090 `/metrics`. Same data; admin-authenticated so it can be exposed outside the cluster.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `curl localhost:7700/health` returns 200 within 100ms of process start
- [ ] `curl localhost:7700/_miroir/ready` returns 503 until all configured nodes are reachable, then 200
- [ ] `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" localhost:7700/_miroir/topology | jq .` matches the plan §10 shape
- [ ] SIGTERM drains in-flight requests (test by sending signal during a long-running search)

issue.description:
## What

Implement:
- `POST /indexes/{uid}/documents`
- `PUT /indexes/{uid}/documents`
- `DELETE /indexes/{uid}/documents/{id}`
- `DELETE /indexes/{uid}/documents` (by IDs array or filter)

## Why

Plan §2 "Write path" is the heart of the product. Four properties that MUST be right:

1. **Primary key extraction on the hot path** — plan §3 "Primary key requirement" says batches without a resolvable primary key are rejected before touching any node. This is a cheap, up-front check and a big UX win.
2. **`_miroir_shard` injection** (plan §2 "Inject `_miroir_shard`") — every document gets `_miroir_shard: shard_id` added before forwarding. Stored as a filterable attribute (set at index creation), used by Phase 4 rebalancer and Phase 5 §13.8 anti-entropy for targeted shard retrieval. Stripped from all API responses.
3. **Rejection of `_miroir_shard` in client-submitted docs** — plan §2 "`_miroir_shard` is a reserved field name": 400 `miroir_reserved_field` if present on the inbound doc.
4. **Two-rule quorum** (plan §2):
   - Per-group quorum = `floor(RF/2) + 1` ACKs from that group's RF nodes
   - Write success if ≥ 1 group met its per-group quorum; `X-Miroir-Degraded` header if ANY group missed
   - HTTP 503 `miroir_no_quorum` only if NO group met its per-group quorum for a given shard

## Details

**Per-batch grouping** (plan §3 "Ingest (add/replace)"): group documents by target node set so each node gets exactly one HTTP request containing all the docs it owns. This minimizes HTTP fan-out count (critical at scale).

**Retry-on-timeout** (plan §4 "Note on `scatter.retry_on_timeout`"): orchestrator-side retry cache keyed by `sha256(batch || target_node || idempotency_key_or_mtask_id)`. When a timeout retries, check the cache first; if the prior dispatch has a cached terminal response, return it rather than creating a duplicate node-side task.

**Delete-by-filter** (plan §5 "Broadcast to all nodes"): cannot be shard-routed; broadcast to every node.

**Delete-by-IDs array**: route each ID to its shard independently (same routing as the write path).

## Acceptance (plan §8)

- [ ] 1000 docs indexed via POST — every doc fetch-by-id returns the same doc
- [ ] Docs distribute across all configured nodes (no node holds < 20% under RF=1/3-node)
- [ ] Batch with one missing primary key → 400 `miroir_primary_key_required`, no docs written anywhere
- [ ] Doc containing `_miroir_shard` → 400 `miroir_reserved_field`
- [ ] RG=2, RF=1, 1 group down: write to 1 group succeeds with `X-Miroir-Degraded: groups=1`
- [ ] RG=2, RF=1, both groups down: 503 `miroir_no_quorum`
- [ ] DELETE by IDs array [docA, docB] with docA on shard 3, docB on shard 7 produces 2 independent per-shard delete calls

issue.description:
## What

Implement `POST /indexes/{uid}/search`:
1. Pick group = `query_seq % RG` (plan §2)
2. Build intra-group covering set (plan §4 `covering_set`)
3. Fan out search to each node in covering set **with `showRankingScore: true` appended** (plan §2 read path step 4)
4. Each node must return up to `offset + limit` results (plan §2 read path "offset/limit")
5. Use P1.4 `merge` to collapse shard hits → single response

## Why

Read latency == max shard latency. This is where hedging (§13.2), adaptive replica selection (§13.3), and query coalescing (§13.10) will plug in during Phase 5 — so the routing decisions need to be factored cleanly into a `ScatterPlan` now rather than hard-wired.

## Details

**`showRankingScore: true` is injected unconditionally** so the merger can global-sort. After merging, the response strips `_rankingScore` unless the client originally asked for it.

**Partial unavailability** (plan §3 `unavailable_shard_policy: partial`, default): if a shard is fully unavailable, return best-effort hits with `X-Miroir-Degraded: shards=3,7,11`. `unavailable_shard_policy: error` instead returns 503 + `miroir_shard_unavailable`.

**Group-unavailability fallback** (plan §2 "Group unavailability fallback"): if the selected group has a shard with no available intra-group RF replica, Miroir optionally falls back to a different group for **that query** (full result, different group).

**Facets** — plan §2 step 7: sum per-value counts across the covering set.

**`estimatedTotalHits`** — sum across covering set.

**`processingTimeMs`** — max across covering set.

## Acceptance (plan §8)

- [ ] Unique-keyword search across 3 nodes returns exactly 1 hit (proves merger + fan-out correctness)
- [ ] Facet counts sum correctly across shards
- [ ] Paging: 5 pages of 10 = single limit=50 order, no dupes/gaps
- [ ] With one node down and RF=2: search still covers all shards (tests fall-back within the group)
- [ ] With one group fully down: search uses the other group; response is not `X-Miroir-Degraded`
- [ ] `X-Miroir-Degraded: shards=...` stamped when a shard has zero live replicas

issue.description:
## What

Implement:
- `POST /indexes` — create index; broadcast to every node; atomically adds `_miroir_shard` to `filterableAttributes`
- `PATCH /indexes/{uid}` — settings updates; sequential apply-with-rollback (legacy strategy; §13.5 two-phase broadcast replaces in Phase 5)
- `DELETE /indexes/{uid}` — broadcast
- `GET /indexes/{uid}/stats` + `GET /stats` — fan out, sum `numberOfDocuments`, merge `fieldDistribution`
- `POST /keys`, `PATCH /keys/{key}`, `DELETE /keys/{key}` — broadcast

## Why

**Plan §3 "Index lifecycle"**: create must broadcast, every node creates the same index with the same settings. Partial creation is rolled back. Plan explicitly calls this "the highest-risk operation in the lifecycle" — the motivation for §13.5. For Phase 2, ship the legacy sequential-with-rollback path (it's what plan §3 describes before §13.5).

**Crucial subtlety**: plan §3 says index creation "additionally broadcasts a settings update to add `_miroir_shard` to `filterableAttributes` on every node — this is required for efficient rebalancing." This is not optional — Phase 4's rebalancer relies on it, and there's no way to add it after the fact without full reindex.

## Details

**Create rollback**: if any node fails, `DELETE /indexes/{uid}` on all previously-created nodes. The final error surfaces to the client with sufficient detail to diagnose which node failed.

**Settings sequential**:
1. Apply to node-0, verify via `GET /indexes/{uid}/settings`
2. Apply to node-1, verify
3. ... all nodes
4. On failure: revert all previously applied nodes to the pre-change settings snapshot

**Settings bucket under `__reserved_settings` for §13.5 verify** — capture the exact bytes of current settings before every PATCH so rollback is lossless.

**Delete-by-filter** — broadcast; note that this is a document endpoint, but the code path joins here.

**Stats aggregation**:
- `numberOfDocuments` — sum across all nodes (duplicates per-replica across RG×RF; divide by (RG × RF) to get logical doc count)
- `fieldDistribution` — sum per-field counts across nodes

## Acceptance

- [ ] `POST /indexes` creates an index on every node; failure on any node rolls back
- [ ] Settings broadcast sequential: a mid-broadcast node failure reverts all previously applied nodes
- [ ] `_miroir_shard` is in `filterableAttributes` immediately after index creation (verified via `GET /indexes/{uid}/settings`)
- [ ] `GET /indexes/{uid}/stats` `numberOfDocuments` = logical count (not replica-multiplied)
- [ ] `/keys` CRUD broadcasts; all-or-nothing (atomic across nodes)
issue.title: P2.4 Index lifecycle endpoints: create/update/delete + settings broadcast

issue.description:
## What

Implement plan §3 "Task ID reconciliation":
- Every write fan-out collects per-node `taskUid` values
- Generate a Miroir task ID `mtask-<uuid>`
- Persist `mtask → {node_id: node_task_uid}` in the in-memory task registry (Phase 3 makes it durable)
- Return `mtask-xxxxx` to client as `{"taskUid": ...}` in Meilisearch shape
- `GET /tasks/{mtask_id}` polls every mapped node task, aggregates:
  - `succeeded` — all nodes report `succeeded`
  - `failed` — any node reports `failed`; include the per-node error detail
  - `processing` — otherwise
- `GET /tasks?statuses=...` — list across all mtasks with Meilisearch-compatible query params

## Why

Clients (SDKs) use the Meilisearch task API as-is. Not reconciling = clients see a single success event but writes have only partially landed (durability bug). Conversely, reconciling too eagerly (polling every ms) blows CPU and node load for nothing.

## Details

**Polling cadence**: exponential backoff per mtask: 25 ms → 50 → 100 → ... cap at 1s. Stop polling once terminal.

**Retention**: default 7 days, pruned by Mode A rendezvous-partitioned pruner (Phase 6 §14.5). Until Phase 3, retention is in-memory only.

**Error aggregation**: if any node fails, present a compact Meilisearch-shaped error but include per-node breakdown as `error.details`.

**`GET /tasks`** (Meilisearch-compatible filters): `statuses`, `types`, `indexUids`, `from`, `limit`. Must paginate across mtasks consistently.

**`DELETE /tasks/{mtask_id}`** — cancel if possible (delegate to Meilisearch; may no-op if Meilisearch doesn't support cancel on that type).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Fan-out to 3 nodes → all 3 `taskUid`s captured in one mtask
- [ ] `GET /tasks/{mtask_id}` while all nodes are processing → `processing`
- [ ] One node fails → status `failed`, error includes per-node breakdown
- [ ] In-memory registry survives the request's own lifetime (Phase 3 makes it persistent)
issue.title: P2.5 Task ID reconciliation and /tasks endpoints


And every `miroir_*` code from plan §5:
- `miroir_primary_key_required`
- `miroir_no_quorum`

## Why

Plan §8 API compatibility: "Test every expected Meilisearch error code against both real Meilisearch and Miroir." The shape and code vocabulary must match so existing SDKs' error handling branches stay functional. Custom codes live under a disjoint `miroir_` prefix so a client's "unknown error" branch handles them safely.

## Details

**Error type enum**: `invalid_request`, `auth`, `internal`, `system` — mirroring Meilisearch categories. Each `miroir_*` code maps to one of these.

**Error struct**:
```rust
#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error, serde::Serialize)]
pub struct MeilisearchError {
    pub message: String,
    pub code: String,   // e.g. "miroir_no_quorum" or "document_not_found"
    #[serde(rename = "type")]
    pub error_type: ErrorType,
    pub link: Option<String>,
}
```

- 400: primary_key_required, reserved_field
- 401: invalid_auth, jwt_invalid
- 403: jwt_scope_denied
- 409: idempotency_key_reused, multi_alias_not_writable

- [ ] HTTP status codes match the plan §5 mapping

issue.description:
## What

Implement the bearer-token dispatch chain from plan §5 "Bearer token dispatch":

0. **Dispatch-exempt check** — if (method, path) is in the exempt list, run handler directly
1. **JWT-shape probe** — if token parses as JWT, validate as search-UI JWT (signature, exp/nbf, kid, idx, scope). Parseable-but-invalid → 401 `miroir_jwt_invalid`. Signature-valid but scope mismatch → 403 `miroir_jwt_scope_denied`. Phase 5 §13.21 adds the JWT validation; Phase 2 stubs this to "not-a-jwt → next step"
2. **Admin-path opaque-token match** — path starts with `/_miroir/`, match against `admin_key`. Exempt: `/_miroir/metrics`, `/_miroir/ui/search/locale/*`, `POST /_miroir/admin/login`, `GET /_miroir/ui/search/{index}/session`
3. **Master-key match** — other paths → `master_key`
4. **Mismatch** → 401 `miroir_invalid_auth`
5. **Dispatch-exempt endpoints** — exhaustive list in plan §5 rule 5

Plus: `X-Admin-Key` short-circuit for admin endpoints.

## Why

Plan §5: "Three token types can appear on `Authorization: Bearer <value>` simultaneously — the `master_key`, the `admin_key`, and a search UI JWT. Miroir resolves them deterministically." Without a consistent dispatch chain, Phase 5 §13.21's JWT path conflicts with admin/master key on the same header. Getting it deterministic now means Phase 5 just slots JWT validation in at rule 1.

## Details

**Rule 0 list** (needs to be kept in sync with §5 table 5):
- `GET /_miroir/metrics` — admin-key-optional
- `GET /_miroir/ui/search/locale/*` — unauthenticated
- `POST /_miroir/admin/login` — credentials in body
- `GET /_miroir/ui/search/{index}/session` — auth per `search_ui.auth.mode`
- `GET /ui/search/{index}` — public SPA

**Constant-time comparison**: use `subtle::ConstantTimeEq` for all opaque-token comparisons to prevent timing side-channels.

**Rate-limit hooks**: wire in `miroir:ratelimit:adminlogin:<ip>` and `miroir:ratelimit:searchui:<ip>` bucket counters from Phase 3 task store; Phase 2 may keep in-memory until Phase 6 multi-pod.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Every row in plan §5 rule 5 exempt list has a unit test (request does NOT match admin_key / master_key)
- [ ] Opaque token on `/_miroir/*` matches only admin_key; never master_key
- [ ] Opaque token on other paths matches only master_key; never admin_key
- [ ] Missing Authorization on auth-gated endpoints → 401 `miroir_invalid_auth`
- [ ] `X-Admin-Key` alone gates admin endpoints equivalently to Bearer admin_key
- [ ] Constant-time compare: test with timing-injection harness shows no measurable delta between "wrong length" and "wrong bytes"
issue.title: P2.7 Auth: bearer-token dispatch (plan §5 rules 0-5) + X-Admin-Key

## What

Implement `miroir-proxy::middleware`:
- Request ID generation (UUIDv7 prefix short-hashed) attached as `X-Request-Id` on every response
- Structured JSON log per plan §10 shape (timestamp, level, message, index, duration_ms, node_count, estimated_hits, degraded)
- Prometheus histogram: `miroir_request_duration_seconds{method, path_template, status}`
- Counter: `miroir_requests_total{method, path_template, status}`
- Gauge: `miroir_requests_in_flight`
- Scatter metrics: `miroir_scatter_fan_out_size`, `miroir_scatter_partial_responses_total`, `miroir_scatter_retries_total`
- Node metrics: `miroir_node_healthy`, `miroir_node_request_duration_seconds`, `miroir_node_errors_total`

## Why

Phase 7 builds dashboards and alerts on these exact metric names. Defining them here (not at Phase 7) means every P2.X feature already emits the right signals without retrofit.

**`path_template` (not `path`)** is critical: `/indexes/{uid}/search` is a template; substituting actual values produces high-cardinality labels that OOM Prometheus. Axum provides the matched route template via `MatchedPath` extractor.

## Details

**Log format** (plan §10 exact shape):
```json
{
  "timestamp": "2026-05-01T12:00:00.000Z",
  "level": "info",
  "message": "search completed",
  "index": "products",
  "duration_ms": 42,
  "node_count": 3,
  "estimated_hits": 15420,
  "degraded": false
}
```

Logs go to stdout, one JSON object per line. Use `tracing-subscriber` with `fmt::layer().json()`.

**In-flight gauge**: increment on request start, decrement via `Drop` guard so even panics decrement correctly.

**Metrics server on `:9090`**: separate axum listener from the client API; no auth (bound to cluster network); `/metrics` returns prometheus exposition format.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `curl localhost:9090/metrics` returns all listed metrics with ≥ 1 sample after a single request
- [ ] `jq` parses every log line without error
- [ ] Request ID appears in response header and in the log entry for that request
- [ ] High-cardinality defense: `path_template` never contains a UUID or arbitrary UID
issue.title: P2.8 Middleware: structured logging + prometheus metrics + request IDs
