issue.notes:
Read-only static verification; no files changed. Tree state: HEAD 316b0ec, branch main, 19 dirty porcelain entries — none of the cited files (main.rs, routes/health.rs, middleware.rs, auth.rs, miroir-core/config.rs, session_pinning.rs, capture script) are dirty, so working tree == HEAD for every cite below. All coordinates re-read fresh from source.

== The route-vs-task trap for /health (wedged-proxy-process terms) ==

The /health ROUTE and the health-checker BACKGROUND TASK are different tokio tasks with disjoint lock sets, in both directions.

- The ROUTE is per-request: axum spawns a fresh task per request; for GET /health that task runs csrf -> auth -> Extensions -> session_pinning -> request_id -> telemetry middleware and then get_health, acquires NO lock, and returns the constant {"status":"available"} (health.rs:21-23 — the handler body has zero await points; it cannot even yield).
- The TASK is the single long-lived loop spawned once at startup (tokio::spawn at main.rs:398-400 -> run_health_checker, main.rs:943). Each tick it takes state.topology.write() (main.rs:956) and holds that guard across the WHOLE tick body — per-node probes, metrics, mark_ready().await (:1098), prune_expired().await (:1110) — releasing only at loop-body scope exit (main.rs:1114, implicit; no drop()). The guard is re-acquired fresh next tick; interval.tick().await (:954) runs unguarded.

In the wedged-proxy process: the wedge is a request-handler task parked holding topology.read() (search.rs:667) forever. On the checker's next tick, THAT task parks inside topology.write().await at main.rs:956 behind the wedged reader (tokio RwLock, write-preferring) and stays there. Hitting GET /health does nothing for it: the route path never touches topology, sessions, or pending_writes, so /health keeps returning 200 from a constant string while the checker task is wedged. Therefore a 200 from /health is NOT evidence the background task is alive, and nothing sent to /health can release the task (the route writes nothing the task reads). Vice versa: the task reads nothing the route writes, so a wedge hypothetically parked in the /health path would be neither releasable nor observable from the task side. The one probe that DOES contend with the task's write guard is GET /_miroir/ready — get_ready takes state.topology.read() (health.rs:46) and would hang behind a mid-tick-wedged checker; that contention does not reach the /health route.

== Coordinates vs cited (drift listed) ==

- Route wired, CITED main.rs:842 — EXACT, no drift: .route("/health", get(health::get_health)), first route on the main Router::new().
- Interval tick, CITED main.rs:943 — DRIFT: 943 is the run_health_checker fn signature (exact as a fn cite). The interval is constructed at 944-945 (tokio::time::interval(Duration::from_millis(state.config.health.interval_ms))); the actual interval.tick().await is at main.rs:954, inside loop { at 953. Tick statement is +11 lines from the cite.
- topology.write, CITED main.rs:956 — EXACT, no drift: let mut topo = state.topology.write().await; (sole topology.write in the file; tokio write guard held to :1114).
- prune_expired, CITED main.rs:1110 — EXACT, no drift: let pruned = state.session_manager.prune_expired().await; (def at session_pinning.rs:318; takes sessions.write + pending_writes.write while the topology write guard is held — the nesting miroir-51d281e7 recorded).

== Cadence correction (attribution drift) ==

"Every ~200ms per miroir-51d281e7" is misattributed: miroir-51d281e7's note records coordinates, not cadence. From source: the tick fires every health.interval_ms, DEFAULT 5000ms (config.rs:248, verified); 200ms is the p13_13 HARNESS override (scripts/p13-13-first-search-capture.sh:352 interval_ms: 200, verified; :353 timeout_ms: 1000 vs default 2000 at config.rs:249). So ~200ms only under the capture harness; 5000ms with default config. The p13_13 test file itself states health interval/timeout stay at serde defaults (tests/p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs:248).

== Shared-nothing, justified from source ==

ROUTE side — no lock anywhere on the request path (outermost->innermost per main.rs:858-866 and the .layer calls at :869-894):
1. get_health() (routes/health.rs:20) takes ZERO parameters — no State extractor, hence no reference to any shared structure; body is a struct literal with zero awaits. Compile-time evidence, not a runtime observation.
2. csrf_middleware (auth.rs:925): GET passes through immediately (auth.rs:930-933) before any auth/redis state access.
3. auth_middleware (auth.rs:822): is_dispatch_exempt(GET, /health) == true (auth.rs:546-548, "unauthenticated liveness probe") -> next.run immediately (auth.rs:827-829); seal/revocation-cache code unreachable.
4. Extension layers (main.rs:880-883): insert config + Arc<state.admin> into request extensions only.
5. session_pinning_middleware (middleware.rs:170-184): parses X-Miroir-Session into request extensions; never touches session_manager.
6. request_id_middleware: stateless header middleware.
7. telemetry_middleware: the ONLY shared leaf — it writes the same prometheus Metrics registry the task updates inside the guard (main.rs:1081-1091) — but prometheus counters/gauges are atomic-backed, not a std/tokio lock; it can neither wedge nor be wedged.

TASK side locks: topology.write (:956, held to :1114), and INSIDE the guard: sessions.write + pending_writes.write via prune_expired (session_pinning.rs:318), sessions.try_read via session_manager.update_metrics, ready.write via mark_ready (admin_endpoints.rs:1050, per miroir-51d281e7), rebalancer.metrics.read via sync_rebalancer_metrics_to_prometheus. The /health path acquires NONE of these — route and task share no lock.

Boundary of the shared-nothing class: /health and /version (get_version, also zero-parameter, health.rs:27-33) are in it; /_miroir/ready is NOT (topology.read at health.rs:46 contends with the task's :956 write guard).

Precision note vs child 2 (miroir-c54e3c22): its note lists the middleware order as "telemetry -> ... -> csrf" in runs-first order; per the source comment (main.rs:858-866, "last layer() call = outermost") csrf is outermost and telemetry innermost. Immaterial to the lock conclusion — every layer passes GET /health through without acquiring the task's locks — but recorded for coordinate hygiene.

=================================================================
STAGE-13 CONSOLIDATED VERDICT + PER-ROUTE LOCK-SHARING ANSWER
(child 4 of 4, miroir-6f43ee2e, 2026-09-12; consolidates the fresh
reads on miroir-b5b1243f [hold span + writer cadences],
miroir-c8554648 [sync-tail cites + arm argument], miroir-93084356

=================================================================

CONSOLIDATED AGAINST: HEAD 32dffe10c73e550e482bce288d9ae2753cf6a367,
the shared dirty working tree (foreign in-flight edits unchanged
across all three children's passes; routes/search.rs is the only
DIRTY cited file — see drift item G). This child independently
spot-checked the load-bearing coordinates on that tree (hold span,
health-checker write span + tick/probe cites, config defaults,
capture-script harness values, admin x6, all three sync-tail cites,
route registrations, handler signatures, tokio version) — all exact
at the stated lines; remaining fine-grained cites rest on the
children's fresh same-tree reads.

-----------------------------------------------------------------
1. STAGE-13 VERDICT: KEEP THE SPLIT — PARK-INSIDE-THE-HOLD
-----------------------------------------------------------------

The /search/products park sits INSIDE the topology.read() hold
(search.rs:667 -> drop(topo) :917, dirty-tree lines; clean-HEAD
equivalents 656/908), not in acquire contention. VERDICT UNCHANGED.

Grounds, freshly re-read:

- THE HOLD. `let topo = state.topology.read().await;` at search.rs:667,
  explicit `drop(topo);` at :917 ("Drop topology lock before building
  response"), spanning planning, the whole scatter-plan build, and the
  whole DFS call (dfs_query_then_fetch_search :901-904). The lock is
  tokio RwLock (state.rs:22 `pub topology: Arc<RwLock<Topology>>`;
  workspace tokio 1.52.3 per Cargo.lock — the 0.1.22 entry is a legacy
  transitive), which is write-preferring/fair: a pending write blocks
  NEW read acquisitions, so a genuinely stuck-held write WOULD queue
  later /search acquires. That is what makes the acquire arm testable
  against the writer cadence, and it fails the test (below).

- WRITER CADENCE (freshly re-read). The only cross-await runtime writer
  is the health checker: run_health_checker (decl main.rs:943, spawned
  main.rs:398-400), `interval.tick().await` :954, then
  `state.topology.write().await` :956 with the guard held across the
  WHOLE tick body — probe send().await :988, gauges 1080-1091,
  sync_rebalancer_metrics :1094, mark_ready 1096-1099,
  prune_expired().await :1110, guard released by implicit scope-end
  ~1114 (no explicit drop(topo) anywhere in main.rs). Admin writers x6
  (crates/miroir-proxy/src/routes/admin_endpoints.rs
  1801/1919/1966/2057/2567/2903 — each `topology.write().await`
  re-verified exact) are ALL await-free under their guards and did not
  fire mid-wedge (zero admin calls in the captures). Rebalancer writes
  are event/job-driven and GroupSync is interval-polled but takes NO
  runtime topology.write at all (its 3 write sites are test-only) —
  zero writes on the stable single-node harness topology either way.

- PROBE BOUND (freshly re-read). The probe client is built per-tick
  inside the per-node loop as reqwest::Client::builder()
  .timeout(Duration::from_millis(state.config.health.timeout_ms)) at
  main.rs:974 — a per-probe total-request deadline on the health
  client, under the write guard. (main.rs:702 is the CANARY client
  timeouted on scatter.node_timeout_ms, default 5000ms — misattributed
  in the audit; drift item B.)

- HARNESS vs DEFAULTS, stated separately:
  * HARNESS: tick 200ms (scripts/p13-13-first-search-capture.sh:352
    `interval_ms: 200`), probe bound 1000ms (:353 `timeout_ms: 1000`);
    single-node topology (one node-0).
  * DEFAULTS: tick 5000ms (crates/miroir-core/src/config.rs:248
    `interval_ms: 5000`), probe bound 2000ms (:249
    `timeout_ms: 2000`).
  Worst-case write hold in the harness is therefore ~1s per dead node
  per tick (sub-ms with the node live — proven mid-wedge by the node
  serving GET /indexes in 259us), so a queued reader is served within
  about one tick + one probe bound (~1.2s absolute worst case, ~200ms
  with the node live).

- WHY THE VERDICT HOLDS. The ACQUIRE arm requires the write side to be
  pinned for the whole park — i.e. the 1s harness probe deadline never
  fires — on the same runtime whose timer wheel demonstrably kept
  spinning through every wedge: RUN B served /health 200 at t+0.9s and
  /nope 404 at t+0.95s after the control arrived, and again at
  t+40/82/115s; background WARN ticks carrying the wedge's ambient
  /search/:index span kept firing at ~5/min through the 4m27s park. A
  fired probe deadline would not even be silent: "node marked Degraded"
  (main.rs:1052) on first failure, "node marked Failed" (:1059) at
  threshold. Census across all 9 archived wedge-window proxy logs:
  ZERO miroir.node warns and ZERO node-marked warns in every one. No
  probe deadline ever fired mid-wedge, so every write hold resolved
  within its bound — irreconcilable with parks of 15s (TERM-bound),
  121s, and 4m27s. The ACQUIRE arm is inconsistent with the evidence.

  The HOLD arm is consistent: everything awaited under the hold was
  already cleared by the L1-L12 consolidated work (uncontended freq-0
  writers, ns-scale holds), the DFS await at :904 has every internal
  leg 5s-bounded (client.rs:25) with INFO-visible expiry, and after the
  last await on each path the tail is fully SYNCHRONOUS — the three
  cites in section 2, all confirmed. No await in the tail means no
  timer can fire inside it: no warn, no completion line, the span stays
  entered (exactly the ambient-span signature on the background WARN
  lines in the captures), and the parked worker spawns no replacement
  (only block_in_place would; Threads constant at 12) while the
  remaining workers serve /health and /nope in single-digit ms.

  SCOPE (must travel with the verdict): this is CONSISTENCY, not
  mechanism. The verdict locates the park inside the hold and proves
  no deadline exists there; it does not explain why finite synchronous
  work fails to return. The falsifier — mid-wedge node-log probe
  cadence (probes STOP => checker frozen on topology.write; probes

  correctly framed as NEVER-RUN: an open experiment, evidence for
  neither arm today.

-----------------------------------------------------------------
2. THE THREE SYNC-TAIL CITES — confirmed / corrected
-----------------------------------------------------------------

[C1] merger.rs:96 — CONFIRMED (attribution note, not a correction of
substance). crates/miroir-core/src/merger.rs:96 is the trait-method
DECLARATION `fn merge(&self, input: MergeInput) ->
Result<MergedSearchResult>;` inside `pub trait MergeStrategy` (94-100):
no async in the signature, so no await is even expressible across the
call. Production body: RrfStrategy::merge :152 -> rrf_merge :231, pure
CPU over owned data; the file greps zero Mutex/RwLock/lock/park/sleep/
spawn. Called at core scatter.rs:1123 in the sync tail after that
function's only await (:1089).

[C2] client.rs:143 — CONFIRMED EXACT. crates/miroir-proxy/src/client.rs:143
is `serde_json::from_str(&body_text)`, the FINAL statement of
`async fn search_node` (decl :73, body closes :145), sitting after its
only two awaits — send().await :104-105 and text().await :117-119. No
.await, no timeout, and OUTSIDE the reqwest client-level total-request
deadline (client.rs:25, node_timeout_ms 5s default): once text()
resolves, parse + return run unbounded, and the target=miroir.node
"node call failed" warn (:106-114) fires only on send() error — a hang
here is log-silent. File is miroir-proxy (miroir-core has no client.rs).

[C3] scatter.rs:1192 — CONFIRMED WITH SYMBOL-RESOLUTION CORRECTION.
The cite is the CALL SITE `Ok(GlobalIdf::from_preflight_responses(
&responses))` at crates/miroir-core/src/scatter.rs:1192 — last
statement of `pub async fn execute_preflight` (1149-1193), following
its only await (join_all :1190, filter_map collect :1191). The
DEFINITION is `pub fn from_preflight_responses(responses:
&[PreflightResponse]) -> Self` at core scatter.rs:70 — non-async, pure
CPU (totals accumulation, HashMap term_df fold, per-term ln()), no
lock, no I/O, no timer. crates/miroir-proxy/src/scatter.rs (266 lines)
contains NO GlobalIdf/from_preflight symbol at all — a proxy-file
reading of this cite would be wrong.

-----------------------------------------------------------------
3. PER-ROUTE LOCK SHARING (lock set in the WEDGED PROXY process)
-----------------------------------------------------------------

NET ANSWER: all four mid-wedge-completing probes take NO lock in the
wedged proxy process — none of the 18 audited lock sites (miroir-6028604d)
is touched by any of them. What the completions positively establish is
timer/reactor/worker liveness, nothing more.

- GET /health -> 200 (cycle 5 00:13:02.996957Z; RUN B t+0.9/40/82/115s)
  — LOCKS: NONE. Registered main.rs:842 `.route("/health",
  get(health::get_health))`; handler get_health
  (crates/miroir-proxy/src/routes/health.rs:22-26) has an EMPTY
  parameter list — no State extractor, no Extension — so no lock
  acquisition is even expressible; it returns a static
  HealthResponse{status:"available"}. The full middleware stack every
  request passes through is lock-free (grep zero for
  RwLock|Mutex|.read().await|.write().await|lock() across middleware.rs
  + auth.rs). Contrast pinned: get_ready (health.rs:40-47) DOES take
  `State(state)` and reads `state.topology.read().await` at :47 — but
  it is mounted only under the /_miroir nest (main.rs:849) and was
  never hit mid-wedge. /health and /_miroir/ready share a file, not a
  lock.
- /nope -> 404 — LOCKS: NONE. No route registered, and the crate's
  single .fallback (search_ui.rs:150) lives inside the /ui/search nest
  (main.rs:856) that /nope never enters: axum's router itself produces
  the 404 and NO application handler runs. Middleware only (telemetry
  client-error WARN branch, middleware.rs:1752-1759).
- POST /indexes/products/search -> 404 — LOCKS: NONE. The /indexes
  nest (main.rs:850) is completely enumerated at indexes.rs:304-330:
  there is NO "/:index/search" route and no fallback on the nest, so
  the probe 404s at the nested router without entering any handler.
  The WEDGED request is a sibling-nest URL — /search nest (main.rs:852)
  whose router is the single route "/:index" POST search_handler
  (routes/search.rs:128), the only one of these routes wired to app
  state: it takes `Extension(state): Extension<Arc<AppState>>`
  (routes/search.rs:175) and is the only execution that can reach the
  18 audited lock sites. The probe URL never reaches it.
- GET /indexes -> 200 in 259us — LOCKS: NONE in the wedged proxy
  process. The event is the proxy's drift reconciler making an OUTBOUND
  call to the node (run() loop :131 -> check_and_repair_all_indexes
  :167 -> list_indexes :322-355 in
  crates/miroir-core/src/rebalancer_worker/drift_reconciler.rs — that
  file is lock-free end to end, 401 lines, grep zero for locks/
  topology; wired as Arc<miroir_core::rebalancer_worker::DriftReconciler>
  at admin_endpoints.rs:442, tokio::spawn main.rs:482-488). The serving
  route lives in the NODE process — different binary, different address
  space — so node-side locks cannot host the proxy's park. (The proxy
  also has its own GET /indexes route at indexes.rs:309, but the
  observed 259us event was node-side; the row's lock set is {} either
  way.)

ROUTE vs TASK — the /health trap, explicit: the /health ROUTE is
get_health (health.rs:22-26, registered main.rs:842) — stateless,
lock-free, executed on demand by an ordinary worker thread. The
health-checker BACKGROUND TASK is run_health_checker (decl main.rs:943,
tokio::spawn :398-400): every tick (:954) it takes topology.write()
(:956), holds the guard across the whole tick body, and touches
sessions via prune_expired().await (:1110) — every 200ms harness
cadence (5000ms default). The route and the task share NOTHING: the
route never touches topology or sessions; the task never runs the
route's handler. A mid-wedge /health 200 therefore proves
reactor/timer/worker liveness ONLY and says nothing about whether the
checker's write side is progressing. (Whether topology.write()
progresses mid-wedge is exactly the never-run falsifier in section 1.)

-----------------------------------------------------------------
4. COORDINATE DRIFT (consolidated from all three children plus this
   child's spot-check; nothing absorbed silently; NO substantive
   drift — every item is line-number, filename, or attribution
   precision)
-----------------------------------------------------------------

A. main.rs write-span sub-cites: gauges audit 1084-1090 -> actual
   1080-1091; sync_rebalancer_metrics audit :1096 -> actual :1094;
   mark_ready audit 1101-1103 -> actual block 1096-1099 (.await :1098);
   guard drop audit ~1116 -> actual ~1114 and IMPLICIT (scope end of
   the tick loop body), not an explicit drop(topo).
B. main.rs:702 misattributed as the health client — it is the CANARY
   execution client timeouted on scatter.node_timeout_ms (:701-705,
   default 5000ms). The health-probe client timeout cite is main.rs:974
   only.
C. main.rs:943 is the `async fn run_health_checker` DECLARATION; the
   actual `interval.tick().await` is :954 (loop opens :953). The other

Shared-nothing boundary: includes /version, excludes GET /_miroir/ready (takes topology.read, health.rs:46).

issue.notes:
VERIFIED AND RESTATED (child 2 of 5, re-split of miroir-0cc8350c; read-only — no source files changed). Re-verified every cite directly against the tree at HEAD 316b0ec with the same dirty file child 1 saw (routes/search.rs uncommitted diff, touching no coordinate this bead relies on). Runtime evidence timestamps (cycle 5, RUN B) are observation cites restated as recorded; everything else below is freshly checked against source.

SCOPING RULE: every lock set below is the set held IN THE WEDGED PROXY PROCESS — the process whose POST /search/:index handler (req abf9606e) is parked forever in state.topology.read() (search.rs:667 worktree = search.rs:656 HEAD, +11 from the dirty diff; tokio RwLock per admin_endpoints.rs:39/422, write-preferring). The :9090 metrics server (main.rs:901/911/917-919) is a separate router with no middleware and is never touched by main-port requests. No concurrency-limiting layer exists in the crate (child 1 grep: no Semaphore/LoadShed/ConcurrencyLimit/TimeoutLayer), so there is no shared admission lock either.

== 1. GET /health -> 200 — LOCKS NONE in the wedged proxy process (CONFIRMED) ==
Evidence: cycle 5 00:13:02.996957Z (req 81f0188f); RUN B answered at t+0.9/40/82/115s.
- Handler: get_health (health.rs:22-26, wired main.rs:842) takes NO extractor at all — empty parameter list, no State, no Extension — and has ZERO await points (body is a struct literal returning the constant {"status":"available"}); it cannot even yield.
- Middleware for this route (outermost->innermost per the main.rs:858-868 comment; wiring main.rs:869-895), all lock-free here: csrf_middleware (def auth.rs:925, wired 889-895) returns next.run immediately for GET/HEAD/OPTIONS (auth.rs:930-932) before any admin/Redis work; auth_middleware (def auth.rs:822, wired 885-888) dispatch-exempts GET /health via is_dispatch_exempt (def auth.rs:546, GET /health branch 548-550) -> next.run (auth.rs:827-828); session_pinning_middleware (middleware.rs:170, wired 877-879) is header-only; request_id_middleware (middleware.rs:138, wired 876) is header-only; telemetry_middleware (def middleware.rs:1683, wired 869-875) has only State<TelemetryState> (a cloned Metrics handle + pod_id), builds InFlightGuard at :1716, and its sole await is next.run at :1718 — no .read()/.write()/Mutex/lock() anywhere in :1683-1785. The wedged POST holds none of these (it only incremented requests_in_flight at entry, middleware.rs:1716).

== 2. /nope -> 404 — LOCKS NONE on BOTH branches (CONFIRMED, scope condition stated) ==
Evidence: cycle 5 00:18:30.048403Z, POST /nope, 5 ms, x-request-id present (req 2c9fc976) — the AUTHENTICATED branch.
- Scope condition: "router-level 404" holds ONLY for the authenticated branch. x-request-id on the response proves request_id_middleware — which sits INNER to auth — actually ran, i.e. auth passed the request through; an unauthenticated /nope never reaches routing and carries no x-request-id.
- Authenticated branch: csrf passes (POST + non-admin path -> auth.rs:935-937, before any Redis/session access); auth dispatch Rule 3 master-key match (auth.rs:769) -> Authenticated -> next.run (auth.rs:892) -> router miss -> axum default unmatched-route 404. There is NO .fallback() on the main router: main.rs:841-896 registers none, nothing is added after with_state (main.rs:896; app served as-is at main.rs:914), and the ONLY .fallback( in proxy src is search_ui.rs:150 — GET-scoped serve_spa inside the /ui/search nest (main.rs:856), unreachable from /nope.
- Unauthenticated branch: dispatch Rule 4 — missing bearer at auth.rs:735, mismatch at auth.rs:774 — returns AuthVerdict::InvalidAuth, converted to the response at auth.rs:903-907 (MeilisearchError::new(MiroirCode::InvalidAuth)) -> 401 per MiroirCode::http_status (miroir-core api_error.rs:137). This happens BEFORE routing and lock-free: dispatch is pure string ops + constant-time compares, and the revoked_sessions DashMap (auth.rs:844) sits behind the is_admin_path(&path) gate (auth.rs:839-850) which is false for /nope (is_admin_path = starts_with("/_miroir/"), auth.rs:620-622).

== 3. ROUTE-VS-TASK TRAP (explicit) ==
The /health ROUTE and the health-checker BACKGROUND TASK are different tokio tasks in the same wedged process with disjoint lock sets, in both directions.
- ROUTE: a fresh per-request task per request, wired main.rs:842; lock set EMPTY as in section 1; it terminates after the response. The handler body has zero await points, so it cannot even yield.
- TASK: one long-lived loop spawned once at startup (tokio::spawn main.rs:398-400 -> run_health_checker, fn def main.rs:943). Each iteration: interval.tick().await (main.rs:954; interval built 944-945 from config.health.interval_ms) -> takes state.topology.write() at main.rs:956 and HOLDS that guard across the WHOLE tick body — per-node probes with send().await inside (main.rs:988), node/shard/task/rebalancer metrics (1081-1094), mark_ready().await (main.rs:1098), session metrics (1105-1107), prune_expired().await (main.rs:1110 -> miroir-core session_pinning.rs:318, which takes sessions.write at :319 and pending_writes.write at :320 while the topology write guard is still held) — releasing only at loop-body scope exit (main.rs:1114, implicit drop).
- In the WEDGED process the task is ITSELF parked at ACQUISITION of topology.write() (main.rs:956) behind the wedged reader: tokio RwLock is write-preferring, so the checker's pending write queues behind the wedged POST's read guard (and later read-seekers queue behind the pending writer). The task holds nothing the route wants; the route takes nothing the task holds.
- Consequences, both directions: a 200 from GET /health is NOT evidence the background task is alive; and nothing sent to /health can release or observe the task (the route writes nothing the task reads; the task reads nothing the route writes).
- Shared-nothing boundary: /health and /version are IN it (see drift 3 for /version's corrected mechanism). GET /_miroir/ready is NOT unconditionally in it — see drift 1: its not-ready path takes topology.read via check_covering_quorum (admin_endpoints.rs:1057) and WOULD contend with the wedge/the checker's write guard; its ready path (state.ready.read(), admin_endpoints.rs:1234) does NOT touch topology and would answer without contending. It is the one probe whose behavior in the wedge is path-conditional.

== 4. COORDINATE DRIFT vs the cites in this bead's description (explicit) ==
1. "GET /_miroir/ready takes topology.read, health.rs:46" — DOUBLE DRIFT, conclusion survives via new coordinates. (a) Line: in health.rs the read is at :47 (get_ready def 40-64); :46 is the closing brace of the where clause. (b) Function identity: health.rs::get_ready is DEAD CODE — the file opens with #![allow(dead_code)] (health.rs:2) and the live route is wired to admin_endpoints::get_ready (admin.rs:43; def admin_endpoints.rs:1228-1249). The live handler's topology.read is INDIRECT: check_covering_quorum (admin_endpoints.rs:1056-1070, topology.read at :1057), reached only on the not-ready path (1240), optionally followed by mark_ready (1243) whose ready.write is at :1051. Live-handler lock set: fast path {ready.read :1234}; slow path {topology.read :1057} then possibly {ready.write :1051}.
2. "401 (api_error.rs:137)" — line EXACT, file unqualified: there is NO api_error.rs in miroir-proxy; the file is crates/miroir-core/src/api_error.rs:137 (Self::JwtInvalid | Self::InvalidAuth | Self::MissingCsrf => 401). Proxy-side response construction: auth.rs:903-907.
3. "includes /version" — CONCLUSION HOLDS, inherited mechanism was wrong. The parent table's basis ("health.rs:27-33, also zero-parameter") describes health.rs::get_version, which is dead code (same #![allow(dead_code)]). The WIRED handler is version::get_version::<UnifiedState> (main.rs:843; def version.rs:14-22): it DOES take State<S> (FromRef AppState) and awaits version_state.get_version() (version.rs:20) — fast path takes version_cache.read + last_cache_update.read (admin_endpoints.rs:117-118, released :124); slow path does an outbound node GET with 2s timeout (127-138) then both write guards (:144-145). It NEVER touches state.topology, and its internal cache locks are touched by nothing else in the wedge — so /version does share nothing with the wedged POST or the checker task; it is simply not "zero-parameter/await-free". It is dispatch-exempt (auth.rs:552-554), like GET /health (548-550) and GET /_miroir/ready (558-560).
4. All other description cites are EXACT against the current tree: topology.write main.rs:956; prune_expired main.rs:1110 -> miroir-core session_pinning.rs:318 (def; lock takes at :319-320); no .fallback() on the main router (main.rs:841-896); dispatch Rule 3 auth.rs:769 / Rule 4 auth.rs:735; csrf safe-method return auth.rs:930 (auth.rs:930-932); telemetry lock-free middleware.rs:1683-1785. Uncited coordinates now pinned: route wired main.rs:842; task spawn main.rs:398-400; fn def main.rs:943; tick main.rs:954; mark_ready main.rs:1098; request_id middleware.rs:138; session_pinning middleware.rs:170; /_miroir/ready wired admin.rs:43.
5. Restatement note (same as parent's cross-child precision note): the description lists middleware as "csrf/auth/session/request_id/telemetry" without order; actual run order is csrf outermost -> auth -> Extensions/DefaultBodyLimit -> session_pinning -> request_id -> telemetry innermost (main.rs:858-868 comment, wiring 869-895). Immaterial to every lock conclusion above.

NET: GET /health locks NOTHING in the wedged proxy process (zero-extractor, zero-await handler; every middleware on its path lock-free); /nope locks NOTHING on both branches (authenticated = router miss to axum default 404, the observed one; unauthenticated = lock-free 401 short-circuit before routing); the /health route and the health-checker task share nothing in either direction, and in the wedged process the task is parked at topology.write acquisition (main.rs:956) behind the wedged reader — so a 200 from GET /health is not evidence the task is alive. Corrections vs the given cites: /_miroir/ready's topology contention lives in the live admin_endpoints::get_ready/check_covering_quorum (admin_endpoints.rs:1057), not health.rs:46; api_error.rs:137 is miroir-core's; /version is in the shared-nothing class via VersionState cache locks, not via a dead-code zero-parameter handler.

run_health_checker: spawned main.rs:398-400, def main.rs:943; per tick (config.health.interval_ms) takes AppState.topology : Arc<tokio::sync::RwLock<Topology>> (decl admin_endpoints.rs:422) WRITE @ main.rs:956. ## Phase 7 Epic — Observability + Ops

Ships the metric set, log format, tracing hooks, alert rules, and Grafana dashboard specified in plan §10 + the resource-pressure additions from §14.9.

## Why A Dedicated Phase

Observability accretes badly: if you wire metrics per-feature, you end up with inconsistent naming, duplicate counters, and missing labels. Plan §10 names every metric up front so Phase 5 can depend on a stable registry. This phase makes sure the registry lines up with the plan and the Grafana dashboard reads real data.

## Scope (plan §10 + §14.9)

**Health endpoints**
- `GET /health` — Meilisearch-compatible, used as liveness
- `GET /_miroir/ready` — readiness; 503 until covering quorum reachable
- `GET /_miroir/topology` — full cluster state (shape in plan §10)

**Prometheus metrics** (all prefixed `miroir_`)
- Requests: `miroir_request_duration_seconds{method,path_template,status}` histogram, `miroir_requests_total` counter, `miroir_requests_in_flight` gauge
- Node health: `miroir_node_healthy{node_id}`, `miroir_node_request_duration_seconds{node_id,operation}`, `miroir_node_errors_total{node_id,error_type}`
- Shards: `miroir_shard_coverage`, `miroir_degraded_shards_total`, `miroir_shard_distribution{node_id}`
- Task registry: `miroir_task_processing_age_seconds`, `miroir_tasks_total{status}`, `miroir_task_registry_size`
- Scatter-gather: `miroir_scatter_fan_out_size`, `miroir_scatter_partial_responses_total`, `miroir_scatter_retries_total`
- Rebalancer: `miroir_rebalance_in_progress`, `miroir_rebalance_documents_migrated_total`, `miroir_rebalance_duration_seconds`
- §13.11–21 family groups (all 11 listed in plan §10 "Advanced capabilities metrics")
- §14.9 resource-pressure: `miroir_memory_pressure`, `miroir_cpu_throttled_seconds_total`, `miroir_request_queue_depth`, `miroir_background_queue_depth{job_type}`, `miroir_peer_pod_count`, `miroir_leader`, `miroir_owned_shards_count`

**Ports**
- Port 7700: `/_miroir/metrics` admin-key-gated
- Port 9090: `/metrics` unauthenticated, pod-internal, ServiceMonitor target

**Grafana dashboard** (`dashboards/miroir-overview.json`) — 8 panels per plan §10 + feature-flag-gated panels for §13.11–21 when flags are on

**ServiceMonitor** (plan §10 YAML)

**Alerting** (`PrometheusRule` per plan §10 + §14.9)
- MiroirDegradedShards, MiroirNodeDown, MiroirHighSearchLatency, MiroirTaskStuck, MiroirRebalanceStuck
- MiroirSettingsDivergence (paired with §13.5 reconciler)
- MiroirAntientropyMismatch (paired with §13.8 at 3 consecutive passes)
- MiroirMemoryPressure, MiroirRequestQueueBacklog, MiroirBackgroundJobBacklog, MiroirPeerDiscoveryGap, MiroirNoLeader

**Tracing (optional)** — OpenTelemetry with configurable sample_rate; disabled by default; each search produces one parent span with a child per covering-set node

**Log format** — structured JSON to stdout; schema per plan §10

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Every metric in plan §10 + §14.9 registered and scraping on port 9090
- [ ] `/_miroir/metrics` on port 7700 returns identical data when admin-key-authenticated
- [ ] Grafana dashboard JSON imports cleanly; all 8 core panels render from a live scrape
- [ ] All 12 alerts live in the shipped PrometheusRule manifest
- [ ] OTel trace contains one parent span per request and one child per node call
- [ ] Log entries match the schema verbatim (parseable as JSON)
- [ ] ServiceMonitor picks up the metrics service in a kind cluster test

## What

Register the plan §10 core metric families on `:9090/metrics` AND `/_miroir/metrics` (admin-key gated mirror):

**Requests** (histogram + counter + gauge):
- `miroir_request_duration_seconds{method, path_template, status}`
- `miroir_requests_total{method, path_template, status}`
- `miroir_requests_in_flight`

**Node health**:
- `miroir_node_healthy{node_id}`
- `miroir_node_request_duration_seconds{node_id, operation}`
- `miroir_node_errors_total{node_id, error_type}`

**Shards**:
- `miroir_shard_coverage`
- `miroir_degraded_shards_total`
- `miroir_shard_distribution{node_id}`

**Tasks**:
- `miroir_task_processing_age_seconds`
- `miroir_tasks_total{status}`
- `miroir_task_registry_size`

**Scatter-gather**:
- `miroir_scatter_fan_out_size`
- `miroir_scatter_partial_responses_total`
- `miroir_scatter_retries_total`

**Rebalancer**:
- `miroir_rebalance_in_progress`
- `miroir_rebalance_documents_migrated_total`
- `miroir_rebalance_duration_seconds`

## Why

Plan §10 + Phase 9 dashboard + alerts all depend on these exact names. Naming is a contract — changing them post-v1.0 breaks every downstream dashboard + alert rule.

## Details

**Label cardinality defense**:
- `path_template` MUST be the axum matched path (not the raw URL)
- `node_id` is bounded (~dozens)
- `status` is the HTTP status code (~10s)
- `error_type` is enum-limited (not a raw error string)
- `operation` is the backend call name ({search, documents_post, stats_get, ...})

**Histogram buckets**: use prometheus default buckets for duration histograms unless the plan calls out specifics.

**Port 9090 (unauth, pod-internal)** is the canonical scrape target; port 7700 `/_miroir/metrics` (admin-auth) returns identical data for ad-hoc inspection from outside.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `curl localhost:9090/metrics | grep '^miroir_'` lists every metric name above
- [ ] `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" localhost:7700/_miroir/metrics` returns the same data
- [ ] `path_template` labels contain no UUIDs or dynamic segments
- [ ] A request that hits 3 nodes produces a `miroir_scatter_fan_out_size` histogram sample of 3

- Tenant (§13.15): `miroir_tenant_queries_total{tenant,group}`, `miroir_tenant_pinned_groups{tenant}`, `miroir_tenant_fallback_total{reason}`

**Label cardinality audit**: `{tenant}` and `{index}` are unbounded — document which metrics need dropping to cardinality caps (e.g., top 100 tenants reported individually, rest bucketed as "other"). Decide per metric during implementation; note decisions in feature-specific beads.

issue.description:
## What

Build the plan §10 Grafana dashboard at `dashboards/miroir-overview.json` with 8 panels:
1. Cluster health — degraded shards, node healthy table
2. Request rate — by path template
3. p50/p95/p99 latency
4. Node latency comparison — per-node histogram quantiles
5. Search overhead — Miroir vs. single-node Meilisearch ratio
6. Task lag — stuck task age
7. Shard distribution — imbalance detection
8. Rebalance activity

Plus conditional feature-flag-gated rows for:
- §13.1 resharding in progress + phase gauge
- §13.5 settings broadcast phase + drift repairs
- §13.8 anti-entropy shards scanned, mismatches found, docs repaired
- §13.13 CDC lag, buffer bytes, events by sink
- §13.18 canary pass/fail heatmap
- §13.21 search UI sessions + p95

## Why

Plan §10 + §12 list the dashboard as a delivered artifact. A sample dashboard shipped in the repo means operators don't reinvent it for each install — they import and customize.

## Details

**Prometheus data source**: parametrized via `$datasource` variable so operators point at their cluster's Prometheus.

**Row visibility**: use Grafana's "template variable" controlling row visibility — set automatic via `enabled_feature` label on metrics (or via a separate `miroir_feature_enabled{feature}` gauge) so rows auto-show when scraped.

**Timezone**: default `browser`; 1-minute refresh; 1-hour default time range.

**Import flow**: `helm install` optional `dashboards.enabled: true` creates a ConfigMap with the JSON labeled `grafana_dashboard=1` so Grafana's sidecar auto-imports.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `dashboards/miroir-overview.json` imports into a stock Grafana v10.x without errors
- [ ] Every panel renders data against a live Miroir scrape in Phase 9 integration cluster
- [ ] Feature-gated rows hide when their metrics are absent; show when present

issue.description:
## What

Ship the plan §10 + §14.9 alerting rules via `PrometheusRule` and the metric-scraping via `ServiceMonitor`.

## ServiceMonitor (plan §10)

```yaml
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: ServiceMonitor
metadata:
  name: miroir
spec:
  selector: { matchLabels: { app.kubernetes.io/name: miroir, app.kubernetes.io/component: metrics } }
  endpoints:
    - port: metrics
      interval: 30s
      path: /metrics
```

## PrometheusRule (plan §10 + §14.9)

Alerts (all 12 from plan):

### Availability (plan §10)
1. `MiroirDegradedShards` — `miroir_degraded_shards_total > 0` for 2m
2. `MiroirNodeDown` — `miroir_node_healthy == 0` for 5m
3. `MiroirHighSearchLatency` — p95 > 2s for 5m
4. `MiroirTaskStuck` — `miroir_task_processing_age_seconds > 3600` for 10m
5. `MiroirRebalanceStuck` — `miroir_rebalance_in_progress == 1` for 2h
6. `MiroirSettingsDivergence` — paired with §13.5 auto-repair (plan §10 description)
7. `MiroirAntientropyMismatch` — paired with §13.8 at 3 consecutive passes (~18h default schedule)

### Resource pressure (plan §14.9)
8. `MiroirMemoryPressure` — `miroir_memory_pressure >= 2` for 5m
9. `MiroirRequestQueueBacklog` — `miroir_request_queue_depth > 500` for 2m
10. `MiroirBackgroundJobBacklog` — `miroir_background_queue_depth > 100` for 10m
11. `MiroirPeerDiscoveryGap` — peer mismatch for 2m
12. `MiroirNoLeader` — `sum(miroir_leader) == 0` for 1m

## Why

Alert rules are part of the shipped product, not something operators have to write. Plan §10 is explicit: the rules fire "only when the self-healing paths described [in §13.5 / §13.8] failed to close the gap on their own" — so noise is minimized and every page is actionable.

## Details

**Helm flag**: `miroir.serviceMonitor.enabled: false` default (only render when operator opts in, requires prometheus-operator in cluster). Same for `miroir.prometheusRule.enabled: false`.

**Alert routing**: operators wire to their own Alertmanager — Miroir doesn't ship routing config.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `helm template` with `serviceMonitor.enabled: true` renders a valid ServiceMonitor manifest
- [ ] All 12 alerts present in the rendered PrometheusRule
- [ ] Each alert tripped at least once in Phase 9 chaos tests (where applicable)

issue.description:
## What

Implement plan §10 structured JSON log format:
```json
{
  "timestamp": "2026-05-01T12:00:00.000Z",
  "level": "info",
  "message": "search completed",
  "index": "products",
  "duration_ms": 42,
  "node_count": 3,
  "estimated_hits": 15420,
  "degraded": false
}
```

Every log entry includes `request_id` (UUIDv7-prefix short-hash, same value as the `X-Request-Id` response header from P2.8) so a log search can trace a single request across pods.

## Why

Structured logs are the only log format that scales beyond "grep through ASCII." JSON-per-line is parseable by every log aggregator (Loki, ElasticSearch, Splunk, CloudWatch).

## Details

**Tracing subscriber stack**:
```rust
use tracing_subscriber::prelude::*;
tracing_subscriber::registry()
    .with(tracing_subscriber::fmt::layer().json())
    .with(tracing_subscriber::EnvFilter::from_default_env())
    .init();
```

**Fields on every log line**: `timestamp`, `level`, `target` (module path), `request_id` (from axum middleware), `pod_id` (env `POD_NAME`), `message`. Plus free-form context per log call (`index`, `shard`, `duration_ms`, ...).

**Log levels**:
- `ERROR`: orchestrator-side internal failures
- `WARN`: degraded responses, fallbacks, soft failures
- `INFO`: one line per request with summary fields
- `DEBUG`: per-node calls, per-sub-query in multi-search
- `TRACE`: fan-out buffer contents, scatter plan internals

**No PII**: never log document content, query strings, or API keys. Hashes of keys are fine (for correlation across requests).

## Acceptance

- [ ] `jq` parses every log line
- [ ] Grepping `request_id=abc123` across all pods' logs returns one-line-per-pod-that-handled-part-of-that-request
- [ ] No API key, document field, or user query appears in any log entry
- [ ] Log volume: < 1 entry per client request at INFO level; more at DEBUG only when env filter allows
issue.title: P7.5 Structured JSON logging + request IDs + trace correlation

issue.description:
## What

Implement plan §10 tracing (disabled by default):
```yaml
miroir:
  tracing:
    enabled: false
    endpoint: "http://tempo.monitoring.svc:4317"
    service_name: miroir
    sample_rate: 0.1
```

When enabled, every search produces a trace with parallel spans for each node in the covering set.

## Why

Plan §10: "makes latency outliers immediately visible." A scatter with one slow node shows up as one span sticking out from the parallel pack — operators can immediately point at the node.

## Details

**OTel SDK**: `opentelemetry` + `opentelemetry-otlp` + `tracing-opentelemetry`. Hook into the existing `tracing` subscriber chain.

**Span hierarchy**:
- Parent span: inbound request (`POST /indexes/products/search`)
- Child span: scatter plan construction
- Parallel child spans: one per node in covering set (`call meili-1`, `call meili-2`, ...)
- Parallel child spans within the scatter: any hedges fired (§13.2)
- Merge span: after gather completes

**Sampling**: head-based `sample_rate` in config. Tail-based (e.g., always sample slow traces) is a future enhancement; v1 ships head-based only.

**Resource attributes**: `service.name`, `service.version`, `host.name` (pod name).

**Disabled default**: no overhead when off (the subscriber chain skips the OTel layer entirely).

## Acceptance

- [ ] `tracing.enabled: false` → zero OTel library calls in a CPU profile
- [ ] `tracing.enabled: true` + Tempo running → traces appear within seconds
- [ ] A slow-node induced in Phase 9 chaos produces a visible outlier span in Tempo
- [ ] Sample rate 0.1 results in ~10% of requests producing traces
issue.title: P7.6 OpenTelemetry tracing (optional, off by default)

Reproduction child 2/4 of the miroir-b6b71143 re-split (depends on miroir-7522b867). - A note on this bead quotes the verbatim outcome: either the wedge evidence (parked connection state, open span request_id, elapsed seconds, during-wedge probe results) or a fast-200 control response in full.

issue.description:
## Genesis Bead
**Tied to plan:** `/home/coding/miroir/docs/plan/plan.md`

## Project Overview

**Miroir** — _Multi-node Index Replication Orchestrator, Integrated Rebalancing_ — is a RAID-like sharding and high-availability layer for **Meilisearch Community Edition (MIT)**. It stripes a large index across a fleet of Meilisearch nodes, fans out search queries across all shards, merges ranked results, and rebalances shard assignments when nodes are added or removed — all without Meilisearch Enterprise.

## Why This Exists

Meilisearch CE loads its entire index into memory-mapped LMDB files. A large index that exceeds a single server's available RAM cannot run on that server. The Enterprise Edition's native sharding and replication are **BUSL-1.1 gated** — production use requires a commercial license. Miroir solves this using only the Meilisearch **public REST API**, with no node-side patches or forks. Every Meilisearch node continues to run unmodified CE.

## Design Principles (from plan §1)

1. **Invisible federation** — clients talk to one endpoint using the standard Meilisearch API
2. **No Enterprise dependency** — pure CE (MIT) everywhere
3. **Rendezvous hashing (HRW)** — matches what Meilisearch Enterprise itself uses internally
4. **RF-configurable redundancy** — RF=1 capacity, RF=2 one-node-loss, RF=3 two-node-loss
5. **Graceful degradation** — partial results with `X-Miroir-Degraded` beats whole-request failure
6. **Static binaries, scratch images** — musl + scratch Docker, trivial deploy, tiny attack surface
7. **GitOps first** — all config in `jedarden/declarative-config`, ArgoCD drives cluster changes
8. **Fixed per-pod resource envelope (2 vCPU / 3.75 GB)** — scale out, not up

## Architecture (high-level)

- **Shards (S)** — logical hash-space granularity, **fixed at index creation**, `S = max_nodes_per_group_ever × 8`
- **Replica Groups (RG)** — independent query pools, each holds a full copy of all shards; scales **read throughput**
- **Replication Factor (RF)** — intra-group copies per shard; scales **HA within a group**
- **Writes** fan out to `RG × RF` nodes (one per-group quorum, cluster-wide success when ≥1 group met its quorum)
- **Reads** target exactly one group per query (round-robin); fan out to that group's covering set only
- **Rendezvous hashing is scoped to each group** — prevents cross-group coverage gaps

## Phase Plan

- [ ] **Phase 0 — Foundation** — Cargo workspace, crate layout, config schema, dependencies
- [ ] **Phase 1 — Core Routing** (plan §2, §4) — rendezvous hash, topology, write targets, covering set
- [ ] **Phase 2 — Proxy + API Surface** (plan §3, §5) — HTTP server, documents/search/indexes/settings/tasks/health, result merger, quorum, error mapping
- [ ] **Phase 3 — Task Registry + Persistence** (plan §4 task store) — SQLite schema (14 tables), Redis mirror for HA
- [ ] **Phase 4 — Topology Operations** (plan §2 topology changes, §4 rebalancer) — add/remove node, add/remove group, drain, dual-write, shard-filter migration
- [ ] **Phase 5 — Advanced Capabilities** (plan §13, subsections .1–.21) — reshard, hedging, EWMA, query planner, two-phase settings, session pinning, aliases, anti-entropy, streaming dump import, idempotency+coalescing, multi-search, vector, CDC, TTL, tenant affinity, shadow tee, ILM, canaries, Admin UI, Explain, Search UI
- [ ] **Phase 6 — Horizontal Scaling + HPA** (plan §14) — pod envelope, request-path statelessness, Mode A/B/C background coordination, peer discovery, HPA spec
- [ ] **Phase 7 — Observability + Ops** (plan §10) — metrics, tracing, logs, alerts, Grafana dashboard, ServiceMonitor
- [ ] **Phase 8 — Deployment + CI** (plan §6, §7) — Dockerfile (scratch+musl), Helm chart, ArgoCD Application, Argo Workflow template
- [ ] **Phase 9 — Testing** (plan §8) — unit, integration (docker-compose), compatibility, chaos, performance (criterion), SDK smoke tests
- [ ] **Phase 10 — Security + Secrets** (plan §9) — sealed secrets, ESO/OpenBao integration, key rotation (admin-scoped, JWT, scoped-key), CSRF posture
- [ ] **Phase 11 — Onboarding + Docs + Delivered Artifacts** (plan §11, §12) — README, CHANGELOG, migration docs, miroir-ctl help, runbooks, release checklist
- [ ] **Phase 12 — Open Problems Tracking** (plan §15) — score normalization at scale validation, arm64 support, Raft-based HA task state exploration

## How to use this bead

- Each phase has its own epic bead that blocks this genesis bead
- Every phase epic decomposes into concrete task beads; most tasks have subtasks
- Dependencies are wired so ready-work can be discovered with `br ready`
- Close phase epics as they complete; update the checklist above by editing this bead's body
- Close this genesis bead only when all phases are complete AND `br ready` returns empty

## Cross-cutting references

- Infrastructure: Hetzner EX44 + Tailscale + iad-ci Argo Workflows (see `/home/coding/CLAUDE.md`)
- Container registry: `ghcr.io/jedarden/miroir`
- Helm chart OCI: `ghcr.io/jedarden/charts/miroir`
- GitHub Pages: `https://jedarden.github.io/miroir`
- Declarative config repo: `jedarden/declarative-config → k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/miroir-ci.yaml`
- Argo UI: `https://argo-ci.ardenone.com` (VPN+SSO)
- ArgoCD read-only API: `https://argocd-ro-ardenone-manager-ts.ardenone.com:8444`

## Resources

- Plan doc: `/home/coding/miroir/docs/plan/plan.md` (3739 lines, authoritative)
- Research: `/home/coding/miroir/docs/research/{ha-approaches,consistent-hashing,distributed-search-patterns}.md`

=== 2. STAGE-15 THREADS VERDICT — FALSIFIABLE FORM ===

Mechanism (tokio 1.52.3 vendored source, worker.rs:359-498, read this cycle): entering block_in_place on a multi_thread worker pushes the lifo-slot task to the run queue (454-457), sets the core into cx.worker.core (470), then UNCONDITIONALLY runs runtime::spawn_blocking(move || run(worker)) (477-478) — per the in-source comment (466-467): "In order to block, the core must be sent to another thread for execution." The calling thread then blocks inside f() (494 exit_runtime); Reset::drop (369-392) steals the core back ONLY when the closure returns. There is NO path that hands the core to an existing parked worker.

Falsifiable argument: H = "the handler is parked inside the 770-773 closure at probe instant T". Under H, at instant T the process necessarily contains a thread executing run(worker) driving the released core, and it persists for the entire park — a permanent park cannot dodge probes. The blocking pool is empty at baseline (tokio KEEP_ALIVE = 10s, blocking/pool.rs:172 applied at 212, wait at 529; miroir's spawn_blocking callers — peer_discovery.rs:138, ttl_worker.rs:155/228, rebalancer_worker/mod.rs — are transient ticks). EXPECTED DELTA: Threads = baseline+1 (i.e. 13 if baseline is 12) at EVERY probe instant of the wedge. OBSERVED: Threads = 12 constant at every probe (miroir-b32bcc98 section 4; RUN B probes t+0.9/40/82/115s across the >=121s wedge). The +1 step never appears, so H is falsified at every probe instant. This is stronger than the rule-out's hedge (miroir-c1169949: "spawns a replacement worker when other tasks are runnable") — the spawn is unconditional; there is no runnability precondition.

Joints recorded, not smoothed:
(a) Thread-reuse: spawn_blocking may reuse an idle blocking-pool thread instead of spawning a new OS thread; if one was idle-alive at wedge onset, Threads stays at baseline during the park and the probe cannot discriminate. Bounded: pool threads drain <=10s after their task, and RUN B's probes never exceeded 12 — including t+82s, which lands ~2s after the 01:01:09Z drift_reconciler tick that runs spawn_blocking SRV lookups — evidence the pool is empty at probe instants.
(b) Baseline composition: #[tokio::main] default (multi_thread, workers = available_parallelism = 12 on this 12-core box, main.rs:301) plus the main thread naively predicts baseline >=13, yet every probe read 12 — the instrument semantics behind "Threads=12" (process NLWP vs a runtime worker gauge) are not derivable from the captures. The verdict therefore rests on the CONSTANT count / absence of a +1 STEP at onset, not on the absolute value 13.
(c) The argument excludes parks shorter than a probe interval; sub-interval parks cannot explain >=15s-4m27s wedges anyway.
Independently, the branch is UNREACHABLE for the control (C5), so C6's exclusion does not rest on the threads argument alone.

Control = POST /search/products, headers Authorization: Bearer + Content-Type only (script:476-480), body {"q":"laptop","limit":10} (script:79), single target; harness yaml: shards 16, rf 1, replica_groups 1, node_timeout unset (5000 default), coalescing default-enabled, replica_selection default-adaptive, result_cache enabled (script:338-359).

== 3. THE ONSET AXIS (S7) — what this ranking honestly cannot do ==
Neither live candidate explains 22:27Z. R1's structure existed and completed in 2-3ms in cycles 1-3; R2's bounds are binary-stable. S7 therefore cannot discriminate R1 vs R2 today — the ranking rests on S1-S6, where R1 is uniquely consistent and R2 is positively excluded (duration + zero warns). == 4. THE ONE CONFIRMATORY PROBE (scoped as the decision input for miroir-a6e9e3c6's final memo; NOT implemented) ==
HEALTH-PROBE CADENCE GREP — node-log, zero code change, nothing to revert (reads logs that already exist). This is the audit's R1 discriminator, carried unrun through every round; it is cheap and it splits the entire field.
Protocol:
1. Trigger one wedge exactly as the harness does (scripts/p13-13-first-search-capture.sh control POST). Note t0 = request arrival. Let it run >=5s (>=25 health-tick periods at the harness 200ms cadence, script :352-353).
2. Read the harness node's container log (docker logs --since <t0-2s> <meili-container>; docker.sock is local) and count the proxy's GET /health probe lines inside [t0, t0+5s].
3. Guards that make the inference airtight: (a) run the control TWICE — under R1 the last probe lands within ~1 tick (~200ms) of EACH request's arrival, so probe-stop time must track request onset, not wall clock (a checker that died of an unrelated panic stops at one fixed instant regardless of the requests); (b) grep the proxy log for a panic in the health-check task — a panicked checker also stops probes.

CLAIM 1 - POST /indexes/products/search -> 404, LOCKS NONE: VERIFIED.
Route enumeration: /indexes nest wired at main.rs:850 -> indexes::router (indexes.rs:304-330) registers: / POST create + GET list; /:index GET/PATCH/DELETE; /:index/stats GET; /:index/settings GET/PATCH/POST; /:index/settings/*subpath GET/PATCH; /:index/_preflight POST; /:index/explain POST; /:index/documents nest -> documents::router (documents.rs:143-152: / POST/PUT/DELETE, /:id DELETE). The proxy search path is POST /search/:index: search.rs:128 registers POST /:index on the /search nest (main.rs:852) - different prefix, cannot match. No .fallback() on the main router (main.rs:841-896, grep confirms) -> axum default fallback -> 404 empty body.
Lock-free path in the wedged process: router match fails BEFORE any handler runs. search_handler (search.rs:173) is never entered, so it never acquires state.topology.read() (search.rs:667 - the lock the wedged POST /search/:index handler sits in), never awaits session_manager/query_coalescer/result_cache/settings_broadcast, issues no node calls. Caveat (precision, not drift): middleware runs first, outermost->innermost (main.rs:858-895): telemetry -> request_id -> session_pinning -> auth -> csrf. csrf: POST to non-admin path passes straight through (auth.rs:934). auth: /indexes/products/search is NOT dispatch-exempt (auth.rs:546 exempts only /health, /version, /_miroir/*, /ui/search GETs, admin login) -> dispatch_bearer (auth.rs:722) runs; it is synchronous and pure (constant-time key compare + JWT validation) - no Redis, no mutex. Net: LOCKS NONE confirmed; 404 immune to the wedge.

Drift from the original claim: it implied the proxy has no /indexes GET route and the node serves the request directly. Re-derived handler behavior (list_indexes_handler, indexes.rs:471-492): extracts ONLY Extension(Arc<Config>) - does NOT extract AppState; builds a fresh MeilisearchClient (new reqwest::Client, 10s timeout) per request; picks config.nodes.first() (503 if empty); issues ONE outbound GET {node}/indexes with bearer node_master_key; 2xx -> parse body to JSON (parse failure degrades to {"results":[]} but STILL returns 200); transport error -> 500; non-2xx -> forwards the node's status code.

issue.description:
## Phase 1 Epic — Core Routing

Implements the deterministic, coordination-free routing primitives that everything else depends on. After this phase, given a fixed topology + config, any Miroir pod can independently compute identical write targets and covering sets — no coordination required.

## Why This Matters

Plan §1 principle 3: rendezvous hashing (HRW) is the same algorithm Meilisearch Enterprise uses internally with twox-hash. Getting this right has **three** properties we rely on downstream:

1. **Determinism** — all pods agree on assignments without any gossip protocol
2. **Minimal reshuffling** — adding a node to a group moves only ~1/(Ng+1) of that group's docs (plan §2 "Properties" bullets)
3. **Group isolation** — hashing scoped to intra-group node lists prevents both replicas of a shard from landing in the same group (plan §2 "Why group-scoped assignment matters")

These properties are the foundation for the §2 write path, §2 read path, §4 rebalancer, §13.3 adaptive selection, §13.4 query planner, §13.8 anti-entropy, and §14.5 Mode A shard-partitioned ownership. A subtle bug here — e.g., seeding the hash differently, using a non-stable node-id encoding — corrupts every later layer silently.

## Scope (plan §2 Architecture + §4 router.rs)

- `router.rs` — `score(shard, node)`, `assign_shard_in_group`, `write_targets`, `query_group`, `covering_set`, `shard_for_key`
- `topology.rs` — `Topology` struct (nodes grouped by `replica_group`), node health state machine (healthy / degraded / draining / failed / joining / active / removed)
- `scatter.rs` — fan-out orchestration primitives (stubbed execution; wired in Phase 2)
- `merger.rs` — result merge primitives (global sort by `_rankingScore`, offset/limit, facet aggregation, estimatedTotalHits summation, `_miroir_shard` + `_rankingScore` stripping) — pure-function friendly for unit testing
- Unit tests per §8 "Router correctness" + "Result merger" bullets

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Rendezvous assignment is deterministic given fixed node list (verified by test)
- [ ] Adding a 4th node in a 3-node group moves at most ~2 × (1/4) of shards (verified by test, plan §8)
- [ ] 64 shards / 3 nodes / RF=1 → each node holds 18–26 shards (verified by test)
- [ ] Top-RF placement changes minimally on add / remove (verified by test)
- [ ] `write_targets` returns exactly `RG × RF` nodes, one from each group
- [ ] `query_group(seq, RG)` distributes evenly (verified by test)
- [ ] `covering_set` within a group returns exactly one node per shard (with intra-group replica rotation)
- [ ] `merger` passes the merge/facet/limit tests in plan §8
- [ ] `miroir-core` ≥ 90% line coverage via cargo-tarpaulin (per §8 coverage policy)
issue.title: Phase 1 — Core Routing (rendezvous hash, topology, covering set)

All 26 acceptance tests pass, verifying: XxHash64 with seed 0, canonical (shard_id, node_id) order, group-scoped assignment, lexicographic tie-breaking, determinism, reshuffle bounds, uniformity, and RF=2 stability. See notes/miroir-cdo.1.md for details.
issue.description:
## What

Implement `miroir_core::router`:
```rust
pub fn score(shard_id: u32, node_id: &str) -> u64
pub fn assign_shard_in_group(shard_id: u32, group_nodes: &[NodeId], rf: usize) -> Vec<NodeId>
pub fn shard_for_key(primary_key: &str, shard_count: u32) -> u32
```

## Why

These three are the atoms everything else builds on. `score` uses `XxHash64::with_seed(0)` with the canonical concatenation order `(shard_id, node_id)` (plan §4 code sample). Any deviation (different seed, different ordering, endianness) forks routing across any two Miroir instances and silently corrupts writes.

## Design Notes (plan §2 / §4)

- **Hash function is `twox-hash` (XxHash family)** — the same one Meilisearch Enterprise uses; the choice is non-negotiable (plan §2).
- **Node-id encoding stability** — the string passed to `node_id.hash(&mut h)` must be byte-stable. Use the bare `id: "meili-0"` string from config, not a reformatted address.
- **`assign_shard_in_group` is group-scoped on purpose** — per plan §2 "Why group-scoped assignment matters": scoping to the group prevents both replicas of a shard from landing in the same group. A global rendezvous would have no such guarantee.
- **Sort by score descending, break ties lexicographically on node_id** so two nodes with identical hash scores (extremely rare but possible) deterministically resolve.

## Acceptance Tests (plan §8 "Router correctness")

- [ ] Determinism: same `(shard_id, nodes)` → identical `Vec<NodeId>` across 1000 randomized runs
- [ ] Reshuffle bound on add: 64 shards, 3→4 nodes in a group → at most `2 × (1/4) × 64` shard-node edges differ
- [ ] Reshuffle bound on remove: 64 shards, 4→3 nodes → `~RF × S / Ng` edges differ
- [ ] Uniformity: 64 shards, 3 nodes, RF=1 → each node holds 18–26 shards (chi-square not rejected at p=0.95)
- [ ] RF=2 placement: top-2 nodes change minimally when a node is added or removed
- [ ] `shard_for_key(pk, S)` is `(XxHash64::with_seed(0).hash(pk) % S)` — verified against a known fixture vector

issue.description:
## What

Implement `miroir_core::topology`:
```rust
pub struct Topology {
    pub shards: u32,
    pub replica_groups: u32,
    pub rf: usize,
    pub nodes: Vec<Node>,
}
pub struct Node {
    pub id: NodeId,
    pub address: String,
    pub replica_group: u32,
    pub status: NodeStatus,
}
pub enum NodeStatus { Healthy, Degraded, Draining, Failed, Joining, Active, Removed }
```

Helpers: `Topology::groups() -> impl Iterator<Item=&Group>`, `Topology::group(g: u32) -> &Group`, `group.nodes() -> &[Node]`, `group.healthy_nodes() -> Vec<&Node>`.

## Why

The `Topology` type is what `router` operates on. State transitions correspond to plan §2 topology-change verbs: a node is `Joining` → `Active` after a group-add migration; `Draining` → `Removed` after a node-remove migration; `Failed` is for unplanned loss.

The state field matters for **routing-eligibility**: writes skip `Draining` for *affected* shards (plan §2 "Removing a node" step 1), but still deliver to it for shards it still owns. A bug where a `Draining` node stops receiving any writes prematurely would create durability gaps during rebalance.

## State Transition Rules

| From | To | Triggered by |
|------|-----|-------------|
| (new) | Joining | `POST /_miroir/nodes` (plan §4 admin API) |
| Joining | Active | Migration complete (Phase 4) |
| Active | Draining | `POST /_miroir/nodes/{id}/drain` |
| Draining | Removed | Migration complete (Phase 4) |
| Active/Draining | Failed | Health check detects (Phase 7) |
| Failed | Active | Health check recovery + optional replication catch-up |
| Active/Failed | Degraded | Partial health (timeouts, not full disconnect) |
| Degraded | Active | Health restored |

## Acceptance

- [ ] Topology deserializes from plan §4 YAML example (RG=2, 6 nodes, RF=1) into the expected shape
- [ ] `groups()` iterator returns `RG` groups in ascending order; each group holds exactly its configured nodes
- [ ] State-machine unit tests cover every legal transition and reject illegal ones (e.g., Joining → Draining)
- [ ] `Node::is_write_eligible_for(shard_id, status)` correctness table has a test per row

issue.description:
## What

Implement the two flat API calls used by the HTTP layer:
```rust
pub fn write_targets(shard_id: u32, topology: &Topology) -> Vec<NodeId>
pub fn query_group(query_seq: u64, replica_groups: u32) -> u32
pub fn covering_set(shard_count: u32, group: &Group, rf: usize, query_seq: u64) -> Vec<NodeId>
```

## Why / Semantics (plan §2)

**`write_targets`** — flat union of `assign_shard_in_group(shard, g)` across all `RG` groups. Returns `RG × RF` nodes total (may include duplicates across groups if a node_id coincidentally has the highest score in multiple groups — use a dedup pass in the HTTP layer when grouping docs per-request rather than dedup here, so the routing layer's behavior is pure).

**`query_group`** — round-robin per the plan's note: "`query_sequence_number` is a per-pod counter, not a cluster-wide one." Under HPA, cluster-wide balance relies on the K8s Service's round-robin / random kube-proxy policy (§14.4 link).

**`covering_set`** — one node per shard within a group. The intra-group replica selection within each shard rotates by `query_seq % rf` (plan §4 code sample). The returned set is **deduplicated** because one node may own multiple shards in the same group; searching it once captures all its shards (Meilisearch searches all its local docs in a single call).

## Critical Invariant

Two different Miroir pods, given identical `Topology` + `rf` + `shard_count`, **must** compute the same `write_targets` for any given `shard_id` and the same `covering_set` modulo `query_seq` rotation. This is the property that makes the request path stateless (plan §14.4).

## Acceptance (plan §8)

- [ ] `write_targets` returns exactly `RG × RF` nodes (counting duplicates)
- [ ] `write_targets` assigns one-per-group: the subset of returned nodes in group g is exactly `assign_shard_in_group(shard, group_g_nodes)`
- [ ] `covering_set` has `|covering_set| ≤ Ng` and covers all `shard_count` shards within the chosen group
- [ ] Two instances of `Topology` with identical content produce identical `covering_set` outputs for the same `query_seq`
- [ ] `query_group` distribution: 10K `query_seq` values `% RG` produce uniformly distributed group choices (chi-square pass)
issue.title: P1.3 write_targets and covering_set

issue.description:
## What

Implement `miroir_core::merger`:
```rust
pub struct MergeInput {
    pub shard_hits: Vec<ShardHitPage>, // one per node in covering set
    pub offset: usize,
    pub limit: usize,
    pub client_requested_score: bool,
    pub facets: Option<Vec<String>>,
}
pub fn merge(input: MergeInput) -> MergedSearchResult
```

## Why

Plan §2 read path step 6 enumerates the exact sequence:
1. Collect all hits with scores
2. Sort globally descending by `_rankingScore`
3. Apply `offset + limit` **after** merge (not per-shard)
4. Strip `_rankingScore` from each hit if client did not request it
5. **Always** strip `_miroir_shard` (and other reserved `_miroir_*` fields)
6. Sum facet counts across shards
7. Sum `estimatedTotalHits` across shards
8. `processingTimeMs` = max across covering set

This must be a pure function — testable without a network — because it will be hit constantly and any non-determinism (e.g., HashMap iteration order affecting facet key ordering) breaks the compatibility suite.

## Design Notes

- Use a binary min-heap of size `offset + limit` to avoid keeping all hits in RAM when fan-out is large
- Facet merging: `BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, u64>>` (ordered) for stable serialization
- `estimatedTotalHits` clamp: Meilisearch caps at 1000 per shard by default — confirm whether Miroir should pass through the cap or sum and let the client see a higher number (consistent with Meilisearch single-node behavior: pass through)
- Tie-breaking: on equal `_rankingScore`, fall back to lexicographic `primary_key` for deterministic ordering

## Score Comparability Caveat (plan §2 read path, §13.5)

Scores are comparable across shards **only if** all nodes have identical index settings — enforced by the §13.5 two-phase broadcast. Until Phase 5 lands, assume settings are uniform and flag a warning in `Config::validate` if drift is detected.

## Acceptance (plan §8 "Result merger")

- [ ] Global sort by `_rankingScore` descending across shards
- [ ] `offset + limit` applied **after** merge; test: 50 docs with known scores, pages of 10 reconstruct single limit=50
- [ ] `_rankingScore` stripped when `client_requested_score=false`
- [ ] `_miroir_shard` always stripped
- [ ] Facet counts sum correctly including keys unique to one shard
- [ ] `estimatedTotalHits` summed across shards
- [ ] Stable serialization: `merge` on the same input twice produces byte-identical JSON
issue.title: P1.4 Result merger (global sort + offset/limit + facets + stripping)

issue.description:
## What

Implement `miroir_core::scatter` with:
```rust
pub trait NodeClient { /* HTTP calls to a Meilisearch node */ }
pub fn plan_search_scatter(topology: &Topology, query_seq: u64, rf: usize, shard_count: u32) -> ScatterPlan
pub async fn execute_scatter<C: NodeClient>(plan: ScatterPlan, client: &C, req: SearchRequest) -> Vec<ShardHitPage>
```

## Why

`NodeClient` is the seam between `miroir-core` (pure, no network) and `miroir-proxy` (HTTP client). Injecting it via a trait means unit tests can provide a fake client; production binds `reqwest` via the trait impl in `miroir-proxy`.

`plan_search_scatter` returns the exact shard→node mapping that Phase 2 hands to `execute_scatter`. Separating the plan from execution is what makes §13.20 `/explain` cheap — the explain path generates the plan and returns it without touching any node.

## Plan Structure

```rust
pub struct ScatterPlan {
    pub chosen_group: u32,        // query_seq % RG
    pub target_shards: Vec<u32>,  // for §13.4 narrowing — initially all 0..S
    pub shard_to_node: HashMap<u32, NodeId>,  // resolved covering set
    pub deadline_ms: u32,
    pub hedging_eligible: bool,   // reserved for §13.2 Phase 5
}
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] Plan construction is pure — no async, no I/O
- [ ] `execute_scatter` with a mock `NodeClient` returns one `ShardHitPage` per node in the plan
- [ ] Partial-failure handling: a failed node surfaces as `Err` on that shard; `merge` downstream applies `unavailable_shard_policy`
- [ ] Deadline propagation: when any node exceeds `deadline_ms`, the result includes a partial-response flag

viability so the umbrella can.
**Produced by:** `miroir-d12debdf` (terminal gate child 4/4 of the `miroir-b6b71143`
re-split; siblings: `miroir-7522b867` docs commit, `miroir-b32bcc98` wedge
reproduction, `miroir-514810ac` parked-stage localization).
**Tree:** 2026-09-15, HEAD `10e412d`. Working tree carries the long-standing
pre-dirty `search.rs` cache-key refactor (5 hunks, first at line 476 — zero
route-registering lines, verified by diff grep) plus non-code files; every route
citation below is identical in HEAD and working tree (all cited route lines
precede the first diff hunk). **No new capture cycles were run for this memo** —
everything cited already existed in bead notes, committed docs, or the tree.

---

## 1. Signature A — final attribution (five-cycle-stable)

### 1.1 Verdict

Signature A — 9/10 p13_13 tests panicking at their first proxy search POST,
`assertion failed: resp.status().is_success()` — is an **axum router miss**
(taxonomy: router 404, empty body, auth passed first) on
`POST /indexes/:index/search`. **Root cause: an API-contract mismatch between the
p13_13 suite and the proxy route table.** The suite addresses the proxy with the
Meilisearch-native path; the proxy serves search only at `POST /search/:index`
and `POST /multi-search` and registers no fallback on the main router, so axum
answers the suite's first search POST with its default empty-body 404 before any
handler runs. The verdict was reproduced identically across eight native-path
observations on eight distinct proxy processes (cycles 1–5) under both the
scratch and committed harness forms; it is not auth (x-request-id present
post-auth), not upstream (no error envelope), not a proxy-internal fault (404,
not 5xx), not environment.

### 1.2 Verbatim evidence — the fifth-cycle file

The final capture cycle is durably preserved in-repo by `miroir-7522b867`'s docs
commit `13b16c0`:

**`docs/notes/p13-13-fifth-cycle-signature-a-capture-2026-09-12.md`** — capture
run 2026-09-12T00:05:19Z (child `miroir-2037d2ee` on child `miroir-454e8c77`'s
manual topology; `miroir-f79b50e1`'s attribution note copied verbatim at lines
199–240). Verbatim fingerprint, lines 91–96:

```
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
x-request-id: 6577bfec
content-length: 0
date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 00:05:19 GMT
```

Decisive headers: `x-request-id` **present** (auth passed — request_id_middleware
is inner to auth_middleware, main.rs:858–865 layer-order comment), `content-length: 0`,
**no** `allow` (not 405), **no** `content-type` and no
`{"message","code","type","link"}` envelope (not upstream passthrough). Proxy-log
cross-check in the same file (lines 98–103): `request_id 6577bfec` WARN "POST 404
Not Found" `path_template=/indexes/products/search duration_ms=0` — response
emitted at the router, no handler work. All three scratch logs are sha256-pinned
(lines 81–85) between BEGIN/END-LOG markers with the documented CRLF
binary-extraction caveat (lines 71–77). Companion files preserve cycles 1–4:
`p13-13-final-signature-a-capture-2026-09-11.md` (20:17Z / 20:42Z),
`p13-13-third-cycle-signature-a-capture-2026-09-11.md` (21:37Z),
`p13-13-fourth-cycle-committed-harness-capture-2026-09-11.md` (the four

### 1.3 Route citations — re-verified at this memo's HEAD (`10e412d`)

- `crates/miroir-proxy/src/routes/search.rs:128` —

  (`.route("/multi-search", post(multi_search::multi_search::<UnifiedState>),) // §13.11`).

`POST /indexes/:index/search` has **never been a live endpoint at any commit**.
