served `POST /search/{index}/search`, never `/indexes/...`; (2) the scaffold-era
`"/:index/:sub"` catch-all in indexes.rs route-matched `.../search` but returned
501 unconditionally (removed by `b2490ea`); (3) the removal of (1) lives in merge
`1f686c6`'s tree resolution, invisible to default `git log -S`.

---

## 2. The control wedge — the second, distinct failure mode

`POST /search/:index` **is** registered and reached — and since 2026-09-11T22:27Z
it has parked inside `search_handler` on **every attempted capture: 10/10**.

### 2.1 Reproduction result (child 2/4, `miroir-b32bcc98`, cycle 6)

Two fresh reproductions on 2026-09-12 (binary unchanged since 2026-09-11 16:42;
pre-flight `ss` clean on 17770/9090; every curl bounded):

- **RUN A** — committed harness `scripts/p13-13-first-search-capture.sh`, 00:50:25Z:
  native 404 fingerprint identical for the 9th consecutive observation; control
  `curl: (28) ... timed out after 15002 milliseconds with 0 bytes received`.
- **RUN B** — manual during-wedge topology, 00:56:08–01:01:50Z: control fired
  00:59:49Z bound `-m 120` → `curl (28)` at 120.002 s, 0 bytes. Method innovation:
  the control was fired 80 s before a background tick so a tick landed inside the
  wedge window.

Count reconciliation: 8/8 at the fifth cycle (4 committed-harness cycle-4 runs +
3 cycle-4 manual diagnostic topologies + the cycle-5 manual capture) + 2 in
cycle 6 = **10/10**, as enumerated by the timeline child `miroir-d9bf6824`.
(`miroir-514810ac`'s localization note says "12 wedge instances"; the
explicitly-enumerated timeline count is 10 — this memo uses 10.) A fast-200
control has not occurred since 22:27Z; cycles 1–3 got three fast degraded-200s
from the *same binary*.

### 2.2 Parked stage (child 3/4, `miroir-514810ac` chain)

Log-provable bracket: the `/search/:index` span **is** entered
(`#[tracing::instrument]` at `search.rs:172`) and the terminal
`info!(… "search completed")` is never reached (literal at `search.rs:1169` at
HEAD; `miroir-514810ac`'s note recorded it as :1130-1131 — superseded by this
re-verified citation). Everything between is debug-level and the captures hold
zero DEBUG records, so logs alone cannot shrink the bracket.

Within the bracket, the named stage under the leading hypothesis is **stage 13's
write-preferring topology READ held across the entire DFS**: acquired at
`search.rs:656` at HEAD (`let topo = state.topology.read().await;`; worktree :667
— the note's clean-HEAD 656/worktree 667 pair checks out), held across the
stage-18 DFS scatter-gather await (`dfs_query_then_fetch_search(...).await`,
HEAD :892–895, `.await` at :895; worktree :901–904), released only at
`drop(topo)` HEAD :908 (worktree :917).

### 2.3 Mechanism hypothesis — R1

The request parks inside a **non-completing synchronous DFS tail** within that
read hold: `strategy.merge` (`core/scatter.rs:1123` → `core/merger.rs:96` trait
decl → `RrfStrategy::merge` :152 → `rrf_merge` :231, pure CPU), the sync serde
parse (`crates/miroir-proxy/src/client.rs:143`, outside the client-level
`.timeout` at `client.rs:25`), or `GlobalIdf::from_preflight_responses`
(`core/scatter.rs:1192`). A sync hang logs nothing and parks no await, which
matches the wedge signature (silent from arrival, span ambient — captured live
as request_id `3af56eda` straddling the 01:01:09Z tick ≥121 s). Because tokio's
RwLock is write-preferring, the held read freezes the health checker at its
`main.rs:956` `state.topology.write().await` (per-node probe
`client.get(&url).send().await` at `main.rs:988` happens inside the write hold),
while lock-free routes keep serving mid-wedge and no "node marked
Degraded/Failed" warn (`main.rs:1052`/`:1059`) ever fires.

Competitors are excluded with falsifiers: **R2** (the upstream
no-overall-deadline family) is hang-capable but capped by ~15 s of per-node
timeouts vs observed ≥121 s / ≥4m27s, with zero `miroir.node` warns in any wedge
window; **R3** (`search.rs` coalesced wait) and **R4** (`block_in_place`) are
dead per `miroir-bdab1a41`. R1 itself is **still unconfirmed** — its
confirmatory probe (health-probe cadence grep on the node log; ~2 min; outcome
table on `miroir-bdab1a41` section 4) has not been run. This memo did not run it
(no-new-cycles charter).

### 2.4 Proxy bug or environment artifact?

**A proxy-internal, per-request park — a proxy bug candidate, not an environment
artifact.** The environment was exonerated *during* the wedge (child 2 RUN B):
socket fully delivered then idle (211-byte request at t0, both queues 0/0,
`lastsnd/lastrcv/lastack` 114 s+ — not transport backpressure); router liveness
(`/health` 200 in ~5 ms, `/nope` 404 in ~5 ms at t+0.9/40/82/115 s); threads
constant at 12 (no pool exhaustion); the Meilisearch node answered direct
`/health` in 0.7–1.2 ms mid-wedge **and logged the proxy completing an outbound
`GET /indexes` → 200 in 259 µs at 01:01:09Z** — proxy→node HTTP works while the
handler parks. The park lives in the registered handler's own body.

### 2.5 The open axis (S7)

Why the same binary produced fast degraded-200s at 20:17–21:37Z and has wedged
on every attempt since 22:27Z is **unexplained by every candidate**, including
spawn-age (a cycle-4 control wedged ~15 ms into process life). S7 is the one
residual axis where a time- or environment-dependent *trigger* of the sync-tail
non-completion cannot yet be excluded — it is a trigger question, not a
park-location question.

---

## 3. Remediation options — updated viability

### (a) Repoint the suite at `POST /search/:index` — **BLOCKED by the wedge**

The contract exists and is registered (`search.rs:128` nested at `main.rs:852`),
and cycles 1–3's fast degraded-200 control (200 + `content-type: application/json`
+ `x-miroir-degraded: shards=0..15` + 55-byte body) was its original
justification. **That justification is dead**: the very endpoint the suite would
be repointed at has wedged 10/10 since 22:27Z, including ~15 ms into process
life, on both harness classes, with a during-wedge capture proving the park is
handler-internal. As-is, (a) trades the suite's current fast-fail 404 for a
probable indefinite hang at its first search POST (:600) — strictly worse for CI
(a hang needs an external kill and burns runner time; nothing behind the POST
gets exercised either way). (a) becomes viable only after the wedge is diagnosed
— at minimum R1's confirmatory probe — and fixed; what a post-fix run would
return (degraded-vs-full semantics for the suite's cache-flow assertions) is
unknown until then.

### (b) Register `POST /indexes/:index/search` in the `/indexes` nest — **fixes signature A outright; inherits the wedge**

Adding a `"/:index/search"` leaf to `indexes.rs:309-329` delegating to
`search_handler` eliminates the router-miss by construction: the suite's first
POST would route, and the five-cycle-stable 404 fingerprint disappears. But it
delegates to the **same handler that wedges** — child 2/3's evidence shows the
park is inside `search_handler`'s body and route-agnostic — so (b) likely
surfaces the **same wedge via the native path**: the suite's first POST would
enter `search_handler` and (under R1) park at the same stage, converting the 404
into a hang. It is also a proxy code change carrying a product-contract question
(is Meilisearch-native search compatibility a requirement?) that only the
umbrella can answer.

### Which option child 3's mechanism favors — and why

R1 does **not** separate the options on wedge exposure: the park is in the
handler body, so both (a) and (b) converge on identical exposure, and R1
therefore does not make (a) safe. To the extent the mechanism informs the
choice, it **favors (b), conditionally**, for two reasons:

1. **Same-surface fix.** R1 localizes the wedge to `search_handler`/`search.rs` —
   the same file a (b) registration touches. A single proxy-side change-set
   (register the native leaf + fix the stage-13 hold) would close both failure
   modes at the root and complete the proxy's already Meilisearch-shaped
   `/indexes` surface (stats/settings/documents/preflight/explain are all
   registered there today). Under (a), the proxy's contract stays
   Meilisearch-incompatible and the wedge still needs its own proxy-side fix —
   two workstreams instead of one.
2. **(a)'s evidentiary basis is gone.** (a) rested entirely on the fast
   degraded-200 control; that endpoint's 10/10 wedge record means repointing
   today yields a hung suite on the one path with a proven indefinite-park
   failure mode.

The binding caveat either way: **under R1, neither option delivers a green suite
until the wedge is fixed** (or its trigger understood via S7), and R1 is
unconfirmed until the pending health-probe cadence grep runs — if probes continue
through a wedge, the entire audited await set is cleared and the problem resets
to S7.

### The decision is not made here

Per charter, choosing between (a) and (b) — and sequencing them against the
wedge diagnosis — belongs to umbrella **`miroir-1ec135a1`** (open as of this
memo). This memo supplies the decision inputs only.

---

| **AC1** — "A note on this bead quotes the captured status line and body (and any decisive headers, e.g. allow/content-length/x-request-id) verbatim." | **MET.** `miroir-b6b71143`'s notes quote both requests verbatim in every capture block: the consolidated verdict (`miroir-f87c46da`, 20:17Z native 404 + control 200 with full header lists and the 55-byte body), the final attribution (`miroir-1b17291c`, 20:42Z, incl. proxy-log cross-check), the third-cycle refresh (`miroir-fc5fa7fd`, 21:37Z), and the fifth-cycle block (`miroir-f79b50e1`, 00:05:19Z). Durably in-repo: the fingerprint block at `docs/notes/p13-13-fifth-cycle-signature-a-capture-2026-09-12.md` lines 91–96 (headers :92–95), the proxy-log cross-check at :98–103, sha256 pins at :81–85; cycles 1–4 in the companion files listed at :40–49. The wedge side is preserved too: the empty attempt-1 section with its epilogue (:126–137) and the rc=28 attempt-2 log (:146–168). |
| **AC2** — "The note attributes signature A to a root cause with evidence and states whether the failing path exists anywhere in the proxy's route table or git history." | **MET.** Attribution to the API-contract mismatch / axum router-404 with the four-way taxonomy exclusions is stated in the consolidated verdict and the fifth-cycle attribution note (fifth-cycle file lines 199–240), and restated as §1.1 of this memo. issue.description:
Sub-child 1 of 5 in the sub-split of miroir-0cc8350c (round-10 Section 4). Read-only static verification — change nothing in the source.

Verify, against the current working tree, the GET /health row of the per-route lock-sharing table: the route holds NO locks in the WEDGED PROXY process (observed 200s mid-wedge: cycle 5 00:13:02.996957Z req 81f0188f; RUN B probes at t+0.9/40/82/115s).

Check freshly: (a) get_health (health.rs:22) takes no extractor at all — no State; (b) the middleware chain is lock-free for GET /health — csrf returns immediately for GET (auth.rs:930), auth dispatch exempts GET /health (auth.rs:548 -> next.run auth.rs:828), session_pinning/request_id are header-only, telemetry (wired main.rs:869-875) uses atomics plus only prometheus-internal label-map locks held within a lookup, never across an await; (c) /health is registered on the main router (main.rs:842; router main.rs:841-896, no .fallback()).

State the route-vs-task trap explicitly: the /health ROUTE (fresh per-request task; the handler body has zero await points) is distinct from the health-checker BACKGROUND TASK (tokio::spawn main.rs:398-400 -> run_health_checker; interval.tick().await main.rs:954; state.topology.write() main.rs:956 held across the whole tick body to implicit drop main.rs:1114; prune_expired().await main.rs:1110 takes sessions.write + pending_writes.write at session_pinning.rs:318 while the topology write guard is held). Route and task share nothing, in both directions. Note the boundary: GET /_miroir/ready is OUTSIDE the shared-nothing class (get_ready takes state.topology.read(), health.rs:46) — /health and /version (health.rs:27-33) are inside it.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- A note on this bead states GET /health -> LOCKS NONE in the wedged proxy process, with file:line evidence freshly checked against the current tree.
- The route-vs-task distinction is stated explicitly, with the task lock span (main.rs:956 -> :1114) and the prune_expired nesting (session_pinning.rs:318) cited.
- Any coordinate drift vs the cites above is listed explicitly.
issue.notes:
VERDICT: GET /health -> LOCKS NONE in the wedged proxy process. All cites freshly checked against the current tree (HEAD 316b0ec; none of the cited files are in the dirty set, so evidence is HEAD state).

(a) HANDLER - health.rs:22-26: pub async fn get_health() -> Json<HealthResponse> takes NO extractor at all (no State, no Extension). Body is Json(HealthResponse { status: "available".to_string() }) - ZERO .await points, zero shared-state access. Cannot block on any lock.

(b) MIDDLEWARE CHAIN lock-free for GET /health (order per main.rs:858-896, outermost first):
- csrf_middleware (auth.rs:925): State<CsrfState> clone only; GET/HEAD/OPTIONS short-circuit at auth.rs:930-932 -> next.run immediately. Exact match to cite auth.rs:930.
- auth_middleware (auth.rs:822): Rule 0 is_dispatch_exempt matches GET /health at auth.rs:548-550 -> return next.run at auth.rs:828, before any session-cache/bearer work (the revoked_sessions lock at auth.rs:844 is admin-path-only, unreached for /health). Exempt contract also unit-tested (auth.rs:1191-1192, dispatch tests 1258-1265). Exact match to cites 548/828.
- Extension layers + DefaultBodyLimit (main.rs:880-884): insert-only / body-limit, no locks.
- session_pinning_middleware (middleware.rs:170-184): parses X-Miroir-Session into extensions, next.run at :183. Despite its name it NEVER touches SessionManager's sessions/pending_writes RwLocks - header-only. Confirmed.
- request_id_middleware (middleware.rs:138-164): header/extension manipulation only. Confirmed.
- telemetry_middleware (wired main.rs:869-875; body middleware.rs:1683-1785): Metrics clone is Arc-handle clone; InFlightGuard (middleware.rs:1634-1661) does prometheus Gauge inc/dec = atomic ops (guard held across next.run :1716-1720 but acquires no mutex). Only real locks are prometheus-family label-map mutexes inside with_label_values (middleware.rs:1727-1734), each held within a single lookup call AFTER the await completes - never across an await. Confirmed as described.

(c) REGISTRATION - main.rs:842 .route("/health", get(health::get_health)), the sole /health registration in the crate; router built main.rs:841-896, ends .with_state(state.clone()) at :896; NO .fallback() anywhere in main.rs. Separate :9090 metrics router serves only /metrics (middleware.rs:1788-1790). Confirmed.

ROUTE vs TASK - distinct tokio tasks, share nothing in both directions:
- ROUTE: fresh per-request task; zero-await handler + middleware as above => it can neither block on nor starve any lock. This is the source-side explanation for the observed 200s mid-wedge (cycle 5 00:13:02.996957Z req 81f0188f; RUN B probes t+0.9/40/82/115s - runtime observations taken from the parent investigation as given; this note is the static side).
- TASK: tokio::spawn main.rs:398-400 -> run_health_checker (fn main.rs:943). Per tick: interval.tick().await main.rs:954 -> state.topology.write().await main.rs:956, and that guard is live for the WHOLE tick body - across every node's probe send().await main.rs:988, sync_rebalancer_metrics_to_prometheus().await main.rs:1094, mark_ready().await main.rs:1098 - until implicit drop at loop-body close main.rs:1114 (fn close :1115). Nested INSIDE that span: prune_expired().await main.rs:1110 -> sessions.write() at miroir-core/src/session_pinning.rs:319 + pending_writes.write() at :320 (fn at :318). Confirmed exactly as dispatched.
- Consequence: any request needing topology (read or write) or sessions/pending_writes queues behind the tick; GET /health needs none of them.

BOUNDARY:
- GET /_miroir/ready is OUTSIDE the shared-nothing class: get_ready takes State<AppState> and state.topology.read().await at health.rs:47 - this read contends directly with the wedged task's topology.write span main.rs:956->1114, so /_miroir/ready CAN hang mid-wedge.
- /version correction: the dispatch cite "health.rs:27-33" is doubly off. Coordinates: the health.rs get_version copy is doc :28 / fn :29-35. Substance: that copy is DEAD CODE (#![allow(dead_code)] at health.rs:2; unreferenced in main.rs) and is NOT what is mounted. main.rs:843 routes /version to version::get_version::<UnifiedState> (routes/version.rs:14-22), which takes State<S> and awaits version_state.get_version() (version.rs:20) -> VersionState::get_version takes version_cache.read()+last_cache_update.read() on hit (admin_endpoints.rs:117-118) or both writes on miss (:144-145). Those two RwLocks are VersionState-private and DISJOINT from the task's lock set (topology/sessions/pending_writes), so the mounted /version still shares nothing with the wedged task - but it is NOT a zero-lock handler like /health. Correct classification: /health = shared-nothing; /version = own locks, disjoint set; /_miroir/ready = contends with the wedge.

COORDINATE DRIFT vs dispatch cites (benign; none change the verdict):
- health.rs:46 (get_ready topology.read) -> actual :47 (fn signature spans 40-46).
- health.rs:27-33 (get_version) -> actual :28-35, plus the dead-code/mounted-substance issue above.
- session_pinning.rs:318 is the fn signature; the two write acquisitions are :319/:320.
- All other cites EXACT: health.rs:22, auth.rs:930, auth.rs:548, auth.rs:828, main.rs:842, main.rs:841-896, main.rs:869-875, main.rs:398-400, main.rs:954, main.rs:956, main.rs:1110, main.rs:1114.

No source files changed - read-only verification.

issue.description:
Child 2/4 of the miroir-74a0c51c umbrella (readiness strictness). In crates/miroir-proxy/tests/p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs, wait_for_ready() used to treat any 2xx from GET /health as ready, but /health unconditionally returns {"status":"available"} once the listener binds (crates/miroir-proxy/src/routes/health.rs:21-26) — so a stale proxy from an earlier run bound to PROXY_PORT passes the loose check and the test burns READY_TIMEOUT on a process that can never be ready.

Acceptance criteria:
- A 2xx from /health counts as ready only when the JSON body equals {"status":"available"}
- A 2xx with a non-JSON body, or with a different JSON body, bails immediately — message names the URL, the HTTP status, the observed body, and PROXY_PORT, and says a foreign process is likely bound — instead of polling until READY_TIMEOUT
- Scope: the success branch of the probe loop in wait_for_ready() in crates/miroir-proxy/tests/p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs; closable once the hunk is present and correct (commit happens in child 4)

Depends on: child 1 (same function, sequential edits to one file). Blocks child 3.
issue.notes: Strictness hunk in wait_for_ready() (crates/miroir-proxy/tests/p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs) is present and correct. Completed that with_context message to mirror the ensure! wording; both branches now bail immediately instead of polling to READY_TIMEOUT, and ready requires body == {"status":"available"} exactly. issue.description:
Apply the p13_12 lesson to the new p13_13 tests. In p13_12_cache_failure_handling.rs, acceptance assertions like 'stats.hits >= 0' on unsigned counters could never fail - clippy flagged them as absurd extreme comparisons, and the fix (commit 3ca59fe) replaced them with real bounds (hits+misses<=20, entries<=20, entries==1, hits==1) each with a comment explaining the vacuous comparison. The new p13_13 files (crates/miroir-proxy/tests/p13_13_cache_flow_handling.rs, p13_13_node_invocation_proof.rs) were written after that lesson and clippy-clean, but clippy only catches some of these - semantic dead assertions need eyes.

READ-THROUGH SCOPE (both p13_13 test files):
- No assertion that can never fire: min/max comparisons on unsigned/bool types, len() >= 0, comparisons against the type's own MIN/MAX.
- No dead scaffolding: the p13_10 pass removed an unwired MockNodeClient/call_count pair; check p13_13 helpers (spawned nodes, clients, keys) are actually exercised by at least one assertion.
- Bounds that ARE asserted should be meaningful: could the assertion fail on a real regression (e.g. cache evicting early, a node invocation skipped)? If a bound is intentional but non-obvious, add a one-line comment in the same style as the p13_12 ones.
- Reason from the actual semantics (ResultCache LRU behavior, failed ops short-circuit before touching inner cache) rather than from the lint.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Zero absurd-extreme-comparison or equivalent lints under -D warnings (already implied by the lint child, re-confirmed).
- Every p13_13 acceptance assertion can fail on a plausible regression; each non-obvious intentional bound carries a comment.
- Findings and reasoning recorded in this bead's notes (including 'nothing found' if the tests are clean).

Actual file under review is crates/miroir-proxy/tests/p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs (10 tests) — the task text's p13_13_cache_flow_handling.rs / p13_13_node_invocation_proof.rs names are stale.

VERDICT PER AREA:

(1) DEAD SCAFFOLDING — NOTHING FOUND. Both audits: every helper, field, and fixture is exercised by at least one assertion (wait_for_ready, search, metric, create_index/add_documents/set_node_settings, PROXY_SLOT, NODE/PROXY_MASTER_KEY, proxy_config_yaml); every never-read field (_proxy_slot/_containers/_proxy) is a documented drop-guard in the 3ca59fe style. Every counter bound rests on verified ground truth: fresh proxy process per test (own Metrics registry); hit path inc_result_cache_hits (search.rs:522) strictly precedes the early return (:556), which precedes both record_scatter_fan_out sites — a served hit structurally cannot fan out; miss wires (:561 deserialize-Err, :567 Ok(None)) fire exactly once per miss; lookup Err (:573-576) records NEITHER counter; insert awaited (:944) before the response is built (:1007), so an entry is durable before the client sees resp1; proxy_counter reads an absent series as Ok(0); scatter_fan_out_size is a histogram, _count +1 per fan-out EVENT (not per node). Four documented leans, none vacuous (all fail loudly): coalescing inert only by sequencing (sits before the cache lookup, subscribe-only, sequential tests — would eat hits deltas if a repeat loop ever parallelizes); task-apply-by-fixed-sleep(500ms) in fixtures; 500ms ttl vs pacing (acceptance_4 hits+4 most exposed — hits never refresh expiry); foreign-process port poisoning (/health is identity-free; mitigated by PROXY_SLOT + pre-flight; memory note p13-13-fixed-ports-contention).

(2) NEVER-FIRING COMPARISONS, acceptance_1-5 — one real gap, FIXED in 49deb4f; otherwise NOTHING FOUND. The gap: acceptance_5 varied limit without pinning it — every query pair differed on q, so a limit-omitting cache key passed all asserts; the prior 'needs >10 matching docs' scoping note was WRONG because the misses delta detects a key collision at ANY dataset size (the colliding query arrives as a recorded hit replay and the delta falls short). Fix: query4 = {q: desk, limit: 20} shares query2's text and differs only by limit; first-pass misses/scatter deltas and repeat hits re-anchored +3->+4; trailing flat compares re-anchored to the first pass; no assert_ne for the 2/4 pair (one Desk doc, rows equal by construction — commented). Key-dimension scope, recorded so no future sweep re-derives it: index_name and settings_version are pinned at the UNIT level (result_cache.rs test_cache_key_creation; p13_10 acc_7; p13_11 acc_6) but their LIVE-PATH wiring is beyond any p13_13 fixture's claim (one index per test; settings_version varied only via acceptance_9's patch, whose body equality a version-ignoring replay also satisfies).

(3) NEVER-FIRING COMPARISONS, acceptance_6-10 — three real defects FIXED (0e20c0b), one gap strengthened (0f3bfd9), one deliberate. acceptance_7: assert_eq!(result1,result2) held whether the repeat re-scattered or was served an entry past its TTL — the acceptance's own regression was invisible; now pinned by misses==+2 and scatter==+2 (q2 must miss past the 500ms ttl) with sleep-anchoring documented. acceptance_9: (a) if-let-Ok around the settings PATCH swallowed transport errors and skipped the whole acceptance while passing — now unconditional with a status assert; (b) body equality cannot see a stale entry surviving invalidation — now misses==+2/scatter==+2, keyed on the two-phase broadcast commit bumping settings_version (settings.rs:239) into the cache key (search.rs:497). acceptance_10: facetDistribution equality was implied by the whole-body equality two lines above (never fires independently) — removed; replaced with hits==+1, the exactly-one-fan-out pin, and the flat bypass check. acceptance_6: no cache failure is injectable against the in-process cache (every get/insert returns Ok) — previously only status+len asserted (nothing cache-flow-shaped could fail it); now pins the degrade flow: misses==+1, scatter==+1, with real failure injection scoped to the p13_12 unit suite. acceptance_8: deliberately counter-free, comment in place — coalesced in-flight duplicates make any hit/miss split flake; the row-identity asserts can fire.

(4) REGRESSION-SENSITIVITY OF THE REMAINING BOUNDS — every remaining bound maps to a named regression (full per-assertion map on miroir-50364550; acceptance_1-5 table on miroir-ddb83593), reasoned from ResultCache LRU behaviour and failed-op short-circuit semantics, not from the lint: ttl anchored at insert, hits never refresh it, an expired lookup pops the entry and counts a miss (so eviction/ttl-stall regressions shorten hits deltas, never pass silently); LRU at max_size 1000 cannot fire at <=4 distinct keys per test (not a vacuous-bound vector); lookup Err records NEITHER counter, so cache fail-open surfaces as failed misses+scatter deltas; insert Err is debug-log-only, so store-never-landing surfaces as a short hits delta on the repeat; a hit-that-still-scatters passes the hits delta but lands on the scatter pin. All counter bounds are == on deltas against pre-read baselines in the same process; the four flat compares (acc_1/2/3/5 scatter) are each pinned non-vacuous by a preceding same-metric ==+N in the SAME test, so an unwired/dead metrics route dies at 0!=1 before any 0==0 could hold. Failure direction re-confirmed LIVE on 2026-09-12: with the route broken (see below), every test dies at its FIRST status assert — no delta is ever reached by luck.

issue.description:
Child 1 of 4 in the miroir-77a3dce4 umbrella split. The parent's notes carry the consolidated findings ledger — run `bead show miroir-77a3dce4` first, then re-verify rather than trusting it.

TARGET: acceptance_1_cache_hit_bypasses_fan_out in crates/miroir-proxy/tests/p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs (function starts ~L449 in the current tree; re-anchor before citing).

For every assert in the test, reason from the counter mapping (the hit path in crates/miroir-proxy/src/routes/search.rs) whether it can fail on a plausible regression — not from the lint, since clippy's absurd-extreme-comparison only catches the mechanical subset:
- scatter_after_first == scatter_before + 1: must fire at 0 if the uncached fan-out is unwired and >= 2 on a doubled scatter.
- hits_after == hits_before + 1: must fire when the repeat query is recorded as a miss (entry not stored, lookup regression, unwired metric) or when cached bytes fail deserialization (that path re-fans-out and records a miss, search.rs ~:561); the 500 ms ttl_ms stall surface must stay documented.

Ground truth: the hit path increments the hit counter (~:522) and returns the cached response (~:556) BEFORE both record_scatter_fan_out call sites (~:811 single-index, ~:1406 multi-target). It must compare two distinct counter reads, never a value with itself.

issue.notes:

VERDICT: acceptance_1_cache_hit_bypasses_fan_out (test fn at p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs:449) — every assert confirmed fail-able on a named plausible regression; NOTHING FOUND, NOTHING TO CHANGE. NOTE: the parent ledger's anchors have drifted AGAIN (it cites L503-507/L533-537/L543-546/L495-496; actual are L510-514/L540-544/L550-553/L502-503) — anchors below are exact.

PER-ASSERT FINDINGS (test file; all deltas via proxy_counter whose Ok(0) fallback makes a dead metrics endpoint FAIL the deltas, never pass silently):
- :500 resp1.status().is_success() — infra bound; fires if the uncached query errors. Empirically demonstrated today: it fired in a contaminated run (see observation below). Nothing found.
- :502 row count assert_eq!(result1["hits"].as_array().unwrap().len(), 1) — .as_array().unwrap() panics on a non-array hits (shape regression); len()==1 fails on empty (0) or duplicate merge output (2). Nothing found.
- :503 row content assert_eq!(result1["hits"][0]["name"], "Laptop") — fires on wrong-row/dropped-field regressions. Nothing found.
- :510-514 scatter_after_first == scatter_before + 1 — exactly-once fan-out. Fires at 0 if record_scatter_fan_out is unwired/renamed (delta 0) or the scatter path stops recording; fires at >=2 on a doubled record (retry or per-node instead of per-plan recording). Ground truth: middleware.rs:1834-1836 scatter_fan_out_size.observe() — the histogram _count the test reads increments exactly once per call, so a doubled call is observable; two distinct reads at :487 and :507. Nothing found.
- :526 resp2.status().is_success() — infra; fires if the hit path errors (e.g. the serde_json::to_string unwrap at search.rs:554 panicking aborts the handler as a 500). Nothing found.
- :531 assert_eq!(result1, result2) — two DISTINCT HTTP bodies (result1 fetched on the scatter path :494, result2 on the hit path :527), not self-equality; fires on cached-body corruption that still deserializes. Correctly documented at :529-530 as unable to detect a bypass on its own. Nothing found.
- :540-544 hits_after == hits_before + 1 — fires when the repeat query is recorded as a miss: entry not stored (delta 0), lookup regression Ok(None) (search.rs:567 records a miss; hit delta 0), unwired hit metric (delta 0), cached bytes fail deserialization (search.rs:561 records a miss and falls through to re-fan-out; hit delta 0), TTL stall >500ms (reads as a lookup regression; documented at :533-536). Boundary case, deliberately accepted: a pure swap of the hit/miss inc calls leaves this delta at +1 spuriously (miss recorded as hit on query 1, real hit recorded as miss on query 2) — but the same swap is caught by acceptance_2's misses_after_first == misses_before+1 against the same proxy binary, so the SUITE has no hole; making this assert immune would just duplicate acceptance_2's miss delta. Nothing found.
- :550-553 scatter_after_second == scatter_after_first — THE bypass assert. Ground truth re-verified in the current tree: the hit path increments the hit counter at search.rs:522 and returns the cached response at search.rs:556, BEFORE both record_scatter_fan_out call sites (search.rs:811 single-index plan, :1406 multi-target plan) — a served hit cannot reach either record site unless the early return is removed/moved. It compares two separate counter reads (:507 vs :547), never a value with itself; fires at +1 if the hit path falls through to the scatter. The search.rs:465 request-coalescing return is a different, earlier short-circuit (before the cache lookup) that also skips scatter recording; the test's sequential queries never coalesce, so it cannot mask the bypass comparison. Nothing found.

TAXONOMY SWEEP (independent): no unsigned >= 0, no comparisons against a type MIN/MAX, no self-equality, no asserts on state the test never varies; every counter delta spans state the test itself varies. 3ca59fe-style comments verified present on every non-obvious bound: :481-483 (deltas over body equality), :505-506 (exactly-once fan-out), :529-530 (body equality cannot detect the bypass), :533-536 (TTL stall reads as a lookup regression), :546 (served hit must short-circuit the fan-out).

The failures were environmental contention, NOT product or assert regressions, and this bead's verdict does not rest on that run. I did not kill or interfere with the foreign process. Consequence worth a follow-up bead: a foreign process on 17770/9090 can make wait_for_ready pass and produce silently wrong test evidence; a pre-flight bind probe (or failing setup when the port is foreign-held) would harden it.

Catches auth/key rejection (401), absent route, upstream failure surfacing as 5xx. Later unwraps shadow it for JSON error bodies, but this is the only bound that names the condition for non-JSON bodies.
2. L509 assert_eq!(result1["hits"].as_array().unwrap().len(), 1) — FIRES. "laptop" vs 3 seeded docs must yield exactly 1 row. Catches broken query forwarding/indexing (len 0) and over-broad matching (len > 1). Dynamic value vs nonzero concrete literal — not an unsigned-vs-zero tautology.

Both branches lock-free (children 1-2 grep zero .read()/.write()/.lock().await in middleware.rs + auth.rs; my re-grep concurs).
- Confusion guard (child 1 nuance, restated because it is the one live trap in this row): POST /search/products IS a real route and IS the wedged control path — different prefix, never reachable from /indexes.

== ROW 2: GET /indexes -> 200 in 259us — LOCK SET = EMPTY in the proxy (LOCKS NONE). ATTRIBUTION RESOLVED: PROXY-SERVED via the proxy's own lock-free list_indexes_handler. Round-11's correction is RIGHT against current source; round-10's "served by the NODE process" was mechanism-wrong. ==
- The route EXISTS on the proxy: indexes.rs:309 `.route("/", post(create_index_handler).get(list_indexes_handler))` under the main.rs:850 nest. Nothing bypasses the proxy.
- Handler re-derived line-by-line, list_indexes_handler indexes.rs:471-492: sole extractor Extension(Arc<Config>) (:471-473) — NO State, hence no AppState: no topology, session_manager, query_coalescer, result_cache, or Redis. Child 1/4 of the miroir-1ec135a1 umbrella split (diagnose-before-fix chain). Signature A = 9/10 p13_13 acceptance tests panicking with `assertion failed: resp.status().is_success()` at their FIRST proxy search POST (assert lines 508/622/738/858/959/1023/1068/1135/1196 in the freshest 05:52 run; crates/miroir-proxy/tests/p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs). The working tree carries uncommitted changes to crates/miroir-proxy/src/routes/search.rs (the live search path; currently 26 insertions / 58 deletions, a result-cache key-reuse rework).

Task: read `git diff crates/miroir-proxy/src/routes/search.rs` hunk by hunk and deliver a verdict — does this diff explain signature A?

Method:
- For each hunk, decide whether it can change the response STATUS of the first search POST or panic/abort the handler mid-request.
- Locate the handler's status-decision sites (the 503/500/200 decisions) and confirm whether they sit inside or outside the hunks.
- Structural check: a handler panic would drop the connection and fail at the test's `.send().await.unwrap()`; the observed failure is a well-formed non-2xx ASSERTION, so decide whether any hunk could produce a deliberate 4xx/5xx response.
- Cross-check the preserved run logs in docs/notes/p13-13-live-run-logs-2026-09-11.md (committed e9c5702; /tmp copies may be gone): readiness was reached in ~205ms and a well-formed response came back every time.

issue.notes:
# VERDICT: the uncommitted search.rs diff does NOT explain signature A

`git diff crates/miroir-proxy/src/routes/search.rs` = 5 hunks, 26 insertions /
58 deletions (diffstat re-verified against the task's claim). No hunk touches a
status-decision site, none can produce a 4xx/5xx response, none can panic
mid-request. Signature A's 404 comes from axum routing, before search_handler
is ever invoked — a request the diff cannot influence. Independent pass; it
confirms the committed diagnosis (docs/notes/p13-13-root-cause-diagnosis.md:96-109).

## Hunk-by-hunk semantic summary

H1  @@ -476,6 +476,16 (search.rs:479-487) — comment + pure declaration:
    `let mut result_cache_key: Option<miroir_core::result_cache::CacheKey> = None;`
    Default-None bookkeeping ahead of the existing cache-lookup block. No
    behavior, no status path.

H2  @@ -501,6 +511,7 (search.rs:514) — infallible capture, inserted after
    `CacheKey::new(...)` inside the pre-existing `if !canonicalized_query.is_empty()`:
    `result_cache_key = Some(cache_key.clone());`
    CacheKey is `{ hash: u64 }` (miroir-core/src/result_cache.rs:67-70) — clone
    cannot fail. The subsequent `result_cache.get(&cache_key)` is unchanged and
    the entire cache-hit 200 path (search.rs:517-557, status decision at :531)
    is untouched.

H3  @@ -800,9 +811,8 (search.rs:813-815) — comment reword + deletion of
    `let facets_for_cache = body.facets.clone();`. The deleted binding has ZERO
    remaining references in the tree (grep over crates/ empty) — it was consumed
    only by the store block H5 deletes. Compile-health is proven by the live
    runs: the suite built from this working tree and reached in-test asserts.

H4  @@ -824,7 +834,6 (search.rs:834-836) — deletion of
    `let capture_body_for_cache = rest_body.clone();`. Same as H3: zero
    remaining references; `capture_body` (canary capture, used at search.rs:961)
    is untouched.

H5  @@ -927,61 +936,20 (search.rs:937-956) — the only substantive hunk: the
    ~50-line post-scatter store block is replaced by
    ```rust
    if let Some(cache_key) = result_cache_key {
        if let Ok(response_bytes) = serde_json::to_vec(&body) {
            match state.result_cache.insert(cache_key, response_bytes).await {
                Ok(_) => { debug!(...) }
                Err(e) => { debug!(...) }
            }
        }
    }
    ```
    Every fallible operation is swallowed (`if let Ok` for to_vec, match→debug!
    for insert). No `?`, no unwrap/expect, no panic, no early return, no
    `Response::builder()` anywhere in the hunk. It runs AFTER the response body
    is fully built and BEFORE the final 200 — it cannot alter that status.

## Status-decision sites — ALL outside every hunk

Hunks span search.rs 479-487 / 514 / 813-816 / 834-836 / 937-956. Decisions:
- 429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS: search.rs:220, :243 (rate limit, pre-hunks)
- 403 FORBIDDEN: search.rs:370
- 500 (coalesced-response deserialize fail): search.rs:428
- 200 OK (coalesced return): search.rs:436
- 200 OK (cache-hit return): search.rs:531 (H1/H2 adjacent but inert here)
- 500 (bad unavailable_shard_policy): search.rs:695
- 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE (version-floor planning failure): search.rs:790
- 500 (dfs_query_then_fetch_search error): search.rs:910
- 200 OK (final success): search.rs:1008

## Structural check

Signature A panics at the ASSERT (p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs:508 style),
meaning `.send().await.unwrap()` at :506 SUCCEEDED — a well-formed HTTP
response arrived and was merely non-2xx. A handler panic would surface at :506
as `Result::unwrap()` on an Err (dropped connection). Preserved logs
(p13-13-live-run-logs-2026-09-11.md, e9c5702) contain 16
`assertion failed: resp.status().is_success()` panics across the three runs and
ZERO connection-level failures (no reqwest send Err / hyper IncompleteMessage /
connection reset); readiness 203.98-209.84ms (~205ms) on all 30 tests. The diff
has no code path emitting 4xx/5xx. The actual 404 source: search::router
registers only `.route("/:index", axum::routing::post(search_handler))`
(search.rs:128) nested at "/search" (main.rs:852) → POST /search/:index only;
the suite POSTs /indexes/products/search (test :501) which matches no route →
axum 404 with empty body before search_handler runs.

## Semantic change (for child 2's live capture)

The diff's ONLY semantic effect is cache-STORE correctness. Old code re-derived
the store key post-scatter: re-read settings_version at STORE time and rebuilt
a SearchRequestBody from captured clones with `ranking_score:
Some(client_requested_score)` — a key that could differ from the one the lookup
computed (lookup canonicalizes `serde_json::to_value(&body)` at search.rs:497),
so stores could land where the next identical lookup never looks. New code
reuses the lookup-time key verbatim. Capture implication: a second identical
query can cache-HIT on the diffed tree where the pre-diff tree may MISS forever
(and stores now carry lookup-time settings_version, not a possibly newer
store-time one) — cache-hit/miss counter deltas may legitimately differ with vs
without the diff, but response STATUS is 200 on both paths either way. Do not
read a hit-count delta as evidence for/against signature A.

Disposition: do NOT revert the diff as part of the fix (matches
p13-13-root-cause-diagnosis.md "Other findings" #2).

issue.notes:
p13_13 counter map (groundwork for umbrella miroir-77a3dce4). Refs: src/routes/search.rs, tests/p13_13_cache_flow_integration.rs.

METRIC WIRING: all three names are minted in middleware.rs — counters at :620/:626, histogram "miroir_scatter_fan_out_size" at :598-605 — label-less, exposed via helpers inc_result_cache_hits (:1848), inc_result_cache_misses (:1852), record_scatter_fan_out (:1834, histogram observe; the test reads the histogram's _count sample). proxy_counter (test :426-435) matches the first whitespace token per exposition line and returns 0 for a missing metric, so a regression that unregisters a metric reads as "flat", not as an error.

1) miroir_result_cache_hits_total — ONE site in this route: search.rs:522, reached only when lookup returns Ok(Some(bytes)) AND serde_json::from_slice succeeds; handler returns the cached response at search.rs:556. (multi_search.rs:359 is the only other site; not exercised here.) Plausible regression that moves it: key divergence between store and lookup — recomputing the key at store time instead of reusing result_cache_key, or a settings-version bump between write and read — makes the repeat query miss; hits delta goes +0, failing acceptance_1 L533-537 and acceptance_2 L645-649.

2) miroir_result_cache_misses_total — TWO sites: search.rs:567 (lookup Ok(None), the true miss) and search.rs:561 (Ok(Some(bytes)) that fail to deserialize — fail-open as a miss, falls through to the fan-out). Plausible regression: hit demoted to miss (arm swap or an over-eager freshness recheck) — acceptance_1's repeat query then records a miss and a second fan-out, failing hits L533-537 (+0) and scatter L543-546 (+1 instead of +0). Conversely a dropped increment in the Ok(None) arm fails acceptance_2 L613-617.

3) miroir_scatter_fan_out_size_count — TWO observe sites: search.rs:811 in search_handler (node_count = plan.shard_to_node.len() at :808) and search.rs:1406 in search_multi_targets (node_count at :1403). The single-target queries these tests send reach only :811. Plausible regression: hit-path return dropped or moved below planning — a second fan-out runs and acceptance_1 L543-546 fails; a planning change altering shard_to_node size breaks the exact +1 deltas at acceptance_1 L503-507 and acceptance_2 L621-625.

SHORT-CIRCUIT (verified by reading control flow, not the comments): in search_handler the hit branch returns at search.rs:556. Both record_scatter_fan_out sites are strictly downstream: :811 sits after planning (~:780-807) in the same function; :1406 is inside search_multi_targets, reachable only via the resolved_targets.len() > 1 delegation at :600-613, which the hit return precedes — and the lookup guard at :491 already excludes multi-target from caching. A served hit cannot reach either site. The deserialize-failure miss (:561) is the only cache-counter path that still fans out; only the true hit short-circuits.

LOOKUP-ERROR FAIL-OPEN (search.rs:573-576): get() returning Err logs at debug and records NEITHER cache counter, then falls through to the full scatter (:811 fires, +1). result_cache_key is set to Some at search.rs:514 BEFORE the get() match, so the store at :941 still runs on the error path and files the entry. Consequences: a transient lookup error on acceptance_2's first query is caught ONLY by the miss delta L613-617 (+0 vs expected +1) — the scatter delta L621-625 still passes (+1 from the fail-open fan-out) and the hit delta L645-649 still PASSES because the repeat query finds the entry that same request stored. Under a persistent lookup error, acceptance_1 L533-537 also catches (a hit can never be served). No delta alone distinguishes lookup-Err from cache-disabled on the scatter/hit axes.

DORMANT NEIGHBOR: query coalescing defaults ON (miroir-core config.rs:140, asserted :625) and is not overridden in the generated test config (test :216). Its served-coalesced early-return (search.rs:465) bumps only miroir_query_coalesce_hits_total — none of the three counters — so it reads flat on every delta. The acceptance tests are sequential, so try_coalesce finds no in-flight twin and the path stays dormant; a future test that fires identical queries concurrently would see a coalesced second query look exactly like a lookup regression (miss flat, hits flat, scatter flat).

- L617 assert!(resp.status().is_success()): fires on any non-2xx for a well-formed, correctly-authenticated search (routing/auth/serialization regression); also keeps L618's .json() from parsing an error body into a confusing secondary failure. Counter-mapped: the miss path answers 200 only after a successful scatter.

issue.description:
## Phase 6 Epic — Horizontal Scaling + HPA

Delivers the §14 promise: **fixed per-pod envelope (2 vCPU / 3.75 GB), scale out never up**. Makes the request path strictly stateless and partitions background work across pods via one of three coordination modes.

## Why This Is A Phase

Plan §1 principle 8 + plan §14 are the architectural spine. Phase 2's proxy already runs on one pod; this phase makes N pods coherent. Every §13 feature's "Scaling mode" column in plan §14.6 gets wired up here — Phase 5's implementations have to already understand they'll run inside one of the three modes.

## Scope

**14.1–14.3 — Per-pod envelope**
- `resources.requests` = 500m / 1Gi; `resources.limits` = 2000m / 3584Mi
- Per-feature memory row validated against plan §14.2 budget
- CPU budget per plan §14.3 (~3 kQPS/pod small responses)

**14.4 — Request path HPA**
- `autoscaling/v2` HPA on CPU 70%, memory 75%, `miroir_requests_in_flight` as `type: Pods` `AverageValue: 500`, `miroir_background_queue_depth` as `type: External` `Value: 10` (plan §14.4 note on metric types)
- `prometheus-adapter` as a chart prerequisite when HPA is enabled
- `values.schema.json` rejects `hpa.enabled=true` without `replicas >= 2 AND taskStore.backend = redis`

**14.5 — Background coordination modes**
- **Mode A — Shard-partitioned ownership** (anti-entropy §13.8, settings-drift check §13.5, task registry pruner, TTL sweeper §13.14, canary runner §13.18)
- **Mode B — Leader-only lease** (reshard coordinator §13.1, rebalancer Phase 4, alias flip serializer §13.7, two-phase settings broadcast §13.5, ILM evaluator §13.17, scoped-key rotation leader §13.21)
- **Mode C — Work-queued chunked jobs** (streaming dump import §13.9, large reshard backfill §13.1)
- **Peer discovery** via headless Service (`miroir-headless`) + Downward API `POD_NAME`/`POD_IP`, 15s SRV refresh
- Rendezvous over peer set for Mode A; `SET NX EX 10` renewed every 3s for Mode B
- Job lease heartbeat every 10s with 30s timeout for Mode C

**14.6 — Per-feature scaling-mode wiring** — 21 rows, each must compile against the chosen mode

**14.7 — Deployment sizing matrix** — ops documentation/tooling surfacing orchestrator pod count vs. corpus × QPS tiers

**14.8 — Resource-aware defaults** — every config knob's default sized for the envelope

**14.9 — Resource-pressure metrics + alerts** — `miroir_memory_pressure`, `miroir_cpu_throttled_seconds_total`, `miroir_request_queue_depth`, `miroir_background_queue_depth{job_type}`, `miroir_peer_pod_count`, `miroir_leader`, `miroir_owned_shards_count`; PrometheusRule alerts

**14.10 — Vertical-scaling escape valve** — documented as supported but not recommended; no implementation work, just docs

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Multi-pod deployment (replicas=3) — every pod independently serves requests with identical routing
- [ ] Kill one of three pods mid-traffic — zero client-visible errors beyond retry budget (plan §8 chaos)
- [ ] Mode A test: spin up 3 pods, anti-entropy runs exactly once per shard per interval cluster-wide
- [ ] Mode B test: start 3 pods, exactly one holds the reshard lease at any given instant; killing it promotes another within `lease_ttl_s`
- [ ] Mode C test: submit a 10GB dump; chunks distribute across 3 pods and HPA reacts to `miroir_background_queue_depth`
- [ ] All §14.2 memory rows fit within 3584 MiB under realistic steady-state load
- [ ] All §14.9 alerts present in the PrometheusRule manifest and trip under induced fault

issue.description:
## What

Implement pod sizing per plan §14.1 + §14.2 + §14.8:
- Helm `deployment.yaml` sets `resources.requests = {cpu: 500m, memory: 1Gi}`
- `resources.limits = {cpu: 2000m, memory: 3584Mi}` (plan §14.8: "leaves headroom under 3.75 GB node limit")
- Config defaults sized for the envelope (§14.8 full YAML)

## Why

Plan §1 principle 8: "Fixed per-pod resource envelope (2 vCPU / 3.75 GB). When aggregate workload exceeds this envelope, scale **horizontally** by adding pods, never vertically beyond the envelope."

Without enforced limits, a runaway per-feature cache (e.g., session_pinning.max_sessions set unreasonably high) can push a pod into OOM-kill territory, inviting HPA to spin up replacements instead of surfacing the misconfiguration.

## Details

**Per-feature memory rows** (plan §14.2) each need their defaults:

| Component | Budget | Knob |
|-----------|--------|------|
| Runtime + axum | 80 MB | — |
| HTTP/2 pools | 50 MB | `connection_pool_per_node` |
| Req/resp buffers | 200 MB | `server.max_body_bytes`, `max_concurrent_requests` |
| Task registry | 100 MB | `task_registry.cache_size` |
| Idempotency | 100 MB | `idempotency.max_cached_keys` |
| Sessions | 50 MB | `session_pinning.max_sessions` |
| Coalescing | 50 MB | `query_coalescing.max_subscribers` |
| Router + EWMA | 20 MB | fixed |
| Plan cache | 20 MB | fixed |
| Alias table | 10 MB | fixed |
| Metrics | 50 MB | fixed |
| Dump import buffer | 128 MB | `dump_import.memory_buffer_bytes` (only during import) |
| Anti-entropy | 128 MB | `anti_entropy.max_read_concurrency` (only during pass) |
| Multi-search scratch | 5 MB | `multi_search.max_queries_per_batch` |
| Vector over-fetch | 30 MB | `vector_search.over_fetch_factor` |
| CDC buffer | 64 MB | `cdc.buffer.memory_bytes` |
| TTL cursor | 5 MB | — |
| Tenant map LRU | 20 MB | `tenant_affinity.mode` |
| Shadow tee | ~50 MB | `shadow.targets[].sample_rate` |
| Canary state | 20 MB | `canary_runner.run_history_per_canary` |
| Admin UI assets | 10 MB | fixed |
| Explain cache | 10 MB | fixed |
| Search UI assets | 10 MB | fixed |
| Search UI rate limiter | 20 MB (Redis-backed) | — |
| Allocator overhead | 800 MB | — |
| **Steady-state total** | **~1.2 GB** | |

**Regression budget**: add a CI check (Phase 9) that flags when steady-state under synthetic load exceeds 1.7 GB.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Helm rendered manifest matches the requests/limits above
- [ ] Idle pod < 300 MB RSS on a 3-node cluster
- [ ] Steady-state (1 kQPS across 3 Miroir pods) under 1.2 GB per pod
- [ ] One heavy background job (dump import) adds < 500 MB to that pod's total

issue.description:
## What

Implement peer discovery per plan §14.5:
- Helm `miroir-headless.yaml` — a headless Service with label selector on the Deployment
- Deployment: Downward API injects `POD_NAME` + `POD_IP` as env vars
- Each pod refreshes peer set every `peer_discovery.refresh_interval_s` (default 15s) via SRV lookup against `miroir-headless.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local`
- Peer set is `Vec<PeerId>` where `PeerId = POD_NAME` — used by rendezvous for Mode A ownership

## Why

Plan §14.5: "All three modes rely on the current peer set." Mode A rendezvous partitions by peer × work-item; Mode B leader election picks one peer; Mode C claim lease is by peer. Without a peer set, we'd need either a central registry (new dependency) or K8s API calls (requires RBAC + API server load).

SRV-based discovery is zero-config — if headless Service exists, it just works.

## Details

**Manifest** (plan §14.5 + §6):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: miroir-headless
spec:
  clusterIP: None
  selector:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: miroir
  ports: [...]
```

**Env injection** (plan §14.5 "Peer discovery"):
```yaml
env:
- name: POD_NAME
  valueFrom: { fieldRef: { fieldPath: metadata.name } }
- name: POD_IP
  valueFrom: { fieldRef: { fieldPath: status.podIP } }
```

**Rust side**:
```rust
pub struct PeerSet { pub peers: Vec<PeerId>, pub refreshed_at: Instant }
pub async fn refresh_peers(service: &str) -> PeerSet { /* SRV lookup */ }
```

**Transient double-work** is acceptable (plan §14.5): "15-second discovery window is harmless: anti-entropy is idempotent, settings-repair is idempotent."

## Acceptance

- [ ] 3-pod deployment: each pod sees all 3 peer names within 30s of last pod ready
- [ ] Scale 3→5: new peers discovered within `refresh_interval_s × 2`
- [ ] Pod eviction: crashed pod drops from peer set within `refresh_interval_s × 2`
- [ ] `miroir_peer_pod_count` gauge matches `kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready`
issue.title: P6.2 Peer discovery via headless Service + Downward API

issue.description:
## What

Implement plan §14.5 Mode A rendezvous-partitioned ownership:
```
owns(shard_or_item, pod) = pod == top1_by_score(hash(item || pid) for pid in peer_set)
```

Applied to:
- §13.8 anti-entropy reconciler — each pod fingerprints/repairs owned shards
- §13.5 settings drift checker — each pod polls subset of (index, node) settings-hash pairs
- Task registry pruner — each pod prunes tasks it owns by `top1_by_score(hash(miroir_id || pid))`
- §13.14 TTL sweeper — each pod sweeps owned shards
- §13.18 canary runner — each canary ID rendezvous-owned by one pod per interval

## Why

Plan §14.5: "No explicit handoff — the new owner runs the next scheduled pass. Transient double-work during a 15-second discovery window is harmless." Mode A is naturally horizontal (work scales with peer count) and idempotent (safe during rescheduling).

## Details

**Ownership function** (reuses Phase 1 `score` with item:pod keys instead of shard:node):
```rust
pub fn owns<T: Hash>(item: &T, self_pod: &PeerId, peers: &[PeerId]) -> bool {
    peers.iter()
        .max_by_key(|pid| score_item_peer(item, pid))
        .map_or(false, |top| top == self_pod)
}
```

**Scheduled runs**: each Mode A worker is a tokio task with a tick interval. On tick:
1. Refresh peer set
2. For each eligible item, check `owns(item, self)` and process if so
3. Record progress per-item so rescheduling mid-run resumes cleanly

**Phase 5 integration**: each §13.x subsection that declared "Mode A" in plan §14.6 calls into this layer rather than implementing its own peer-partitioning.

## Acceptance

- [ ] 3 pods running anti-entropy: each shard processed exactly once per interval cluster-wide
- [ ] Kill one pod mid-pass: its shards reassigned to other peers within `refresh_interval_s × 2`; no shard processed by two pods simultaneously beyond the 15s window
- [ ] Unit test: `owns()` returns true for exactly one peer per item across the peer set
- [ ] Integration: induce divergence; Mode A anti-entropy converges across 3 pods with no double-repair
issue.title: P6.3 Mode A: shard-partitioned ownership (anti-entropy, drift, TTL, canaries, pruner)

issue.description:
## What

Implement plan §14.5 Mode B leader-only lease:
- SQLite: advisory lock row in `leader_lease` (plan §4) — the lease holder is recorded so recovery reads the last committed phase state
- Redis: `SET <key> <pod_id> NX EX 10` renewed every 3s
- Leader-loss mid-operation: pause; new leader reads persisted phase state and resumes at the last committed phase boundary
- All Mode B operations are designed to be **idempotent** and safe to resume at phase boundaries

Lease scopes (plan §14.6):
- §13.1 reshard coordinator: `reshard:<index>`
- Phase 4 rebalancer: `rebalance:<index>` (or global `rebalance`)
- §13.7 alias flip serializer: `alias_flip:<name>`
- §13.5 two-phase settings broadcast: `settings_broadcast:<index>`
- §13.17 ILM evaluator: `ilm`
- §13.21 scoped-key rotation: `search_ui_key_rotation:<index>`

## Why

Plan §14.5: "Leader loss mid-operation causes a pause; the new leader reads the persisted phase state from the task store and resumes from the last committed phase. All operations are idempotent by design and safe to resume at any phase boundary."

Without lease-based coordination, two pods could each run a reshard on the same index simultaneously → double shadow creation, conflicting alias flips, data corruption.

## Details

**Lease renewal**: every 3s (`leader_election.renew_interval_s`); TTL 10s (`leader_election.lease_ttl_s`). If renewal fails, leader gives up voluntarily to reduce split-brain.

**Phase state persistence**: each Mode B operation persists enough state after each phase so resumption picks up where the dead leader left off:
- Reshard: current phase ∈ {shadow, backfill, verify, swap, cleanup} + per-shard cursor
- 2PC broadcast: current phase ∈ {propose, verify, commit} + per-node ACK list
- ILM: per-policy next-check-time + in-flight rollover state

**Config**:
```yaml
leader_election:
  enabled: true                      # auto-true when replicas > 1
  lease_ttl_s: 10
  renew_interval_s: 3
```

**SQLite substitute**: for single-pod dev, the `leader_lease` row is still written (so recovery can read the last committed phase state after a crash); lease semantics reduced to "always-leader."

**Metrics**: `miroir_leader` gauge (1 if this pod is leader, 0 otherwise).

## Acceptance

- [ ] 3 pods: exactly one is leader at any instant; killing it promotes another within `lease_ttl_s`
- [ ] Kill the leader during reshard phase 3 (verify); new leader resumes at phase 3, not phase 1
- [ ] Kill the leader during 2PC phase 2 (verify); new leader resumes verify without re-applying phase 1
- [ ] `miroir_leader` sum across all pods is always 1 (or 0 transiently during failover)
issue.title: P6.4 Mode B: leader-only singleton coordinator (reshard, rebalance, alias flip, 2PC, ILM, scoped-key rotation)

issue.description:
## What

Implement plan §14.5 Mode C work-queued chunked jobs:
- `jobs` table (Phase 3) with states `queued | in_progress | completed | failed`
- Any pod can `claim_job(pod_id)` — atomic compare-and-swap `claimed_by IS NULL → claimed_by = pod_id`
- Claim TTL: `claim_expires_at`, heartbeat every 10s, timeout 30s — pod loss → claim expires → another picks up
- Large jobs **split into chunks** on input boundaries by the first pod that picks them up
- Per-chunk progress persisted so crashed claims resume at last committed offset (idempotent via primary keys)

Applied to:
- §13.9 streaming dump import — chunks on NDJSON line boundaries, `chunk_size_bytes` default 256 MiB
- §13.1 reshard backfill — partitions by shard-id range

## Why

Plan §14.5: "Heavy streaming operations can exceed a single pod's envelope." A 500 GB dump is easily 10× a pod's memory budget — must chunk.

Plan §14.4 HPA: `miroir_background_queue_depth` gauge → HPA scales out when backlog grows; scales back in when drained.

## Details

**Chunking**: first pod that picks up a large job inspects the input, computes split points, and re-enqueues per-chunk jobs. Original job transitions to `in_progress` with progress = "splitting" → "delegated" when chunks enqueued.

**Claim heartbeat**: `UPDATE jobs SET claim_expires_at = now + 30s WHERE id = ? AND claimed_by = ?` — succeeds only if we still hold it. Pod crash → no heartbeat → next lease expiry releases claim.

**Idempotent resume**: chunks record `{bytes_processed, docs_routed, last_cursor}`. A resumed chunk starts at `last_cursor` and re-writes docs (PK-idempotent at Meilisearch level → no dupes).

**Queue depth metric**: `miroir:jobs:_queued` set; `SCARD miroir:jobs:_queued` = `miroir_background_queue_depth`. Fed to HPA as external metric per plan §14.4.

**Config** tied to §13.9:
```yaml
dump_import:
  chunk_size_bytes: 268435456        # 256 MiB per §14.5 Mode C chunk-parallel coordinator
```

## Acceptance

- [x] 1 GB dump: first pod splits into 4× 256 MiB chunks; 3 pods claim 3 of 4 chunks in parallel; queue drains
- [x] Kill a claimant mid-chunk: claim expires in 30s; another pod picks up and resumes at `last_cursor`
- [x] HPA on `miroir_background_queue_depth > 10` triggers scale-up during the burst; scale-down once empty
- [x] Two concurrent dumps: chunks from both interleave in claims; neither starves
issue.title: P6.5 Mode C: work-queued chunked jobs (dump import, reshard backfill)

issue.description:
## What

Ship the HPA spec (plan §14.4):
```yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
spec:
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 24
  behavior:
    scaleDown: { stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300 }
    scaleUp:   { stabilizationWindowSeconds: 30 }
  metrics:
    - Resource cpu 70%
    - Resource memory 75%
    - Pods miroir_requests_in_flight AverageValue: 500
    - External miroir_background_queue_depth Value: 10
```

Chart preconditions enforced via `values.schema.json`:
- `hpa.enabled: true` requires `replicas >= 2 AND taskStore.backend: redis`
- `prometheus-adapter` (or equivalent) as a documented prerequisite when HPA is enabled

## Why

Plan §14.4: "`miroir_requests_in_flight` is **per-pod** and uses `type: Pods`. `miroir_background_queue_depth` is **global** and must use `type: External` with `type: Value`." Getting the metric type wrong produces a pathological HPA that monotonically scales to `maxReplicas`.

## Details

**Per-workload-tier min/max** (plan §14.7):
| Peak QPS | minReplicas | maxReplicas |
|---|---|---|
| ≤ 500 | 2 | 3 |
| ≤ 2k | 2 | 4 |
| ≤ 5k | 4 | 8 |
| ≤ 20k | 8 | 12 |
| ≤ 100k | 12 | 24 |

Default values.yaml ships the ≤ 5k tier; operators override per workload.

**prometheus-adapter config**: add a ConfigMap-defined `rules.externalMetrics` entry mapping `miroir_background_queue_depth` to the external metrics API. This is NOT shipped by the Miroir chart (operators install prometheus-adapter separately); the chart's `NOTES.txt` calls it out.

**Stabilization windows**: scale-up fast (30s), scale-down slow (300s). Avoids pod flapping.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `helm lint --strict` with `hpa.enabled: true + replicas: 1` → fails with schema error
- [ ] `helm lint --strict` with `hpa.enabled: true + replicas: 2 + backend: sqlite` → fails
- [ ] HPA in a kind cluster: induce CPU load → scales up within 30s; load drops → scales down after 300s
- [ ] External metric binding: `miroir_background_queue_depth` visible via `kubectl get --raw /apis/external.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1/...`
issue.title: P6.6 HPA spec + prometheus-adapter + schema validation

## What

Register the plan §14.9 resource-pressure metrics:
- `miroir_memory_pressure` gauge (0=ok, 1=warn >75%, 2=critical >90%)
- `miroir_cpu_throttled_seconds_total` counter (cgroup throttling)
- `miroir_request_queue_depth` gauge
- `miroir_background_queue_depth{job_type}` gauge
- `miroir_peer_pod_count` gauge
- `miroir_leader` gauge
- `miroir_owned_shards_count` gauge

And the associated `PrometheusRule` alerts (plan §14.9).

## Why

These surface under-scaling BEFORE user-visible impact. `miroir_memory_pressure` + `MiroirMemoryPressure` alert give operators (and HPA) a leading indicator instead of waiting for OOM-kill.

## Details

**cgroup reads**: on Linux, read `/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.stat` (cgroup v2) or `/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.stat` (v1) for `nr_throttled`/`throttled_time`. Convert throttled_time nanoseconds → seconds for the counter.

**Memory pressure gauge**: read `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.current` + `memory.max`; compute utilization; map to 0/1/2 per threshold.

**PrometheusRule**:
```yaml
- alert: MiroirMemoryPressure
  expr: miroir_memory_pressure >= 2
  for: 5m
- alert: MiroirRequestQueueBacklog
  expr: miroir_request_queue_depth > 500
  for: 2m
- alert: MiroirBackgroundJobBacklog
  expr: miroir_background_queue_depth > 100
  for: 10m
- alert: MiroirPeerDiscoveryGap
  expr: miroir_peer_pod_count < kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready{deployment="miroir"}
  for: 2m
- alert: MiroirNoLeader
  expr: sum(miroir_leader) == 0
  for: 1m
```

- [ ] `miroir_memory_pressure` reports 2 when artificial allocation pushes RSS > 90% of limit
- [ ] `MiroirNoLeader` fires after killing the leader without replacement within 1 min

issue.description:
## Phase 4 Epic — Topology Operations

Makes the cluster *elastic*: operators can add or remove nodes within a group (capacity scaling) or add/remove entire replica groups (throughput scaling) without a full reindex and without downtime.

## Why This Matters

Plan §2 "Topology changes" and §4 "Rebalancer" together are **the** operational differentiator. Without this phase, Miroir is a static sharder — useful but not production-grade. Elasticity is what justifies the complexity of the whole system.

Plan §15 Open Problem 1 (dual-write race) is partially mitigated by careful sequencing here and fully closed by §13.8 anti-entropy in Phase 5. Getting the sequencing right here means Phase 5's reconciler is a safety net, not the primary correctness mechanism.

## Scope

**Node addition (within a group; plan §2 "Adding a node")**

1. Assign new node to a group; mark `joining`
2. Recompute assignments — ~S/(Ng+1) shards move
3. Dual-write: new inbound writes for affected shards go to **both** old owner and new node
4. Background migration per shard: `GET /indexes/{uid}/documents?filter=_miroir_shard={id}&limit=1000&offset=...` → write each page to new node
5. Mark `active`; stop dual-write; `POST /indexes/{uid}/documents/delete` with `filter=_miroir_shard={id}` on old owner

**Replica-group addition (plan §2 "Adding a new replica group")** — mark `initializing`, background-sync from any healthy group using the same `_miroir_shard` filter, then flip to `active` and start routing queries.

**Node removal (plan §2 "Removing a node")** — mark `draining`, recompute, migrate ~RF/Ng fraction to survivors, mark `removed`, operator deletes PVC.

**Group removal (plan §2 "Removing a replica group")** — mark `draining`, stop routing queries; no data migration (other groups hold the docs); decommission.

**Unplanned node failure (plan §2 "Node failure")** — mark `failed`; surviving intra-group replicas cover if RF>1; cross-group fallback if RF=1; schedule background replication to restore RF.

**Admin API** (plan §4 admin table) — `POST /_miroir/nodes`, `DELETE /_miroir/nodes/{id}`, `POST /_miroir/nodes/{id}/drain`, `POST /_miroir/rebalance`, `GET /_miroir/rebalance/status`.

## Design Notes

- Relies on `_miroir_shard` being `filterable` on every node — set by Phase 2 index-create broadcast
- Only one rebalance at a time per index (advisory lock → Phase 6 Mode B leader lease)
- Chunked migration bounded by `rebalancer.max_concurrent_migrations` (default 4) to stay under the per-pod 3.75 GB envelope
- Migration progress reported via `GET /_miroir/rebalance/status` and `miroir_rebalance_*` metrics (§10)
- No full-corpus scans ever — the `_miroir_shard` filter is the key primitive; any code path that enumerates "all docs" is a bug

## Open Problem Closure

Plan §15 #1 — dual-write cutover race: document the exact sequencing here and note that §13.8 anti-entropy is the guaranteed safety net on the next pass.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Chaos test: add a node mid-indexing — every doc remains readable; no duplicates on a subsequent search
- [ ] Chaos test: drain a node while queries are in flight — zero client-visible failures; `X-Miroir-Degraded` absent or transient only
- [ ] Chaos test: add a replica group while queries are in flight — existing groups unaffected; new group starts serving reads only after sync completes
- [ ] Rebalance of a 3→4 node cluster moves ≤ 2×(1/4) of docs (optimal per plan §8 benches)
- [ ] Restart a killed node mid-rebalance — rebalance pauses + resumes; no data loss
issue.title: Phase 4 — Topology Operations (rebalance, add/remove node + group, drain)

issue.description:
## What

Implement the rebalancer as a background Tokio task (plan §4 "Rebalancer"):
- Advisory lock — only one Miroir instance runs the rebalancer at a time (Phase 6 §14.5 Mode B replaces with leader lease)
- Reacts to topology change events (node add/drain/fail/recover) from the admin API + health checker
- Computes affected shards (the `~S/(Ng+1)` or `~RF/Ng` delta) using the Phase 1 router
- Drives the migration state machine for each affected shard
- Updates `miroir_rebalance_in_progress`, `miroir_rebalance_documents_migrated_total`, `miroir_rebalance_duration_seconds` (plan §10)

## Why

The rebalancer is the orchestrator of all Phase 4 operations. Everything else in this phase is a subroutine called by this worker. Keeping it as a dedicated task — rather than inline in admin handlers — means a slow migration doesn't block admin API responses and a crash restarts cleanly from the task-store state.

## Details

**State machine per-shard**:
```
Idle → DualWriteStarted → MigrationInProgress → MigrationComplete → DualWriteStopped → OldReplicaDeleted → Idle
```

**Concurrency bound**: `rebalancer.max_concurrent_migrations` (default 4) to stay within plan §14.2 memory budget for migration buffers.

**Progress persistence**: per-shard cursor in `jobs` table (Phase 3) so a pod restart resumes at the last committed offset. Idempotent per primary key (same doc re-written on resume is no-op at Meilisearch level).

**Cancellation**: an admin API call can pause (not delete) an in-progress rebalance; resuming picks up at the persisted cursor.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Advisory lock: two pods running the rebalancer simultaneously produce 0 duplicate migrations (enforced via the `leader_lease` row for scope `rebalance:<index>`)
- [ ] Progress persistence: kill the pod mid-migration; another takes over within lease TTL and completes without starting over
- [ ] Metrics tick: `miroir_rebalance_documents_migrated_total` monotonically increases; `_duration_seconds` histogram records per-shard migration time
issue.title: P4.1 Rebalancer background worker + advisory lock

issue.description:
## What

Implement the node-addition flow from plan §2 "Adding a node to an existing group":
1. Admin API: `POST /_miroir/nodes` body `{"id": "meili-N", "address": "...", "replica_group": G}`
2. Mark `joining`
3. Recompute assignments — `affected_shards` where `meili-N` enters the top-RF within group G
4. **Dual-write**: new inbound writes for affected shards go to **both** old owner and new node (idempotent — Meilisearch PUT semantics handle dupes via primary key)
5. For each affected shard, background migration via the shard-filter primitive (plan §4):
   ```
   GET /indexes/{uid}/documents?filter=_miroir_shard={shard_id}&limit=1000&offset=0
   GET /indexes/{uid}/documents?filter=_miroir_shard={shard_id}&limit=1000&offset=1000
   ... until exhausted
   ```
6. Write each page to the new node (docs already carry `_miroir_shard`)
7. Mark `active`; stop dual-write
8. Delete migrated shard from old node: `POST /indexes/{uid}/documents/delete {"filter": "_miroir_shard = {shard_id}"}`
9. Documents on unaffected shards never touched

## Why

Plan §1 principle 4 (RF-configurable redundancy) + §2 "Three independent scaling dimensions" depend on this. The `_miroir_shard` filter primitive is what makes migration move only `~total_docs/(N+1)` docs instead of `total_docs` — a 10–100× reduction in I/O vs. a naive "copy everything then diff" approach.

## Details

**Dual-write durability invariant**: between steps 4 and 7, every accepted write for the affected shards lands on both old and new. If dual-write is skipped while migration is running, writes arriving at that exact moment may land only on the old owner and be lost when step 8 deletes. Plan §15 Open Problem 1 is the remaining race; §13.8 anti-entropy (Phase 5) is the safety net.

**Pagination cursor**: `offset` is the simplest, but Meilisearch `limit + offset` has an internal cap (default 1000 + 0 → max ~20 for safe). Configure `pagination.maxTotalHits` per-node at index creation to allow deep pagination (safe: we're just iterating our own injected shard).

**Per-page batch**: `rebalancer.migration_batch_size` (default 1000) — one page read + one page write per cycle.

**Fail-open behavior**: if the source node becomes unavailable mid-migration, the rebalancer pauses this shard; other shards continue. When source comes back, resume.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Integration test: 3-node → 4-node migration, 10K docs, each doc still retrievable by ID after migration
- [ ] Chaos: toggle writes on/off during migration; dual-write window catches all late writes
- [ ] Performance: migrating `~S/(Ng+1)` shards moves ≤ `total_docs / (Ng+1) × 1.1` docs (10% slack for dual-write dupes)
- [ ] The old node is not queried for the migrated shards after step 8 (verified via log inspection)
issue.title: P4.2 Node addition: dual-write + paginated shard migration

issue.description:
## What

Implement `POST /_miroir/nodes/{id}/drain` + `DELETE /_miroir/nodes/{id}` (plan §2 "Removing a node"):
1. Mark `draining`; stop routing writes for its affected shards to it
2. Recompute assignments — affected shards reassigned to surviving nodes in the same group
3. Background migration: copy affected shards to new owners via the `_miroir_shard` filter primitive
4. Mark `removed`
5. `DELETE /_miroir/nodes/{id}` actually removes from config; operator deletes pod + PVC out-of-band

## Why

Plan §2: "movement: ~RF/Ng of that group's documents" on removal. The drain API decouples "stop taking writes" (immediate) from "delete the pod" (operator decision) — gives operators room to verify before committing to hardware loss.

## Details

**Order matters**: drain → remove. `drain` is reversible (mark `active` again); `remove` is not. CLI (`miroir-ctl node drain meili-2` per plan §11) should pause and await confirmation before the remove step.

**Still readable during drain**: reads that previously routed to the draining node still work — the node is not down, just not accepting new writes for the affected shards. Read traffic naturally drifts to the replacement replica via Phase 1 `covering_set` intra-group rotation.

**Safety check**: refuse drain if it would drop a shard below RF=1 in its group AND the group has no healthy peer group to fall back to. Require `--force` to override.

**Post-drain verification**: query `GET /indexes/{uid}/documents?filter=_miroir_shard={s}&limit=1` against the drained node — should return 0 results for every shard before `remove` is permitted.

## Acceptance

- [ ] 3-node RF=2 group: drain node-1; searches still succeed with zero degraded responses

issue.description:
## What

Implement the "Adding a new replica group" flow from plan §2:
1. Provision new nodes; assign `replica_group: G_new` in config
2. Mark new group `initializing`; queries NOT routed here
3. Background sync: for each shard, copy all docs from **any** healthy existing group to the new group's nodes via `filter=_miroir_shard={id}` pagination; new inbound writes already fan out to the new group immediately
4. When all shards synced, mark group `active` — queries begin routing in round-robin
5. Existing groups continue serving queries throughout (zero read interruption)

## Why

Plan §2 "Adding a new replica group (throughput scaling)": adding a group multiplies query capacity without touching existing groups' data. This is the primary "we need more search QPS" lever. Unlike intra-group rebalance which moves a subset, group-add **copies** every shard to the new group — so the I/O is proportional to total corpus size, not `1/(Ng+1)`.

## Details

**Source group selection**: round-robin across existing `active` groups to spread read load during sync. Per-shard picks a different source so one group isn't hammered.

**Write fan-out during sync**: new group already receives writes from step 3 onward. This is the durability guarantee — only the backfill window of historical data is transient.

**Progress tracking**: per-shard cursor in `jobs` table; can be paused/resumed per Phase 6 Mode C.

**Verification before `active`**: `GET /indexes/{uid}/stats` against new group → docs count within 0.1% of source group (allows for writes landing during sync). If higher variance, delay the flip and investigate.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Integration test: RG=1 → RG=2; during sync, query throughput on original group unchanged (no regression)
- [ ] After `active`, queries distribute round-robin between the two groups (verified via per-group metrics)
- [ ] Mid-sync write test: 100 writes landing during the backfill window are all present on both groups when sync completes
- [ ] Failed sync (source group becomes unavailable mid-copy) pauses without corrupting new group; resumes when source returns

issue.description:
## What

Two related flows from plan §2:

**Removing a replica group** (decommission a query pool):
1. Mark group `draining` — queries stop routing immediately
2. Nodes can be decommissioned; no data migration needed (other groups hold the docs)
3. Remove nodes from config; operator deletes pods + PVCs

**Unplanned node failure**:
1. Health check detects failure → mark `failed`, stop routing writes to it
2. If RF > 1 within the group: surviving replicas serve reads — no immediate migration
3. For reads: if failed node's shards have no intra-group RF replica, fall back to a healthy group for those shards
4. Schedule background replication to restore RF within the group; degrade to cross-group fallback until restored

## Why

Plan §2: "Changes to one group do not affect other groups' data or query routing." Group-removal is instant (no data movement) — lets operators shed throughput capacity without a migration window. Unplanned node failure is the most time-sensitive case: readers must not see errors; RF-restore runs in the background.

## Details

**Group-removal preconditions**: refuse to remove a group if it's the last group holding a shard (would be data loss). Require `--force` and document the risk.

**Failure detection**: plan §4 config:
```yaml
health:
  interval_ms: 5000
  timeout_ms: 2000
  unhealthy_threshold: 3   # 3 consecutive failures → mark degraded
  recovery_threshold: 2    # 2 consecutive OKs → mark healthy again
```

**Cross-group fallback**: Phase 1 `covering_set` already deterministic per-request; the fallback is a per-shard "if intra-group has none, check other groups" decision **inside** the scatter planner (Phase 2).

**RF-restore**: similar to P4.2 node addition but for an existing node that lost its data — re-run `_miroir_shard` filter migration from the best intra-group source.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Remove a group with healthy peer groups → queries route away within one `query_seq` tick; no read errors
- [ ] `--force`-remove the last group holding shard S → loud warning; operator must re-type the index UID to confirm
- [ ] RF=2 group with 1 node killed → reads succeed on remaining replica; `X-Miroir-Degraded` absent
- [ ] RF=1 group with 1 node killed → cross-group fallback kicks in; `X-Miroir-Degraded` absent if fallback succeeds
- [ ] Restored node re-hydrates from a peer replica within its group; `miroir_rebalance_in_progress` transitions 0→1→0
issue.title: P4.5 Group removal + unplanned node failure
